## nbody-sandmark

Sandmark 5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507,
benchmarks/benchmarksgame/nbody.ml. The header credits Christophe Troestler.
Retain the directory Revised BSD notice and its original CRLF bytes, source,
build/run metadata and identities. The five-body constants are embedded program
data; no external astronomical dataset is acquired.

## Algorithm and known variants

Simulate the Sun and four outer planets by direct pairwise gravitational
updates, fixed timestep 0.01, and a separate position-update pass. Preserve
pair order, dx*otherMass*mag multiplication association, source pi literal,
solar_mass=4*pi*pi, forward mutable momentum sums including the initially
stationary Sun, and kinetic-before-potential energy accumulation.

The classic SML/NJ nbody uses immutable data. nofib's n-body uses a contiguous
seven-slot mutable body layout, different momentum/energy summation order and
position-update placement. Share neither implementation nor name merely because
the physical equations agree. This source's mutable records become SML records
with six real refs and an immutable mass. Record layout, boxing and aliasing
are explicit translation choices. No array-of-scalars replacement or change
to force accumulation is introduced.

## Profiles, observation and validation

Smoke 10 and normal 10,000 are reduced step counts; large preserves the selected
50,000,000-step upstream run. Reconstruct all bodies and offset momentum at
every invocation, including repeated calls. This resets the original mutable
globals and gives each run the same physical initial conditions. Selected
indices/counters fit 31 bits; all numerical work is binary64 on supported hosts.

The original prints two energies with nine fractional digits. The portable
driver checks full-precision initial/final energies and all 35 final body fields,
then reports steps:37:checked. No energy alone substitutes for the complete
state. Absolute/relative budgets are 1e-10/1e-10 for smoke/normal and 1e-5/1e-8
for large, allowing accumulated integration/math-library rounding on the
selected trajectories. They are not general orbit/energy conservation bounds.
Reference parsing and validation are measured work. No physical constants,
step count, timestep or stopping rule is changed.

Original two-line outputs agree with rounded observer energies at 0/10/10,000/
50,000,000 steps. An independent 60-digit integration from the exact zero-step
binary64 state validates all smoke/normal coordinates and velocities, energies
and momentum. At 10,000 steps, maximum state error is about 6.8e-12 and energy
error about 5.3e-16. Full large original state is retained; universal large SML
execution/high-precision large integration is not claimed.

Semantic checks include complete states, independent fresh records, momentum,
hand-computed two-body updates, kinetic/potential energy, one-body drift and
perturbed/missing/nonfinite state rejection. Mutable record allocation, ref
accesses, scalar arithmetic, loop specialization and energy order are diagnostic
hypotheses until investigated by compiler inspection or measurements.

## mandelbrot6

Sandmark 5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507,
benchmarks/benchmarksgame/mandelbrot6.ml. The header credits Paolo Ribeca and
its earlier OCaml 3 ancestry to Christophe Troestler, Christian Szegedy and
Yaron Minsky. Retain that header and the directory Revised BSD notice with
its original CRLF bytes. No external image/input dataset is acquired.

## Algorithm and variants

Render the source viewport with zr/zi/trmti scalar refs, at most 50 iterations
and strict squared escape test >4. Preserve zi-before-zr updates, cached previous
square difference, increment order and per-pixel Exit exception/handler.
A successful last iteration sets the bit; an escape clears it. Emit the exact
binary P4 header, MSB-first bytes and zero-padded final row byte.

The source carries one shifting int accumulator across all rows without reset.
Only its low eight bits reach output_byte. The port uses Word8 shifts/or with
modulo 256 truncation, preserving every observed byte while making machine-width
arithmetic portable. Do not replace it by a signed 31-bit accumulator that can
overflow. Keep the shared accumulator, odd-width padding and exception pattern.
Other classic/nofib Mandelbrot programs have different viewport/iteration/data
representations and remain separately named.

Smoke 17 explicitly exercises partial bytes; normal 256 is reduced comparative
work. Large preserves the selected 16,000-square source run. Inputs use the
same coordinate division and fixed 50-step limit, with no clock-dependent search.
All selected counters fit 31 bits; numerical operations use binary64.

A thin emit callback replaces output_byte. It reads and compares every expected
PBM byte through SML97 BinIO, then requires EOF. Streaming verification keeps
memory bounded rather than retaining the full image; expected-file I/O and
comparison are measured work. The source's diagnostic header and bit encoding
remain exact. The final result reports width:checked-bytes. There is no
floating error tolerance that accepts a different classification bitmap.

Original images at 1/7/8/9/16/17/64/256 and 16,000 have verified headers, sizes
and identities. An independent direct-complex iterator with separate row-bit
packing agrees on every byte through normal size. Full 32,000,015-byte large
source image is retained. Large SML execution is claimed only where explicitly
recorded. Numeric roundoff near escape boundaries is therefore observable.

perturbation (including padding), truncation and extra bytes. No SIMD batching,

## pidigits5

Sandmark 5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507,
benchmarks/benchmarksgame/pidigits5.ml. The header credits Christophe Troestler,

Generate pi by a three-component integer transformation (num,den,acc). Extract

coefficients. nofib's optimized pidigits uses different quotient/remainder
safety/refinement work. Keep these materially different representations and

independent AGM calculation or reuse another kernel merely because digits agree.

Smoke 27 preserves the no-argument source default. Normal 128 is a bounded
comparative input; large preserves the selected 10,000-digit source run.

for selected profiles fit 31 bits; coefficients have arbitrary precision.

Preserve ten-column blocks, row counts, tabs, final spaces/newlines and the
special zero-count output. A thin emit callback replaces print_int/Printf and
checks every generated character against reviewed complete output. It retains
streaming observation without materializing the digit sequence first. File
loading and checks are measured work; the final result reports count:checked.
Every invocation starts with the same initial transformation.

All original outputs at 0/1/10/11/27/128/256/1,000/10,000 agree exactly with an
independent high-precision Gauss-Legendre pi calculation and separately built
block layout. Source/independent fixtures and identities are retained.
Large execution of the SML port is claimed only where explicitly recorded.
Semantic/negative tests cover extraction, refinement, negative accumulators,
truncating division, block boundaries and perturbed/missing/extra output.

## References and diagnostic questions

Gibbons's [Unbounded Spigot Algorithms for the Digits of Pi](https://www.cs.ox.ac.uk/people/jeremy.gibbons/publications/spigot.pdf)
supplies algorithm-family context. The retained source defines this particular
three-state implementation and output adapter. Integer division, coefficient
growth, repeated additions, intermediate allocation, specialization, tuple
representation and bigint-library behavior are source-based hypotheses until
supported by inspection or measurements. Standard reports compare identical
SML; OCaml/Zarith and the independent AGM computation supply references.

[Complete provenance](pidigits5/PROVENANCE.md).

## evolutionary_algorithm

Sandmark 5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507,
benchmarks/multicore-numerical/evolutionary_algorithm.ml. The embedded description
credits Per Kristian Lehre, 6 May 2020. Despite the collection/title, this selected
file runs sequentially and uses no domain spawning. Retain the directory Revised
BSD notice with original CRLF bytes, source and build metadata. No dataset is
acquired; chromosomes are generated by the retained OCaml RNG.

## Algorithm and variants

Use boolean-array chromosomes, cached float fitness, binary tournament selection,
full Theta(n) copying mutation, and a fresh population each generation. Preserve
Onemax's sequential float sum, strict fitter comparison with second-individual
tie selection, two tournament samples and every mutation probability draw.
Mutation p=0.4/n still draws when it changes no bit; it always allocates a new
chromosome. Do not replace arrays by packed integers in the measured kernel.
The independent packed-bit oracle is a separate implementation.

The source checks time*population_size>runtime after constructing next_pop.
It therefore constructs floor(budget/lambda)+2 new generations, in addition to
the initial population. Preserve that strict post-generation test and its extra
work. Budget zero still evaluates three populations. These are deterministic
fitness-work parameters, not wall-clock stopping conditions.

OCaml records/arrays become SML records with boolean Arrays and real fitness.
For loops become portable tail loops; order, allocations, parent sharing and
whole-population replacement remain explicit. Selected fitness values are
integers represented exactly by binary64, so exact fitness comparison applies.
All selected counters fit 31 bits. No parallel/runtime feature is added.

## Reproducibility, profiles and checks

Replace Random.State.make_self_init by the documented seed 42 initialization.
This is an intentional adaptation required for reproducible inputs. Preserve
OCaml 4.14.1 generator/selection/float operations using the reviewed shared SML
RNG; retain its original source and LGPL/linking-exception notices. Every
invocation resets the RNG/population, including repeated in-process runs.

Smoke uses chromosome length 16, population 16, budget 128; normal 128/128/10,000.
Large preserves source defaults 1,000/1,000/100,000. Tournament size 2 and mutation
chi 0.4 remain unchanged. Fixed source/reference populations cover every profile.
Check all final chromosome bits, each stored fitness, independently recounted
Onemax fitness, dimensions and the best fitness. The original prints only the
best float; the suite reports length:population:budget:checked after complete
validation. Reference parsing and scans are measured work.

A bit-packed/integer-popcount implementation independently agrees on every tiny,
smoke and normal individual. It confirms 6/176/10,368 evaluations, including the
source budget overshoot. All original deterministic profiles, including large,
complete with full final-population fixtures. Large SML execution is claimed
only where explicitly recorded. Numeric or RNG host failures remain failures;
no source stream or expected population is adjusted to hide them.

Semantic checks cover tie behavior, mutation allocation/draw count, certain
mutation, tournament sampling, exact budget edges, complete populations and
perturbed/missing results. The seed 42 source patch, original code, input/RNG
identities and independent reference are retained.

## Recorded native32 limitation

Both profiles raise the already isolated bounded-random threshold Overflow on
managed 32-bit SML/NJ. Six selection-dependent semantic checks fail at both
levels; mutation and other nonselection cases pass. Other native hosts and
all Rune engines pass. Preserve the generator expression, fixed seed and
population fixtures; see [the existing arithmetic report](validation/smlnj32-random.md).
Failed configurations cannot contribute measurements.

## References and diagnostics

The [retained source](https://github.com/ocaml-bench/sandmark/blob/5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507/benchmarks/multicore-numerical/evolutionary_algorithm.ml) identifies the Onemax/tournament/mutation workload and its author. Its purpose is sequential evolutionary computation within a multicore
collection, with independently checked deterministic work. Array allocation,
selection recursion, RNG operations, higher-order fitness specialization,
boolean representation and population lifetimes are source-based performance
questions until supported by inspection or measurements. Standard comparisons
use identical SML; OCaml and independent packed-bit computation supply references.

[Complete provenance](evolutionary_algorithm/PROVENANCE.md).

## smallpt

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, real/smallpt/smallpt.hs,
Makefile and README.mkd. The README credits Davean Scies and bollu's Haskell
port and links the original smallpt-opt repository. Kevin Beason's
[smallpt](https://www.kevinbeason.com/smallpt/) supplies renderer ancestry.
The selected Haskell files state no separate program redistribution notice;
retain the files/history without inferring a grant from another version.
The scene constants are embedded program data, not an acquired image dataset.

## Algorithm and variants

Trace the nine-sphere Cornell-style scene with diffuse, specular and glass
materials. Preserve intersection order/ties, epsilon 1e-4, cosine-weighted diffuse
sampling, Schlick-style reflection weights, branch/split order, path roulette,
2x2 subpixels, tent-filter jitter, per-subpixel averaging/clamping and descending
image rows. The selected Haskell refractive split tests the incoming depth;
do not substitute an ancestor's incremented-depth convention. Keep the black
front wall and RNG draws even when color contributions later vanish.

Vectors/rays/spheres have strict numerical fields in the source. SML uses strict
real tuples and constructors, preserving scalar operation association. The
selected hash observation consumes every RGB channel. Keep row-sized lists and
force each row's sequential state actions before consumption, avoiding a full
image array or an additional cached-result variant. Tuple/header layout and
GHC's UNPACK annotations have no portable SML memory-layout equivalent and are
recorded representation differences.

The full modulo 2^64 state recurrence is retained. Source bitcast construction
of 1+out/2^48 followed by subtraction becomes exact dyadic conversion of the
masked 48 bits, split into two 24-bit pieces that fit every host's Int. Both
terms and their sum are exactly representable in binary64. Retain row seed
y^3 shifted 32 and all state updates; no alternate RNG or sampling distribution
replaces it. A state fixture independently verifies all 50 selected full 64-bit
states and exact draw values.

## Profiles, references and output checks

Smoke 16x12x1 and normal 64x48x1 reduce image dimensions through the upstream
smallpt API. Large preserves 512x384x6, the selected slow profile. Upstream CLI
FAST/NORM both use 512x384x1; that full reference is also retained. All dimensions,
seeds, scene values and sample counts are fixed. Each invocation reconstructs
row RNG state; repeated execution does not reuse rendered pixels.

The source hash prints six decimal places without a final newline. Pinned
nofib fixtures add one terminal LF. Reference checks record that formatting
adaptation and agree on both one/six-sample values. An export-only observer
retains complete RGB values and full-precision channel sums at every profile
and the full upstream normal input.

The driver streams every RGB reference line, checking each channel within
1e-8+1e-8*abs(reference) and the sequential channel sum within
1e-6+1e-10*abs(reference). Require exact pixel count and EOF. These budgets
cover selected deterministic results/math rounding, not arbitrary Monte Carlo
scenes. Gamma conversion/PPM image mode are outside the chosen hash workload.
Reference I/O and per-channel checks are measured work; the final report is
width:height:samples:checked. Large SML execution is claimed only where recorded.

GHC 9.4.7 lacks unboxed-ref in this environment. A correctness-only adapter
implements its used API with boxed STRef and strict initialization/writes.
This preserves state semantics while changing representation; its executions
are not original-runtime performance measurements. Both pinned hashes and
complete strict-adapter scene outputs agree. Retain adapter/source identities,
its explicit limitation, and the initial fixture-newline comparison attempt.

Semantic/negative tests cover vector algebra, normalized directions, near/far/
miss intersections, epsilon, full RNG states, complete smoke RGB, zero-sample
behavior, bad pixels/sums, truncation and extra reference data.

## Recorded native32 findings

Both selected profiles produce different pixels on managed 32-bit SML/NJ.
The full-state/value RNG check also fails, while the other geometry and negative
checks pass. Other supported native hosts and all Rune engines pass. Preserve
the Word64 expressions and reviewed references; the existing
[Word64 host reports](../../docs/bugreport/smlnj/README.md) describe related
constant/arithmetic defects. This workload's exact first failing operation is
not reduced, so a specific cause is not asserted from the image difference.
Failed pixels cannot contribute accepted measurements.

## References and diagnostic questions

The [original smallpt explanation](https://www.kevinbeason.com/smallpt/) describes
Monte Carlo illumination, diffuse sampling, roulette and sphere scenes. The
retained Haskell program defines this workload's exact ordering, PRNG and hash
mode. Recursion, strict tuple boxing, scalar/library math, branch behavior,
state refs, row retention and allocation are source-based performance questions
until supported by inspection or measurement. Standard reports compare identical
SML. Original C++ OpenMP behavior is outside this sequential Haskell port.

## revcomp2

## Algorithm and workload

Reverse each FASTA record's sequence, complement uppercase and lowercase ASCII
through a 256-byte lookup table, and emit at most 60 sequence bytes per line.
The source retains a reversed list of input lines, walks each line backwards,
and writes through a 61-byte mutable buffer whose first byte is a newline.
The port keeps that algorithm, buffer index convention and retained record.

## History, authorship and aliases

Sandmark 5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507,
benchmarks/benchmarksgame/revcomp2.ml credits Ingo Bormuth and the Computer
Language Benchmarks Game. Preserve the complete source, directory Revised BSD
notice, aggregate Unlicense, Dune build and directory README. The established
revcomp2 name identifies this implementation; other reverse-complement algorithms
are not silently substituted. No upstream timing claim is transferred.

## Known variants and exact source behavior

This variant stores strings in a list and uses a small byte buffer rather than
reversing a whole contiguous record in place. Preserve its handling of header-only
records (no added newline), consecutive headers (concatenated), a sequence without
a header (leading newline), blank lines (record flush), terminal lines without LF,
60/61-byte boundaries, ambiguous IUPAC codes and unknown bytes (space).
OCaml input_line removes only LF: CR remains in headers and maps to space in
sequence data. These source behaviors are recorded rather than normalized to a
different FASTA reader's conventions.

## Portable translation and adaptations

SML97 TextIO.inputLine replaces OCaml input_line, explicitly removing its terminal
LF. String lists, Word8Array lookup/buffer storage and descending indexed loops
preserve traversal and output order. An output callback replaces stdout; the
streaming BinIO reference checker consumes every emitted byte and verifies EOF.
Its I/O and validation are measured work. The source's catch-all read termination
is retained, and the input is closed at the end or after a callback exception.
All mutable buffers and indices are reconstructed on each invocation.

The source hardcodes input25000000.txt. The suite accepts an explicit controlled
input path and reference path. Reference runs keep the original fixed filename
in fresh working directories; no source algorithm edit is required. Output is
reported as a validated byte count only after full equality, not a hash-only test.

## Compiler/runtime questions

Record retention, list nodes, generic byte-array representation, input strings,
buffer accesses, tail calls and callback/checker overhead are source-based
performance questions until established by compiler inspection or measurement.
SML comparisons use identical sources. OCaml supplies correctness references.
The workload is sequential and needs no FFI, parallelism or runtime extensions.

## Inputs, validation and references

Fixed smoke/normal/large inputs are generated by the same pinned Sandmark fasta3
with parameters 1,000 / 50,000 / 500,000, seed 42, width 60 and sequence lengths
2n/3n/5n. The ALU sequence and distributions are embedded source literals;
there is no separately acquired dataset. Retain the generator's original author
credits, notice, source identity and every generated input/output identity.
Large is an explicitly reduced scaling profile. Dune's 25,000,000 default and
5,000,000 auxiliary input remain documented; neither full generator input is
claimed as an executed revcomp2 profile in this import.

Original OCaml outputs agree byte for byte with an independent implementation
that joins each generated record, reverses/complements it and wraps at 60.
Eleven original edge fixtures specify the unusual source formatting. Semantic
checks consume these fixtures and the complete smoke output; deliberately
corrupted, truncated and extra references must fail. Large SML execution is
claimed only when separately recorded. The retained source/header and suite
measurement survey provide history and methodology; FASTA itself does not define
this implementation's exceptional-input behavior.

[Complete provenance](revcomp2/PROVENANCE.md).

## knucleotide

## Algorithm and workload

Extract the FASTA sequence whose header begins with >THREE, uppercase it, and
count overlapping nucleotide substrings. For each length, clear a chained hash
table, reuse a mutable lookup key, copy the key only on insertion, and increment
a reference on a hit. Emit sorted one-/two-base frequencies and counts for the
five source queries of lengths 3, 4, 6, 12 and 18. Preserve the inclusive final
window and the original descending-frequency/ascending-key ordering.

## History, authorship and aliases

Sandmark 5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507,
benchmarks/benchmarksgame/knucleotide.ml credits Troestler Christophe and Mauricio
Fernandez, with Computer Language Benchmarks Game ancestry. Preserve that file,
Dune, directory README, Revised BSD notice and aggregate Unlicense. OCaml 4.14.1
library sources are separately pinned at 99cb5d93fc30f1a6f3e69f5aa5d2063994d33a93;
the installed hashtbl.ml and buffer.ml match those exact source bytes. Their
Xavier Leroy/INRIA copyrights, LGPL 2.1 notice and linking exception are retained.
The replacement buffer/table support follows those algorithms; the corresponding
notice also appears in the SML source.

## Differences between known variants

The separately inventoried knucleotide3 packs nucleotide values into integers,
uses width-dependent key thresholds and retains its tables across query lengths.
Its loop also omits the last window. These are material differences; do not
replace the present byte-key/clear-per-length implementation or its expected
frequencies with that version. Original full outputs and independent replays of
both variants document the differences. knucleotide3 is not claimed imported here.

## Portable translation and adaptations

SML97 CharArray keys replace OCaml Bytes; integer references retain mutable counts.
A self-contained chained table starts with 262144 buckets, uses the source
polynomial hash h*5+byte, inserts at the head, and doubles above two entries per
bucket. Rehashing preserves chain order with mutable links and tail arrays.
Word64 retains the source's 63-bit hash arithmetic without host-Int-width
assumptions; bucket indices/counts fit every selected SML host's Int. SML's
record/reference and generic array layouts may add indirections or initialization.
Lookup returns an SML option instead of raising OCaml Not_found on a miss.
Counts still perform exactly one lookup and copy only newly inserted keys;
option construction/branching replaces the source exception boundary and is an
explicit library-call cost difference, rather than a measured optimization claim.

The input buffer starts at 1000, doubles as required, retains its existing bytes,
and makes the final sequence copy. ASCII uppercasing and terminal-LF removal
preserve source input semantics. The first-data-line catch-all and comment skip
remain, as do rejection of an empty subsequent line and missing THREE header.
Closing the file on return/error supports repeated invocation. All mutable
sequence/table state moves from process initialization into Benchmark.run,
restoring fresh-process semantics on every repetition and avoiding file I/O
while native hosts export their entry points.

SML97 has no standard sort, so portable merge sort replaces List.sort. The exact
comparison, binary64 operation association and fixed three-decimal formatting
remain; sort implementation/allocation is an explicit library adaptation.
A callback replaces stdout and the BinIO checker consumes every output byte plus
EOF before returning its byte count. Input loading, table allocation, formatting
and reference I/O/checking are measured work. No precomputed frequency replaces
execution of any count pass.

## Compiler/runtime behavior to investigate

Byte-key copying, collision chains, mutable counters, clearing cost, table growth,
string/buffer retention, boxing, Word64 arithmetic and sorting/formatting are
source-based performance questions until supported by inspection or measurement.
Standard reports compare identical SML; OCaml supplies correctness references.
No parallelism, effect handlers or FFI are required.

## Inputs, checks and references

Smoke/normal/large reuse pinned fasta3 inputs with n=1000/50000/500000, seed 42,
width 60 and the embedded ALU/probability tables. THREE contains 5000/250000/2500000
bases. Source Dune uses n=25000000 and also generates n=5000000; those complete
revcomp/nucleotide defaults are not claimed executed here. Large is an explicit
reduced scaling input. No separately acquired dataset or dataset notice is added.

Complete original outputs agree with an independent dictionary-based substring
counter for every selected input, including the large reference. Original edge
fixtures cover case conversion, prefix header matching, initial comments, record
termination, short input, absent terminal LF, initial empty lines and unusual
characters. Tests also cover rejected malformed inputs, deliberately wrong/
truncated/extra references, per-length clearing, and 256 independent four-mer
counts through forced collisions and multiple table resizes. Large SML execution
is claimed only where separately recorded. The retained source headers and suite
measurement survey provide the history/methodology; no historical timing claim
is transferred to this translation.

[Complete provenance](knucleotide/PROVENANCE.md).

## integer-lazy

## Algorithm and workload

nofib's integer workload traverses a Cartesian grid separately for machine Int
and arbitrary-precision Integer. It repeats this pair of passes for addition,
subtraction, multiplication, floor division/modulus, truncating quotient/remainder,
gcd, lcm and all five comparisons. Preserve operation order, ascending outer and
inner enumerations and forcing every result. Source seqlist observes WHNF but
prints nothing. The suite additionally consumes each value into a checked digest;
that validation cost is measured work.

## History, authorship, revision and aliases

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, spectral/integer/Main.hs and
Makefile. The individual files state no author or separate redistribution notice;
preserve their exact bytes/history without inventing attribution or a grant.
The established integer name is qualified as integer-lazy and integer-strict for
the two evaluation variants. This is arithmetic enumeration rather than the
separately imported pi or primality workloads.

## Variant differences and numeric semantics

The lazy variant uses explicitly memoized list spines and heads. Each arithmetic
result is forced by the consumer before advancing. Enumeration arithmetic remains
inside the delayed tail, and repeated demand shares that tail. The strict variant
uses the same finite sequence operations with eager suspensions, constructing the
current operation's result list before consuming it. Their values and digests
must agree; their retention and allocation can differ materially.

Original GHC 9.4.7 uses 64-bit signed Int. Word64-based helpers retain that machine
arithmetic on SML hosts whose default Int may be 31 bits. Addition/subtraction/
multiplication wrap modulo 2^64. Signed ordering, magnitudes, sign-adjusted quotient
and floor-division rules are explicit. Zero divisors raise Div; signed minimum
quotient -1 raises Overflow. Gcd/lcm use magnitude/remainder iteration. IntInf
separately implements arbitrary-precision operations, including distinct div/mod
and quot/rem. Every selected grid operand is bounded by 2100000000, and products
and lcm fit signed 64 bits. The machine/extreme-value tests supplement these
selected grids; arbitrary-precision computation is not replaced by Word64.

## Translation and result consumption

The portable SML97 functor uses the shared suspension and cell-sequence support.
The source's machine primitives become explicit Word64 operations and sign rules;
this changes primitive/library implementation costs, which must not be presented
as original Haskell runtime performance. The IntInf gcd/lcm helpers are separate.
Per-run enumeration/result state is recreated; no output is cached across calls.

The source receives one start/step/limit triplet and uses it for both axes and
both numeric representations. Some internal formal b parameters are ignored or
refer back to astart; the public driver preserves the selected CLI behavior,
rather than inventing a different rectangular-grid benchmark. Negative argument
spelling becomes canonical SML ~ for the checked portable driver. The
driver accepts positive strides, operands within +/-2100000000 and at most
2100 values per axis, making the fixed profile domain and resource guard
explicit; it does not claim the original CLI's zero/negative-stride behaviors.

After each pass, consume every value into h=h*1664525+value modulo 2^64 from
1013904223. Booleans become 0/1; integer values convert modulo 2^64 only after
performing their original operation. Compare all 28 exact pair-count/digest
lines and EOF with a reviewed fixture. This prevents an unused-result benchmark
while adding hashing/reference I/O costs to all SML hosts consistently.

## Compiler/runtime questions

Calls through arithmetic functions, explicit delays, tail consumption, eager
retention, machine-word boxing, IntInf representation and division/gcd allocation
are source-based performance questions until backed by compiler inspection or
measurement. Treat digest cost separately when interpreting the workload.
Standard reports compare identical SML; GHC supplies correctness references.
No FFI, compiler feature or runtime extension is required.

## Inputs, independent references and checks

All profiles keep range -2100000000 through 2100000000. Smoke step700000001
has six operands per axis. Normal step14000001 preserves the upstream FAST
300-operand grid for a bounded comparative run. Large step2000001 preserves the
upstream SLOW 2100-operand grid. The original NORM step4500001/934-operand grid
is also retained as a correctness reference and calibration point, rather than
being silently relabeled as the selected normal profile. No dataset is required.

Unmodified GHC originals terminate successfully with empty output on all three
upstream/reduced reference inputs. A reference-only observer adds Show constraints
and a strict digest consumer while retaining original operation selection and
machine/Integer passes. Complete digests agree with an independent exact Python
model for all selected grids and upstream NORM. Observing values changes reference
costs; these are not original-runtime timing results.

A separate GHC/native64 observer and independent model agree on 98 arithmetic
results covering sign combinations, negative division and values beyond signed
31 bits. Tests additionally check machine wrap, exceptional division, gcd/lcm zero,
complete lazy/strict smoke, exact agreement, memoized tail demand, eager strict
enumeration, and wrong count/digest/truncated/extra references. Large SML execution
is claimed only where recorded. See the suite's nofib and measurement literature
for context; no historical speed claim is transferred.


## Recorded native32 diagnostic findings

Managed 32-bit SML/NJ fails two of 114 semantic checks at both levels: constant
signed64 subtraction/multiplication wrap. The other 112 pass there; all 114
pass every other configuration. A separate runtime-input probe passes both
wrap checks on all ten configurations. Native32 prints constant subtraction
7FFFFFFF3FFFFFFF versus runtime 7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF, and constant multiplication
FFFFFFFF3FFFFFFE versus runtime FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFE. These constant-path findings
are consistent with the existing [Word64 low-half reports](../../docs/bugreport/smlnj/README.md).
Keep the original expressions and reviewed expected values; no arithmetic
workaround or altered reference is introduced. Full selected-profile outcomes
are recorded separately from these diagnostic failures.

[Complete provenance](integer-lazy/PROVENANCE.md).

## secretary-lazy

## Algorithm and workload

Simulate the secretary selection rule on a random ordering of 100 distinct
values. Generate random Integer values in 1..100, remove repeats with linear
list membership, and take the first 100 distinct values. Inspect the first k
values to obtain their maximum; select the first later value at least that
large, and succeed only when it is 100. Evaluate k=35..39 using seeds 1..n,
filter successful trials, count them and divide by n in binary64.

performance evidence. Individual workload headers state no separate license;
retain them without inferring a grant from the RNG dependency.

Pin System.Random 1.1 at cfdfe6f09ad414fde5b855cc5f90207533413241. Its complete
Random.hs, package metadata and LICENSE retain University of Glasgow credits,
BSD-style terms and the accompanying Haskell98 Report notice. The unmodified
workload and exact library source compile with GHC 9.4.7 and reproduce the pinned
stdout exactly. No replacement RNG, OS seed or unrecorded package version is
used. Name the meaningful evaluation variants secretary-lazy and secretary-strict.

## Variant differences, demand and sharing

The lazy variant keeps explicit memoized raw random-stream heads/spines, nub's
reversed seen list and the finite take100 spine. The same finite sequence is
shared by the prefix maximum and later search. Stop at the first qualifying
candidate, or after all 100 distinct values when the prefix already contains
100. Taking one candidate must not demand its tail or seek a 101st distinct
value in an exhausted 100-value domain.

The strict variant materializes all 100 distinct values before applying the
same rule. A bounded producer combines the infinite raw stream/nub/take boundary,
so strict evaluation terminates while preserving repeated-draw rejection and
linear seen-list membership. This is an explicit evaluation/allocation
adaptation: it consumes the complete coupon-collection prefix, while lazy trials
may stop earlier. The source's finite trial map/filter/length remains explicit
in both styles. Their success counts/probabilities agree; their draw counts,
retention and allocation can differ.

## Portable translation and arithmetic

SML97 Word32 retains StdGen's two strict Int32 state fields. Schrage quotient/
remainder decomposition keeps each mathematical intermediate within signed32;
Word32 sign-bit checks implement its negative corrections without relying on
default Int width. Convert the positive output to IntInf for the source Random
Integer range accumulator, base expansion, q=1000 target magnitude and modulus.
Seed masking and every state/draw transition remain explicit. All selected seeds
fit even a 31-bit host Int. No Float or alternative bounded-integer sampler replaces
this library's algorithm.

Each call recreates seeds/trial state. Mutable references occur in memoized
delays and test-only draw observers, rather than a shared global RNG. The source's
unneeded global RNG, time/FFI initialization, splitting and unrelated Random
instances are not ported; the complete original library remains available as
reference/provenance. Word32 boxing, arbitrary-precision range calculations and
portable stream/list construction have different layout/library costs from GHC.
These are documented translation costs, not original-runtime comparisons.

## Inputs, result checks and diagnostic questions

The population remains 100 and k remains 35..39. Smoke uses 50 trials, normal
uses 500, and selected large preserves the original 5000 through the simulate API.
A 50000-trial reference is retained separately. The bounded normal selection
follows resource calibration; a final-state lazy 5000 preflight takes about
305 seconds under the recorded load and is not a headline timing comparison.
Seeds are exactly 1..n for each k, without cross-k caching. No dataset is needed.
Validate all five exact success counts and the original binary64 ratios against
reviewed count/probability fixtures, then require EOF. The absolute probability
budget is 1e-15: selected integer conversions are exact, with one binary64
division and decimal-reference parsing; it is not a Monte Carlo confidence
interval. Wrong counts/probabilities, nonfinite values, truncation and extra
reference data must fail. Checking/reference I/O is measured work. The suite prints n:checked after
validating every count/probability, replacing the original probability-list
output. The driver exposes the simulate trial-count parameter with a positive
1..50000 bound; it does not add a universal size argument to unrelated kernels.

Source inspection suggests questions about membership scans, repeated random
draws, memoized prefix sharing, early stopping, boxed words/integers and retained
lists. These remain hypotheses until supported by compiler analysis or
measurements. Standard reports compare identical SML; Haskell supplies correctness
references. No compiler/runtime feature is introduced.

## Independent references and literature

The original default prints [0.356,0.356,0.358,0.3596,0.3594]. A count-only observer
retains the original processing expression and exposes its numerator at fixed
trial counts. An independent model uses multiplicative modular recurrences,
set-based full permutations and direct threshold evaluation. All five counts
agree through 50000. Separate original observers agree with every selected RNG
state, full permutation and minimum lazy/complete strict draw count. Wide Integer
ranges through signed 10^50 also agree with independent base expansion.

Tests cover 60 full RNG transitions, five general ranges, six complete permutations
in both variants, 30 lazy demand/sharing and strict consumption cases, complete
smoke results and numerical/negative checks. Large SML execution is claimed only
when recorded. Earlier IntInf-state resource calibration is intermediate work;
the final helper retains the source's fixed-width state representation.

[Ferguson, Who Solved the Secretary Problem?](https://doi.org/10.1214/ss/1177012493)
provides mathematical and historical context. System.Random credits L'Ecuyer's
[Efficient and Portable Combined Random Number Generators](https://doi.org/10.1145/62959.62969)
and Lennart Augustsson's transliteration. The pinned source determines this
workload's exact seeding/range rules; those papers do not establish its SML
performance or validate a changed RNG stream.

[Complete provenance](secretary-lazy/PROVENANCE.md).

## secretary-strict

## mandel-lazy

Selected: current Mandel.lhs with memoized cyclic orbits, coordinates and pixel streams.

## Algorithm and workload

Construct a pixmap by mapping a complex orbit escape count across a rectangular
viewport. Each orbit begins at c and applies z*z+c. Pixels enumerate Integer
coordinates s=1..width and t=1..height, mapping both axes with multiply before
divide. RGB is (count, limit-count, limit-count), sharing the latter value.
The pixmap retains Integer dimensions, Int depth and a list/stream of RGB tuples.
Force and consume every metadata field and colour; do not substitute a bitmap,
zero-based sampling grid or a different Mandelbrot recurrence convention.

## History, authorship, revision and names

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, spectral/mandel/Main.hs,
Mandel.lhs, MandelOld.lhs, PortablePixmap.lhs and Makefile. The literate modules
retain a report-style explanation and a Falconer citation. The format banner
credits Jon.Hill, 28/5/92; the embedded PPM manual retains Jef Poskanzer's
1989/1991 copyright. The individual workload modules state no separate grant;
preserve their bytes and notices without inferring one from another component.

GHC base's Data/Complex.hs and complete BASE LICENSE are separately pinned at
GHC 9.4.7 revision 00920f176b0235d5bb52a8e054d89a664f8938fe. Retain its
University of Glasgow and Haskell98 Report notices. Its multiplication and
scaled magnitude define the selected generic variant's library operations.
The source stem mandel is distinct from classic SML mandelbrot, nofib mandel2
and Sandmark mandelbrot6. Explicit -lazy/-strict names record evaluation choices;
mandel-old identifies the materially different historical module.

## Known variants and exact numeric differences

The current Mandel.lhs uses generic complex multiplication/addition and scaled
magnitude. Its magnitude scales components by the maximum exponent, squares,
sums, takes a square root and scales back. Divergence tests magnitude>radius,
where radius=max(viewport spans)/2. Take limit orbit elements, then count the
prefix before the first divergent element. A bounded orbit returns limit,
not zero. At limit0, neither the initial complex coordinate nor the next orbit
value is demanded by this consumer.

MandelOld.lhs explicitly squares complex components, using 2*(r*i) for the
imaginary product. It compares x*x+y*y>=max(viewport spans) directly; that
quantity is the source's radiusSq, not a replacement derived formula. The
predicate precedes the zero-limit test, forcing the current orbit head even
at limit0 and one additional head at an exhausted positive limit. Inclusive
boundary behavior differs from the current module. Preserve these algorithms,
operation associations and data flows separately.

The pinned Makefile excludes MandelOld.lhs from its default SRCS. Preserve it
as a historical variant rather than silently dropping it. The reference needs
two syntax-only adaptations for modern GHC: remove [sequential] from a literate
code delimiter and parenthesize both operands of :+ against +. Original bytes,
patches, failed compile attempts and adapted source remain recorded. No numeric
formula is repaired or replaced by a dense rendering shortcut.

## Portable SML translation and evaluation

Specialize the selected complex operations to real pairs with explicit component
types; preserve the separate generic multiply/add results and the historical
scalar expressions. The runtime requires binary64 Real. Integer grid indices
and pixmap dimensions remain IntInf. Bounded colour counts use the supported
hosts' default Int. All selected counts/dimensions fit even 31-bit Int.

Lazy variants retain explicit memoized orbit heads/spines and the feedback
list knot. The current module also retains a lazy take spine. Coordinates are
passed as delays so limit0 does not evaluate them. Historical zero-limit and
boundary behavior are tested separately. Strict variants materialize finite
orbits, with limit elements for the current module and limit+1 for the old
consumer; a final-element case avoids an unintended additional step. They may
compute unused post-escape IEEE infinities/NaNs before the consumer stops;
those values are not reported as pixel results. Strict grid/pixel lists replace
the lazy spines explicitly. Final integer RGB values must agree with the
corresponding original variant.

A polymorphic Pixmap wrapper retains metadata and either the stream or strict
list. Full-image reference checks remain available, while the timed driver
consumes every RGB channel into a checked 64-bit rolling digest and exact pixel
count, then checks metadata and EOF. It reports repetitions:checked instead
of the original empty stdout. The digest starts at 1013904223 and folds each
r/g/b in order with h=h*1664525+value modulo 2^64. Hashing/checking costs are
measured work; they are not original Haskell runtime timings.

## Profiles, repeated work and compiler/runtime questions

Smoke is 1 repetition of 7x5; normal preserves upstream FAST 25x25 for the
source's 100 repetitions; large preserves SLOW 180x180 for 100. All use the
original -2..2 viewport and depth75. Upstream NORM 80x80 remains a complete
reference. Deterministic SML97 generation writes each repetition's seven
parameters. The driver reads a fresh row each time, retaining the original
Main's repeated getArgs dependency and preventing the entire render from
becoming a loop-invariant value. It consolidates argument reading/parsing
into one file row and uses SML negative spelling. File I/O and parsing are
explicit driver adaptations. A parameter file starts with the repetition count,
then exactly that many minX/minY/maxX/maxY/width/height/limit rows. The reviewed
digest line contains width, height, depth, pixel count and uppercase hex hash. Width/height are limited to 1..180, depth to
0..75, repetitions to 1..100, and finite viewports to the documented +/-2 box.
No separately acquired dataset is needed.

Source-based questions include complex boxing/unboxing, generic specialization,
scaled-norm cost, lazy knot/take allocation, sharing, early escape, eager unused
orbits, strict list retention and Integer-index conversion. These are hypotheses
until established by compiler inspection or measurement. Ordinary comparisons
use identical SML. No parallelism or runtime facility is required merely because
the literate explanation discusses parallel mapping.

## References and validation

Complete original GHC RGB components and independent binary64 recurrence/scaled-
norm models agree through 180x180, including rectangular and zero/one-limit
cases. Separate original Word64 observers agree with independently derived
full-image digests. Checks cover all channels/metadata, exact count/digest/EOF,
boundary differences, zero-limit demand, extra historical orbit forcing,
cyclic sharing and strict evaluation after escape. Wrong RGB, metadata, counts,
digests, empty/truncated/extra references must fail. Final results are discrete
integer colours and require exact agreement; no generic floating tolerance
is applied to a changed escape decision. A mismatch alone is not a language-
conformance proof. Large SML execution is claimed only when recorded.

The retained modules explain their own implementation choices. Falconer's
[Fractal Geometry](https://doi.org/10.1002/0470013850) provides broader mathematical
background (the linked later edition is not claimed as the source's historical
edition). The nofib literature and suite measurement survey provide benchmark
context; they do not establish performance causes for this translation.

[Complete provenance](mandel-lazy/PROVENANCE.md).

## mandel-old-strict

Selected: historical MandelOld.lhs with eager finite orbits and pixel lists.

## Algorithm and workload

Construct a pixmap by mapping a complex orbit escape count across a rectangular
viewport. Each orbit begins at c and applies z*z+c. Pixels enumerate Integer
coordinates s=1..width and t=1..height, mapping both axes with multiply before
divide. RGB is (count, limit-count, limit-count), sharing the latter value.
The pixmap retains Integer dimensions, Int depth and a list/stream of RGB tuples.
Force and consume every metadata field and colour; do not substitute a bitmap,
zero-based sampling grid or a different Mandelbrot recurrence convention.

## History, authorship, revision and names

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, spectral/mandel/Main.hs,
Mandel.lhs, MandelOld.lhs, PortablePixmap.lhs and Makefile. The literate modules
retain a report-style explanation and a Falconer citation. The format banner
credits Jon.Hill, 28/5/92; the embedded PPM manual retains Jef Poskanzer's
1989/1991 copyright. The individual workload modules state no separate grant;
preserve their bytes and notices without inferring one from another component.

GHC 9.4.7 revision 00920f176b0235d5bb52a8e054d89a664f8938fe. Retain its
University of Glasgow and Haskell98 Report notices. Its multiplication and
scaled magnitude define the selected generic variant's library operations.

## Known variants and exact numeric differences

The current Mandel.lhs uses generic complex multiplication/addition and scaled
magnitude. Its magnitude scales components by the maximum exponent, squares,
sums, takes a square root and scales back. Divergence tests magnitude>radius,
where radius=max(viewport spans)/2. Take limit orbit elements, then count the
prefix before the first divergent element. A bounded orbit returns limit,
not zero. At limit0, neither the initial complex coordinate nor the next orbit
value is demanded by this consumer.

MandelOld.lhs explicitly squares complex components, using 2*(r*i) for the
imaginary product. It compares x*x+y*y>=max(viewport spans) directly; that
quantity is the source's radiusSq, not a replacement derived formula. The
predicate precedes the zero-limit test, forcing the current orbit head even
at limit0 and one additional head at an exhausted positive limit. Inclusive
boundary behavior differs from the current module. Preserve these algorithms,
operation associations and data flows separately.

The pinned Makefile excludes MandelOld.lhs from its default SRCS. Preserve it
as a historical variant rather than silently dropping it. The reference needs
two syntax-only adaptations for modern GHC: remove [sequential] from a literate
code delimiter and parenthesize both operands of :+ against +. Original bytes,
patches, failed compile attempts and adapted source remain recorded. No numeric
formula is repaired or replaced by a dense rendering shortcut.

## Portable SML translation and evaluation

Specialize the selected complex operations to real pairs with explicit component
types; preserve the separate generic multiply/add results and the historical
scalar expressions. The runtime requires binary64 Real. Integer grid indices
and pixmap dimensions remain IntInf. Bounded colour counts use the supported
hosts' default Int. All selected counts/dimensions fit even 31-bit Int.

Lazy variants retain explicit memoized orbit heads/spines and the feedback
list knot. The current module also retains a lazy take spine. Coordinates are
passed as delays so limit0 does not evaluate them. Historical zero-limit and
boundary behavior are tested separately. Strict variants materialize finite
orbits, with limit elements for the current module and limit+1 for the old
consumer; a final-element case avoids an unintended additional step. They may
compute unused post-escape IEEE infinities/NaNs before the consumer stops;
those values are not reported as pixel results. Strict grid/pixel lists replace
the lazy spines explicitly. Final integer RGB values must agree with the
corresponding original variant.

A polymorphic Pixmap wrapper retains metadata and either the stream or strict
list. Full-image reference checks remain available, while the timed driver
consumes every RGB channel into a checked 64-bit rolling digest and exact pixel
count, then checks metadata and EOF. It reports repetitions:checked instead
of the original empty stdout. The digest starts at 1013904223 and folds each
r/g/b in order with h=h*1664525+value modulo 2^64. Hashing/checking costs are
measured work; they are not original Haskell runtime timings.

## mandel2-lazy

Selected: memoized corner colours and children with source right-spine forcing.

## Algorithm and workload

Build an adaptive binary MandTree with NS/EW children and integer-colour leaves.
Check rectangle corners and selected perimeter points; retain a leaf when the
source considers them uniform, otherwise split the longer axis (x on ties).
The default root is inclusive (0,0)..(200,100); coordinate scaling still uses
the source size constant 200 and denominator199. It is not a 200x200 image.
Each point uses binary32 arithmetic, initial z=0, escape radius-squared20 and
26 colour levels. Test k+1==26 before demanding the next coordinate/radius.

## History, authorship, revision and aliases

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, spectral/mandel2/Main.hs,
Makefile and the NofibUtils.hs symlink to common/NofibUtils.hs. The header
credits David Hanley and is dated 11/03/1992; it cites The Beauty of Fractals,
page121. Preserve the exact date and source text. These individual files
state no separate redistribution notice; do not invent a grant from another
program's license. Record the symlink bytes, resolved source and original path.
The explicit names mandel2-lazy/mandel2-strict distinguish evaluation variants
from mandel's complex-orbit pixmaps and other Mandelbrot programs.

## Exact source quirks and evaluation variants

Preserve the original perimeter direction conditions. Positive-height vertical
checks usually stop immediately; zero-height rectangles can scan above/below
their bounds until colours differ. Do not repair the inequalities or clamp
coordinates. The complete independent 200-root model observes 707 distinct
outside coordinates; this is a model observation, not an instrumented GHC call
count. The resulting tree is the specified workload, not a claim of equivalence
to evaluating every interior pixel.

The source's par is locally defined as a sequential no-op. Its right child is
forced to WHNF before a node is constructed, while the left stays lazy; this
recursively forces a right spine. The lazy port preserves memoized children,
corner-colour sharing and short circuiting. The strict variant evaluates all
four corner bindings and completes the right subtree before the left. Those
costs and retention differences are intentional; complete tree results agree.
Counting point-function tests cover unused corners, one shared col1, the
single-point case, outward scans, right-first forcing and memoized children.

## Portable SML translation and numerical semantics

A finite-normal binary32 helper represents selected values exactly in binary64
and rounds every source add/subtract/multiply/divide to 24 significand bits,
nearest-even. It preserves signed zero. Source coefficients are dyadic except
the fixed 3/199 step; original bit fixtures validate coordinates, every selected
orbit step, radius and colour. Preserve left association in 2*x*y+q. SML97
Real is required to have binary64 representation; no new compiler/runtime
Float32 feature or native-host Real32 substitution is introduced.

This is a workload-specific helper, not general support for binary32 NaNs,
subnormals or overflow. Active selected orbits remain in its finite-normal/zero
domain; unsupported values raise Domain rather than silently widening the
workload. Complete tree comparisons and per-operation bit checks exercise
all selected paths. Final tree tags/bounds/colours require exact agreement;
no floating tolerance accepts a different split or colour.

Tree nodes retain delayed or strict children and the source NS/EW/Leaf shapes.
Default Int represents bounded geometry, colours and counts, all within signed
31-bit limits. A point-function module parameter permits direct demand tests;
it does not change the numerical function. Complete preorder validation
reconstructs bounds and checks every node, colour and EOF. Serialization,
checking and reference I/O are measured work. The final result reports checked
repetitions and node count rather than the source's empty stdout.

## Inputs, optimizer barrier and runtime questions

Smoke uses one root extent64 via the original build_tree API, with the global
coordinate scale left at200. Normal uses the full200 extent and upstream FAST
2 repetitions. Selected large uses full200 and upstream NORM20; source SLOW100
is retained as an original execution/reference, not silently relabeled.

The original salt is pure with NOINLINE, preventing invariant-input floating.
A deterministic SML97-generated size file supplies one runtime extent per
repetition as a portable input dependency. It preserves the fixed size values,
while adding documented one-line input/parsing work. The driver bounds extents
to1..200 and repetitions to1..100, validates each complete tree and requires
EOF in the size file. Its first line is the repetition count, followed by
exactly that many integer extents. Expected preorder rows contain NS/EW plus
four bounds, or L plus bounds and the leaf colour. No exact-value guard before construction exposes a
constant extent to the optimizer. No FFI, effects or parallel runtime is needed.

Source-based performance questions include emulated binary32 cost, corner
sharing/short circuiting, source outward scans, tree allocation/retention,
right-spine forcing, specialization and GC interaction. These remain hypotheses
unless supported by source analysis or measurements. Standard reports compare
identical SML; original Haskell supplies correctness evidence.

## References and recorded limits

Original executions terminate at2/20/100 repetitions. Complete GHC trees agree
with an independent struct-packed binary32/perimeter model for extents
1/2/3/8/16/64/200. Golden bit patterns and full-tree checks preserve the source's
unusual boundaries and arithmetic. Negative fixtures change colour/branch,
truncate or append rows. Large SML execution is claimed only when recorded.

A preliminary full-tree host run shows default-nursery differences on managed
legacy64 SML/NJ despite its passing scalar bit checks. The same original-source
contexts pass with a 64 MiB nursery. Diagnostic callback changes move the first
mismatch. This is nursery/context-sensitive evidence consistent with existing
GC reports; its first corrupt operation is not reduced. Preserve failed
outputs, source identities and diagnostic settings; do not change the kernel,
expectation or default configuration to hide the result. Final profile outcomes
must be recorded separately from these preliminary contexts.

[Peitgen and Richter, The Beauty of Fractals](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-61717-1)
provides the cited mathematical background; page121 is an upstream attribution,
not a claim that the page was independently audited here. The suite's nofib
and measurement references supply context. Neither the book nor these source
observations establishes the relative speed of the SML variants.

[Complete provenance](mandel2-lazy/PROVENANCE.md).

## boyer2-lazy

Selected evaluation: lazy finite terms, LUT paths and rule-bucket spines.

## Algorithm and workload

Parse a Lisp-like rule base, construct its unbalanced lookup tree, substitute
into a transitivity statement, rewrite arguments before ordered lemma attempts,
and check the resulting conditional term as a tautology. Each iteration inserts
a distinct cN atom into two substitution terms. Preserve statement/substitution
text, rule insertion order, association lookup, short circuiting and every result.
The z substitution uses the source's [] symbol, without renaming it to nil.

## History, authorship, revision and variants

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, spectral/boyer2/Main.hs,
Lisplikefns.hs, Rewritefns.hs, Checker.hs, Rulebasetext.hs and Makefile. Headers
credit Tony Kitto's Hope+ work beginning March1988 and record a June1993 Haskell
conversion as JSM; do not expand those initials without evidence. Rule comments
cite Gabriel pages118..126 and record the altered or rule. Individual files
state no separate license; retain their notices without importing the public-
domain claim from the different nofib boyer program.

Classic SML boyer and nofib boyer share ancestry, but this implementation parses
text into binary Nil/Atom/Cons nodes and uses an unbalanced string-keyed LUT,
rather than per-function embedded lemma fields/property lists. It also varies
cN each iteration. Preserve these material variants as boyer2-lazy/strict,
without conflating their implementations or expected normal forms.

## Exact source behavior and quirks

The lexer treats only space and parentheses as delimiters. Tabs remain symbol
characters. Trailing spaces can produce an empty token; top-level leftover
tokens return Nil. The parser accepts end-of-input without a final close.
Selectors on non-cons values return Nil. Association lookup stops on malformed
entries. Unification terminates successfully when the first argument list ends,
even if the pattern list has remaining arguments. Do not silently strengthen
it to equal-length matching.

One retained difference rule has no RHS after parsing. The source accepts it
into the LUT and caddr returns Nil. Preserve that exact malformed string and
behavior; independent references explicitly account for it. New rules prepend
to a matching bucket, so reversing insertion priority changes the workload.

## Portable translation, laziness and state

SML97 retains binary Lisp nodes, association lists, unbalanced persistent LUT
nodes and ordered rule buckets. The lazy variant memoizes term/tree/bucket
spines and fields; substitution and rewrite results are demanded by the checker.
The strict variant constructs finite terms, bucket spines and LUT paths eagerly.
Both retain short-circuit matching/Boolean logic and agree on results. A shared
Nil and empty bucket represent source nullary constructors.

Tokens use immutable SML strings instead of Haskell character lists; tokenization
is strict while preserving exact token boundaries and text. Literal rule strings
are extracted byte-for-byte, including spaces, into a portable SML data module.
The original raw source and extraction/reference scripts remain available.
The active rule base and statement are immutable CAF-like caches. An outer
memoized delay in both variants keeps parsing/LUT construction inside runtime
execution, including native-host export adapters. Repeated in-process calls may
reuse these immutable caches, as the source does; fresh-process runs start anew.
No mutable substitution state leaks between theorem inputs.

Indices/counts use bounded default Int; selected 0..3000 inputs and rule/string
sizes fit 31 bits. Runtime cN construction uses decimal positive integers. No
arbitrary-precision or modular numeric operation is silently substituted.

## Inputs, validation and compiler/runtime questions

Smoke runs one theorem; normal preserves NORM600 and large SLOW3000. Upstream
FAST60 also has a complete reference. Every original result/report line agrees
with the pinned fixtures. The portable driver validates every Boolean result,
then reports count:proved instead of printing the repeated report sentence.
Bounds and output suppression are explicit driver adaptations. No dataset or
external runtime facility is needed.

Four complete input/rewritten forms agree between original GHC and an independent
proper-tree/dictionary rewrite model. An independent truth-table evaluator checks
all 32 assignments for each normalized formula. SML lazy/strict variants compare
every byte of the complete normal forms in supplemental checks. Negative checks
reject wrong, truncated and extra forms; small tests cover parsing, rule order,
unification quirks, failed-head tail demand, substitution and false formulas.
Forcing complete normal forms is a test observation, not extra benchmark work:
the timed driver retains the original tautology check's demand pattern.

Source-based questions include parsing cost, string comparisons, unbalanced LUT
shape, rule priority, memoized rewriting, eager unused terms, sharing and cache
warmup. Treat them as hypotheses until measured/inspected. Standard comparisons
use identical SML; GHC supplies correctness references. Large execution is claimed
only where recorded. Gabriel's Performance and Evaluation of Lisp Systems and
the nofib/measurement survey supply context; their historical results do not
establish causes or rankings for this translation.

[Complete provenance](boyer2-lazy/PROVENANCE.md).

reject wrong, truncated and extra forms; small tests cover parsing, rule order,
unification quirks, failed-head tail demand, substitution and false formulas.
Forcing complete normal forms is a test observation, not extra benchmark work:
the timed driver retains the original tautology check's demand pattern.

Source-based questions include parsing cost, string comparisons, unbalanced LUT
shape, rule priority, memoized rewriting, eager unused terms, sharing and cache
warmup. Treat them as hypotheses until measured/inspected. Standard comparisons
use identical SML; GHC supplies correctness references. Large execution is claimed
only where recorded. Gabriel's Performance and Evaluation of Lisp Systems and
the nofib/measurement survey supply context; their historical results do not
establish causes or rankings for this translation.

## pretty-lazy

Selected evaluation: lazy metadata fields, CharSeq nodes and output.

## Algorithm and workload

Construct a higher-order document containing the -42/@/string header, comma-space
line and a hanging label followed by repeated xxxxx words. Pretty functions take
width and vertical context and return text, last-line length, emptiness and fit
metadata. A separate CharSeq tree stores append/indent/newline/string/character
nodes; flatten it with an indentation worklist, then append the Main newline.
Preserve this metadata-driven layout and tree traversal rather than replacing
the benchmark with direct construction of its known output string.

## History, authorship, revision and aliases

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, spectral/pretty/Main.hs,
Pretty.hs, CharSeq.hs, Makefile and pretty.stdout. The selected headers state
no author or separate redistribution notice. Retain the files and comments
about historical nhc/hbc behavior without inventing attribution or a license.
Explicit pretty-lazy/strict names distinguish evaluation variants. This is the
pinned flag-based implementation, not a replacement modern pretty library.

## Known behavior and variant differences

The source uses ppCat, which keeps all repeated words beside each other. Width80
does not wrap its default 50 words; the hang decision chooses a new indented
line. Tabs represent each complete group of eight indentation columns. Empty
string differs from nil; trailing spaces, the final newline, and raw embedded
newlines remain observable. ppNest applies only in vertical context. Retain the
source's horizontal contexts for both ppHang candidates, including its TODO.

The lazy variant memoizes whole pretty results, individual metadata fields,
CharSeq nodes and character output. Fit/emptiness tests can avoid unused child
results or layout alternatives. The strict variant evaluates finite metadata,
CharSeq and output nodes eagerly. Both retain a memoized cyclic word-input
stream with a finite take boundary: forcing an infinite strict producer is
not substituted for the source input. Complete output bytes agree.

## Portable SML translation and representation

SML97 implements the required document combinators, append/indent worklist,
short-circuit flags and character lists. Field delays preserve where-bound
sharing and non-demand; ordinary strict Boolean function calls would force too
much. Source constructors whose nil/indent simplifications were commented out
remain unsimplified. Selected ASCII literals use SML char lists; no Unicode
workload is claimed. Source negative integer spelling becomes '-' in output,
while bounded counts/widths fit even 31-bit Int.

The port covers the benchmark's required APIs and adds source combinators used
by edge tests. Unused PprStyle and numeric-formatting exports remain in the
retained upstream files, without claiming a complete general-purpose library.
Each invocation constructs the document/results anew; only constant constructor
cells and immutable input values are shared. Checking consumes every byte and
EOF and reports width:words:bytes rather than writing the formatted document to
stdout. Reference I/O and validation costs are measured work.

## Profiles, checks and diagnostic questions

Smoke width20/10 words uses the source ppShow/take interface. Normal preserves
width80/50 words and the pinned 343-byte output. Selected large width80/5000
words has a complete 30043-byte original/independent reference. The driver bounds
width to0..65535 and words to0..5000. No universal size argument or acquired data
is introduced.

Unmodified GHC output agrees with the fixture. Parameterized original calls and
an independent main-document layout model agree at empty, one-word, fit-boundary,
smoke/normal/large inputs. Eleven original combinator edge layouts agree with
independent expected bytes. Tests cover unused alternatives, negative-width
short circuiting, shared child metadata/text, nil indentation demand, and exact
spaces/tabs/newlines. Changed bytes/whitespace, truncation and extra output fail.

Source-based questions include closure allocation, metadata selection, lazy
record sharing, eager alternative construction, CharSeq traversal, worklist
retention and output lists. They remain hypotheses until source/measurement
analysis establishes them. Standard reports compare identical SML; Haskell is
an original correctness reference. Large execution is claimed only when
recorded. The maintained nofib source and suite measurement literature provide
context; a general pretty-printing paper does not specify these exact flags,
TODO behaviors or output bytes.

[Complete provenance](pretty-lazy/PROVENANCE.md).

## last-piece-lazy

Selected evaluation: lazy candidates, remaining-piece inputs and solution tree.

## Algorithm and workload

Tile the fixed 8x8 board using the source's sex-constrained piece orientations.
Start with the three-square a piece, scan row-major from (1,2) Female, choose a
remaining piece/orientation, fit it into a persistent board map, and recursively
construct Soln/Choose/Fail search results. Render every solution in source order.
The full puzzle has three solutions; retain the exact piece data and ordering.

## History, revision, authorship and dependencies

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798,
spectral/last-piece/Main.hs, Makefile and last-piece.stdout. The header credits
Simon Peyton Jones, May 2002. It states no separate redistribution notice;
retain the original without inventing a grant from another component.

Original GHC 9.4.7 uses containers 0.6.7 and pretty 1.1.3.6. Pin containers at
9f4a93604c66a5e605ce46fc30003b71802b3cfd and pretty at
c3a1469306b35fa5d023dc570554f97f1a90435d. Retain complete selected source files,
package versions and BSD-style notices. Map source credits Daan Leijen and
Andriy Palamarchuk; the rendering module credits Glasgow and the Hughes/
Peyton Jones design. The explicit last-piece-lazy/strict names preserve
meaningful search-tree evaluation variants.

## Source ordering, preconditions and variants

pickOne reverses the skipped prefix: choices for [a,b,c] leave [b,c], [a,c],
then [b,a]. Do not replace it with the usual stable-order deletion. Orientations
retain their exact order and share the remaining-piece thunk for one piece.
Fitting checks offsets first and inserts the anchor last without another bounds/
occupancy check. Source search establishes that anchor precondition; direct fit
is not silently strengthened. Row transitions and occupied squares flip sex
exactly as written. Selected offsets keep rows positive, so the source's absent
lower-row guard is not added.

The lazy variant memoizes candidate/result spines and solution children, fitting
one candidate before demanding its recursive search. Rendering visits all
solutions/failures in the source order. The strict variant constructs finite
candidates and the complete result tree eagerly, retaining the same board-map
algorithm and output. Both agree on full outputs; their temporary allocation,
retention and evaluation timing differ.

## Portable SML translation

SML97 keeps the size-balanced persistent map with cached subtree sizes,
delta3/ratio2 and the source's specialized balanceL/balanceR rotations. Every
insertion-prefix shape agrees with original containers on four 64-key traces.
It is not replaced with an AVL or mutable occupancy array. Native pointer-
equality insertion shortcuts are omitted: benchmark insertions use fresh keys,
so those early returns cannot occur. General replacement values preserve map
contents/shape without claiming identical pointer-identity optimizations.

Board keys, offsets, sizes and counts fit signed 31-bit Int. Piece identifiers
are the original ASCII characters. Remaining-piece and orientation lists retain
their values; candidate/result nodes and shared remaining lists use explicit
memoized delays where needed. Immutable piece data/initial board may be shared;
each solve call reconstructs the result tree, preventing previous solutions
from being reused as a repeated-run result cache.

The used-domain renderer replaces the external pretty library with portable
SML emission. Fixed board lines fit width200 and ribbon ratio1.5; no wrapping
alternative is exercised. Preserve Success!, reverse row display, two-space
nesting, indented blank lines and the final newline, including empty-result
behavior. This is not a claimed port of every general pretty API. Full byte/EOF
checking and reference I/O replace stdout and are measured work. The driver
reports remaining:solutions:bytes only after complete validation.

## Profiles and diagnostic questions

Smoke leaves the last two source pieces and preplaces the others from the first
reviewed original solution. This is a valid subproblem through the original
search API, with the same board size, initial a, sex and orientation rules.
Normal preserves all 13 remaining pieces and the original three solutions.
An eight-piece subproblem is also retained as a correctness reference. The
fixed original board is already the maximum source instance, so no artificial
large profile is introduced; the harness still supports explicit repeated mode.
The driver bounds remaining pieces to 0..13. SML generates runtime board inputs
from exact embedded data; no external dataset or input-generating interpreter
is required.

Source-based questions include map rotation/allocation, failed fits, reversed
choice order, memoized search, eager result retention and rendering/check costs.
These remain hypotheses until source/measurement evidence establishes effects.
Standard reports compare identical SML. No parallelism, FFI, effects or compiler/
runtime feature is required.

## References and validation

The unmodified original's complete 300-byte output matches the pinned fixture.
Original prefix calls and an independent bitmask/reversed-choice model agree on
all boards and exact output for 0/2/8/13 remaining pieces. The full model visits
103513 search states and finds three solutions; original tree statistics agree.
Every board covers all 64 squares. The smoke/normal inputs are not fabricated
by merely dropping pieces from an empty board.

Tests cover 256 complete map-prefix shapes, initial board, reversed pickOne,
shared/delayed remaining pieces, unforced child search, source fit preconditions,
complete prefix outputs/statistics and changed/truncated/extra output rejection.
Both SML variants reproduce the full original output in bounded preflights.
Large or other configuration validation is claimed only where recorded.
Pinned source and dependency explanations provide the exact implementation
reference; the shared nofib/measurement literature supplies context without
claiming a measured performance cause for this translation.

[Complete provenance](last-piece-lazy/PROVENANCE.md).
