indices and formatting counters have explicit bounded widths; signed zeros are
distinguished by the encoder. The initial timestep has bits 3CA3D70A. Each driver
invocation creates a fresh experiment instead of retaining the source top-level
test CAF across repeated suite invocations. Internal child-stream sharing is
retained. Profile arguments and the reviewed position file are read once.

Numeric formatting uses SML GEN9 instead of Haskell's shortest Float renderer.
Every numeric character is inspected, a binary32 roundtrip is checked, and tab/
newline lengths are consumed. Renderer-dependent text lengths are bounded rather
than exposed as cross-compiler expected output. Controlled output reports
position-count:rolling-bit-checkword, using explicitly modular Word32 xor/multiply
(seed 811C9DC5, multiplier 01000193). Every position is independently checked
against its fixture before contributing; this checkword does not replace checking.

### Compiler/runtime diagnostic questions

Investigate unshared recursive calls, within-invocation sharing, finite eager/
lazy vectors, unused velocities, closures, list temporaries, GC and whole-program
specialization. Emulated binary32 rounding and format validation are substantial
parts of this SML workload. Timing comparisons use identical SML across compilers;
GHC supplies correctness references. The source's historical compiler story does
not establish a performance explanation for current configurations.

### Inputs, correctness and references

| Profile | Displayed states | Input origin |
|---|---:|---|
| smoke | 100 | bounded prefix of the original FAST workload |
| normal | 2500 | unchanged NORM_OPTS |
| large | 4000 | unchanged SLOW_OPTS |

All three original 1000/2500/4000-state text fixtures remain in provenance.
Smoke uses 100 states to cover negative positions while keeping routine checks
bounded; normal/large keep the original parameters. Default limits apply.
Upstream text/bit observers agree with an independent linear binary32 Euler model
on all 4000 positions and velocities. Observers force velocities for auxiliary
checking; the primary lazy benchmark preserves the position-only demand.

SML probes check exact position/state bits, stream demand/triangular structure,
source vector quirks, sharing, ties to even, signed zero, finite-helper domain,
format roundtrip and wrong/short/extra references. Whole normal Rune O2 pilots
validate both policies at 2500 positions. Other coverage is recorded in validation.md.

[The pinned program](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/blob/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/spectral/atom/Main.hs)
provides the algorithm, attribution and historical explanation.
[Partain](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17) supplies nofib context.
[The SML Real interface](https://smlfamily.github.io/Basis/real.html) specifies the
rounding/conversion operations used by the helper. Source analysis, finite-input
bit checks and future performance explanations have separate evidence scopes.


## exact-reals-lazy

Finite series evaluation: lazy.

### Algorithm and workload

Represent a constructive real by a function from requested binary precision to
an arbitrary-precision integer approximant. Evaluate the left-associated sum of
sin(i*pi), i=1..n, and render forty decimal places. The result is zero, but the
port performs the source exact arithmetic, range reduction and power series.
Nonzero scalar reference cases independently exercise its arithmetic.

### History, authorship, revision and notices

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, spectral/exact-reals/Main.hs,
Makefile and exact-reals.stdout. The header credits David Lester's 2012 paper,
[The world's shortest correct exact real arithmetic program?](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ic.2011.09.004),
Information and Computation 216, pages 39–46. Preserve the complete program and
fixture. These files state no separate redistribution notice. The suite retains
the established exact-reals name and gives meaningful evaluation variants
explicit lazy/strict suffixes.

Selected GHC base sources are pinned at 00920f176b0235d5bb52a8e054d89a664f8938fe.
Full base/LICENSE and the Ratio, Enum, List and Foldable sources preserve their
own notices. Their scope does not confer a notice on Lester's program.

### Evaluation, representation and translation

CR remains a precision-to-IntInf function. Function results are not memoized by
precision. Multiplication shares its two bound calculations within the CR value;
reciprocal repeats its precision search on every function call, as written.
Top-level pi, pi/2, pi/4 and sqrt(1/2) constructions and infinite coefficient
streams are memoized. Constants store CR functions, never precomputed answers.

The lazy policy suspends finite coefficient/power lists and their heads, stopping
at the first zero rounded term without forcing the unused tail. The strict policy
constructs those selected finite lists and evaluates their heads eagerly. Infinite
coefficient streams remain delayed in both. This policy deliberately exposes
otherwise unused series terms; the algorithm, bounds and requested precision stay
the same. No infinite list is made eager.

Keep the source left-associated sum. GHC.List/Foldable's list sum uses a strict
left fold; each CR addition still stores a function and requests two extra guard
bits from its operands. Reassociating or balancing the sum would change both work
and precision propagation. Enum CR uses the source default integer enumeration:
fromEnum evaluates at digitsToBits(40)=137, rounds to an integer, and toEnum
constructs each exact integer CR. The endpoints are not replaced by an unchecked
host loop convention.

Reuse the portable exact ratio operations shared with SCS. They follow GHC's
cross-product/reduction rules using IntInf, including normalization and gcd.
Each floor-square-root improvement constructs and normalizes its source ratio
before floor division. Rounding is floor(rational+1/2), with ties toward positive
infinity, including negative half integers. It is independent of host Real.round.
Only digitsToBits uses binary64 log/ceiling, yielding 137 for the selected forty digits. Full scalar and rendered
references are checked on every host. All integer precision counters fit signed 31-bit; arbitrary
precision intermediates retain IntInf.

Implement the source sine, cosine, atan branches, range reduction and square-root
path needed by this workload and auxiliary checks. Unused logarithm, exponential,
hyperbolic, reading and instance methods are omitted from the SML kernel; the
complete original remains. Finite SML strings replace Haskell output lists.
Read/validate arguments once per run, construct a fresh summation and compare
every rendered character with the forty-zero result before accepting it.
Coefficient/constant sharing persists across repeated in-process calls, as source
top-level definitions do; final sums are not cached. No runtime feature is added.

### Inputs, validation and calibration

| Profile | Summation endpoint | Origin |
|---|---:|---|
| smoke | 1 | small complete sum at unchanged forty digits |
| normal | 10 | calibrated complete sum at unchanged forty digits |
| large | 60 | original FAST_OPTS |

Upstream NORM_OPTS=350 and SLOW_OPTS=800 remain documented and available in
original reference evidence, but are not the suite normal/large choices. An
initial Rune stack pilot at endpoint 60 reached its 600-second limit before
finishing the lazy case; the combined pilot never started strict mode. This
records a time limit, not a wrong result. Endpoints 1 and 10 validate on both
policies at full precision. Large keeps the default 3600-second/8-GiB limit;
whole large SML validation is only claimed where separately recorded.

Rune's current IntInf library uses portable base-2^30 limbs and quotient-limb
search. This exact-rational workload is much more expensive there than on native
hosts with different big-integer implementations. Reducing digits, replacing
ratios with unchecked division or changing the summation would alter the workload;
they are not calibration changes. Profiles change n only.

Original GHC executions at 60/350/800 match the complete shared zero fixture.
Export-only observers record their 137-bit integer approximants as zero.
Fourteen scalar cases (pi, signed thirds, sqrt(1/2), trigonometric values and atan
across its branches) supply 84 exact integer approximants at six precisions and
14 forty-place texts. Both policies must match these source outputs exactly.
An independent 120-decimal-digit mpmath calculation checks integer error <=1
scaled unit and text error <=5.1e-41; this is a numerical cross-check, not a formal
proof. No floating tolerance replaces the primary exact output comparison.

Auxiliary tests cover half-integer rounding, first-zero stopping, unused inputs,
shared multiplication bounds, repeated reciprocal searches, left-addition
precision, small integer square roots, enum endpoints and the empty sum.
Primary smoke/normal matrices and counts use the manifest. Raw evidence and
validation scopes are recorded separately in validation.md.

### Compiler/runtime diagnostic questions and literature

Investigate arbitrary-precision arithmetic, gcd/normalization, function closures,
guard-bit propagation, coefficient sharing, early series termination, finite
eager evaluation, allocation lifetimes and whole-program specialization.
These are source-based hypotheses, not measured causal explanations. The common
SML program is the compiler comparison; original Haskell is a correctness
reference. Tiny or single-sample native runs are adapter diagnostics.

Lester's paper supplies the constructive-real algorithm and its error argument.
[Partain](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17) supplies suite context.
The pinned original and base sources supply the specific definitions translated
here; the independent high-precision check does not establish universal correctness.

## minimax-lazy

Finite data evaluation: lazy.

### Algorithm and workload

Play the original tic-tac-toe game from a board with O at row 1/column 2 and X
at row 2/column 2. Generate moves in row-major order, alternate maximizing and
minimizing players, build alternating game trees, prune at depth five, map the
source static score, crop winning nodes and evaluate by a right fold. Retain
first-board tie breaking. Play until a win or a full board. Maximizing/minimizing
players remain function arguments through selection and recursive evaluation.

### History, variants and notices

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, spectral/minimax, all six
Haskell modules and Makefile. No author or individual redistribution notice is
stated in those files. Complete originals remain. The established minimax name
gets lazy/strict suffixes for material finite evaluation variants. It is not
combined with other game/search workloads merely because they use similar ideas.

The original driver takes one decimal string as both repetition count and prog
input. Every selected string chooses the same test board; only the impossible
driver string "doesn't happen" takes its six-row branch. Preserve that branch
and its subsequent pattern failure in auxiliary tests.

### Demand, data and portable translation

Use the same nested finite board/row lists and immutable piece values. Replacing
a piece reconstructs the complete three-cell row and three-row board, retaining
unchanged cell/row references. Game trees retain separate repetition, pruning,
mapping, cropping and evaluation stages rather than a direct recursive solver.
Static scoring keeps the eight winning-mask order and cumulative nonwinning
scores. The full-board test retains its mapped Boolean list. Position
comprehensions construct fresh delayed row/column enumerations per call. Winning constructors short circuit the right fold in lazy mode.

The lazy variant memoizes finite list spines/heads, tree roots and payloads.
Depth-zero pruning avoids generating children; cropping a winning node inspects
the child spine but avoids its head. The strict variant eagerly constructs these
finite values, including the complete unpruned tree before the depth-five cut,
and evaluates fold tails before a winning first value can discard them. All
trees are finite as moves consume empty squares. A counted linear-tree probe
distinguishes zero child expansions at lazy depth-zero pruning from four eager
expansions. This substantial work/allocation difference is deliberate.

Inclusive index loops become finite lists. Bounded scores, indices, repetition
counts and selected output lengths fit signed 31-bit int. No optional runtime
facility is used. The source printed result is the complete 194-character game,
including five XWin evaluations, but Main only forces length(prog input) and
prints nothing. The SML driver fully renders and checks every character against
a reviewed fixture, then reports repetitions:total-character-count. SML string
construction and complete validation are added costs compared with lazy
character-spine length consumption.

Each repetition constructs a fresh board/tree/game. Original compilers may share
the invariant prog result inside their loop; the port does not precompute a
repeated-run answer. Original Haskell runs supply correctness references, while
comparative timing uses the identical SML on all hosts.

### Inputs, validation and literature

| Profile | Complete fresh games | Origin |
|---|---:|---|
| smoke | 1 | bounded repetition count, original board/depth |
| normal | 100 | bounded repetition count, original board/depth |
| large | 1000 | scaling repetition count, original board/depth |

Original FAST/NORM/SLOW counts 180000/1800000/9000000 remain in Makefile and
provenance. The selected counts accommodate fresh reconstruction and the eager
variant while retaining the complete game and depth five. Default limits apply.
Both normal Rune O2 pilots validate all 100 games under their recorded guards;
larger coverage is claimed only for separately recorded runs.

Unmodified GHC runs produce empty stdout as expected. An export-only observer
records the full game and seven immediate static scores. A separate Python
position evaluator agrees on that complete game and eleven varied board
analyses, including both wins, ties and first-winning-mask behavior. GHC confirms
all eleven complete static/max/min analyses. SML tests also cover repetition,
wrong-character rejection, occupied squares, stable ties, invalid board shape,
prune/score demand and eager construction.

[Partain](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17) supplies nofib context;
the preserved Board/Game/Tree/Wins/Prog modules define this particular heuristic,
tree depth and evaluation order. They are source evidence for diagnostic
questions about closures, sharing, short circuiting, tree allocation, higher-order
folds and specialization. No measured causal explanation is asserted.

## nbody-sandmark-multicore-numerical

## Algorithm and workload

Create randomly distributed mutable bodies, apply the original momentum offset,
compute energy, advance by dt=0.01 and compute final energy. Each advance visits
every ordered i,j pair with i!=j, updating only body i's velocity. Update all
positions in a separate pass after the velocity loops.

This differs from nbody-sandmark's five fixed solar-system bodies and symmetric
i<j pair updates, and from the classic immutable SML/NJ implementation. Preserve
the existing unsuffixed classic name and -sandmark name; the category suffix
disambiguates this additional sequential workload.

### History, sources, authorship and notices

Sandmark 5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507,
benchmarks/multicore-numerical/nbody.ml and its sequential Dune executable.
The header credits Troestler Christophe and Computer Language Benchmarks Game
ancestry. Retain the complete source, Dune file, individual directory revised-BSD
LICENSE (Brent Fulgham/Isaac Gouy), aggregate LICENSE.md and both applicable
run-plan extracts. The directory's parallel executable has a separate deferred
inventory disposition; no domain/parallel support is added here.

The OCaml 4.14.1 Random replacement is shared with the earlier sequential
Sandmark array imports. Its full source, LGPL 2.1/linking-exception notice and pin
99cb5d93fc30f1a6f3e69f5aa5d2063994d33a93 remain beside this import too.
The tested installed reference matches that version. Inputs are generated
internally; no external dataset or unstated seed is introduced.

### Portable translation, evaluation and numerical behavior

Keep seven fields per body, six mutable. SML real refs implement mutable record
fields and a mutable array holds distinct records. Reuse the identical source
energy, momentum and state helpers from the five-body port; its unused fixed
initializer is not called. The ordered-pair advance remains a separate kernel.
Tail-recursive helpers implement inclusive loops. Field arithmetic retains
binary64 operation order; no pair symmetry, vectorization, softening, collision
rule or alternative force algorithm is introduced.

The compiled original evaluates record initializer fields right to left:
mass,vz,vy,vx,z,y,x. Explicit SML bindings preserve that random draw assignment.
The default 55-word generator state is copied per invocation, with every draw
and floating mapping retained. Initial zero-step state fixtures and an independent
generator model check the chosen order. This records the tested OCaml order;
it does not assert that the OCaml language specifies that record evaluation order.

Keep the source's offset denominator solar_mass even though body zero has a
random mass. Consequently, the routine name does not imply zero total momentum.
The random masses, positions and velocities retain their original ranges and
scales. Each run creates fresh body fields and RNG state instead of retaining
a previously advanced top-level array.

The original prints two energies with nine fractional digits. A reference-only
observer changes those two format precisions to 17 significant digits and exports
all seven final fields per body. Its prefix rounds back to the unmodified
original stdout. The SML driver checks both energies and every state field,
rejects nonfinite values and validates exact length before returning
steps:body-count:checked-number-count. Reference parsing and full checking are
measured additions.

### Inputs, result bounds and validation

| Profile | Steps | Bodies | Origin |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| smoke | 1 | 16 | bounded complete simulation |
| normal | 20 | 256 | bounded comparative workload |
| large | 500 | 1024 | unchanged source defaults |

The published run plans also select 512/2048 and 128/8192. These larger
configurations are recorded in provenance but not selected profiles. No claim
is made that every upstream run configuration has been validated in SML.
Default resource limits apply to the three selected profiles.

Each finite number uses absolute bound 1e-9 plus relative bound 1e-11 times
the expected magnitude. These tolerances allow small binary64 differences in
the recorded operation sequence; they are not energy-conservation or physical
accuracy bounds. Every energy, coordinate, velocity and mass is independently
checked. Deliberate changes exceeding the bound in each of the 30 components
of a four-body fixture must be rejected; an interior perturbation is accepted.
Short, extra, NaN and infinite results are rejected.

Original OCaml runs and full-state observers cover small cases, smoke, normal,
source-default large and larger initial arrays. A separate Python binary64
generator/simulator agrees exactly on all checked initial/small/smoke/normal
numbers. It reuses the reviewed default seed words, not the SML update code.
Original large integration has reference evidence; whole large SML validation is
claimed only where separately recorded. Auxiliary tests cover distinct/fresh
body fields, ordered two-body updates, the solar-mass offset quirk and fresh RNG
state.

### Diagnostic questions and references

Source inspection suggests numerical operation lowering, bounds checks, nested
loops, field/ref representation, mutation, random generation and validation
costs as hypotheses to investigate. Compiler comparisons use identical SML.
The original OCaml and independent model are correctness references, not timing
competitors. The retained source and Sandmark survey establish ancestry; the
Barnes-Hut literature describes a different tree approximation and is not used
to explain this all-pairs workload's measured behavior.


## array_iter

## Algorithm and workload

Visit every identity-array element and retain the source upper-bound assertion.

Array generation retains make-zero-array followed by index mapping into a distinct array. The selected arrays are ordinary mutable integer arrays. SML Array.foldl/app and an explicit short-circuit forall loop replace their OCaml counterparts. The original asserts unit for iter/forall; unit is encoded as zero in the report. Every final array element is independently checked.

### History, source and notices

Sandmark 5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507, benchmarks/stdlib,
the retained original module and Dune executable. The module states no individual
author or separate notice. Preserve the aggregate LICENSE.md and original bytes.
Names follow the executable's selector strings; distinct selectors remain
distinct workloads. Result-only Sys.opaque_identity wrappers do not require a
new compiler barrier: the portable driver consumes/checks their results. No
claim is made that such wrappers prevent every optimization inside the operation.

### Portable translation and library changes

Kernels, generation and checks are SML97. Inclusive loops become tail-recursive
helpers; all selected indices, loop counts, scalar comparisons and individual
fold results fit signed 31-bit. The observer total may be larger, so the measured
driver uses explicitly modular Word32 addition, with wrapping independent of
native int width. Counters stay bounded and the final expected arithmetic uses
IntInf outside the hot loop.

The common report is calls:hex-checkword:negative:zero:positive. It consumes each

## primetest-lazy

Finite evaluation: lazy.

### Algorithm and workload

Process decimal integer candidates with the source 100-round strong probable-prime
test. Even/nonpositive guards consume no random values. For each odd candidate,
factor n-1 as 2^k*q, select the source base, compute the nested modular-power
algorithm and inspect up to k repeated squares for its witness. Composite
witnesses stop the remaining trials early.

### History, authorship, variants and notices

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, spectral/primetest,
the four literate Haskell modules, Makefile, Readme, mersenne607 and all three
stdin/stdout pairs. Main's author macro explicitly names David Lester; its RCS
last-committer tag is history, not that declaration. The log dates the program
to 1992 and records the 2004 Random-to-MyRandom rename. IntLib credits Joe Fasel
for this modular-power coding; MyRandom credits Lennart Augustsson's generator.
No separate redistribution notice or dataset author is stated in these files.
Retain all original bytes and history. The established primetest name gets
lazy/strict suffixes for material evaluation variants.

The input files provide decimal constants; Readme identifies 2^607-1 as its
principal Mersenne candidate. Smaller and composite candidates remain part of
the collection rather than treating probable-prime output as a general proof.

### Arithmetic, demand and translation

Keep arbitrary-precision candidates, exponents, powers, residues and base-65536
digits in IntInf. Preserve the source nested modular-power loop, including its
exponent-zero shortcut returning 1 without reduction, and the findKQ call at each
trial as written. Selected square counts fit signed 31-bit when converted to the
finite take counter. No fixed-width replacement is used for large arithmetic.

Reuse only the raw two-state generator engine shared with SCS. Initialize the
source states directly to 111/47; do not call SCS's seed mapping or interval
mapper. Explicit Word32 expresses the signed-32-bit Schrage transitions on every
host. Their corrected values stay in the source ranges. Raw result heads and
state transitions remain separately memoized, avoiding unused-head forcing.
Raw numbers become IntInf when used by the digit mapping, covering values that
do not fit a 31-bit SML int.

Retain chop, the source conditional uniform digit mapper and left-associated
makeNumber fold. Lazy accumulation is delayed; strict finite accumulation is
eager. The mapper is not replaced by System.Random, modulo n or a rejection
algorithm. Its zero-low-digit partiality is retained and tested; actual random
bounds n-2 are odd, so that partial case is outside the valid program path.
Fixed seeded witnesses do not establish independent-uniform sampling or transfer
a general statistical confidence claim to the benchmark.

The lazy variant memoizes finite digit/witness spines and heads. Its initial
1/-1 and secondary 1/-1 decisions stop before unused square tails. The strict
variant evaluates the selected finite square list and digit values eagerly,
including source-unused repeated squares. Infinite raw and square streams stay
lazy in both. splitAt retains shared prefix/tail projections; taking the tail
does not force discarded raw heads in lazy mode.

SML reads the selected input file as a finite string and decimal line list.
A final LF is removed as a line terminator while internal empty lines remain
invalid candidates. The selected parser accepts signed decimal integers and
surrounding whitespace, not the full Haskell Read grammar. The complete output
is assembled before returning, whereas the original prints labels incrementally.
Source labels have no separating newlines; preserve that exact result. Only the
suite's controlled report adds its normal line framing.

Each run resets the two seed states and constructs fresh stream cells instead
of retaining a top-level input-stream CAF across repeated suite invocations.
Within-run sharing and state advancement remain. File reading, result validation
and these initialization decisions are measured costs. Unused IntLib cube-root,
logarithm and display helpers are not translated; complete originals remain.

### Inputs, calibration and correctness

| Profile | Candidates | Trials |
|---|---|---:|
| smoke | second original FAST candidate, 74 bits | 100 |
| normal | original FAST candidates 2–4, including the composite | 100 |
| large | complete original five-candidate FAST input, including 607 bits | 100 |

The selected normal input contains 74/112/63-bit candidates. These source subsets
keep bounded routine/comparative work. Removing earlier candidates changes which
deterministic witnesses the remaining candidates see; original and independent
references are regenerated for the exact new sequence with unchanged seeds.
Large preserves the complete FAST sequence. Original NORM=60 and SLOW=300
candidate inputs remain documented and referenced but are not selected profiles.

Both policies' 607-bit single-candidate pilots hit the initial 600-second limit;
these are timeouts, not incorrect results. Smoke and the three-candidate normal
input validate at all 100 rounds under their recorded guards. Large retains the
default 3600-second/8-GiB allowance. Both policies validate the complete
original FAST input on Rune native code at O2, under profile limits and a
2-GiB RSS guard. All profiles keep 100 rounds and the original arithmetic.

GHC originals match every complete upstream fixture. A separate Python integer/
modular-power/generator model agrees on 380 original/small candidates, raw
prefixes and successor-state observations for the small and FAST sequences.
It also confirms the newly selected profiles. Eight exact power cases agree
between GHC and Python, including two nontrivial 607-bit moduli. Those finite
checks are separate from a proof of primality.

Auxiliary SML checks compare candidate outcomes and successor streams, scalar
powers, exact complete normal output, state reset, decimal parsing, factoring,
digit roundtrips and source partiality. Demand probes check unused square tails,
strict selected powers, unused split heads, prefix sharing and zero-length take.
The driver preserves empty-line semantics. All validation is exact, with no
floating tolerance.

### Compiler/runtime behavior and references

Investigate arbitrary-precision multiply/division, exponent loops, finite eager
squares, closure/list allocation, memoized raw state, data width and early exits.
Investigate Rune's portable IntInf limb/division implementation when explaining
large-case timeouts. A different arithmetic library is a different configuration,
not a port fix.
These are source-based diagnostic questions, not measured causal claims.
Comparisons use identical SML; original Haskell supplies correctness references.

[Rabin, Probabilistic algorithm for testing primality](https://doi.org/10.1016/0022-314X(80)90084-0)
provides algorithmic context; the preserved source specifies this particular
witness selection and control flow. [L'Ecuyer's combined-generator paper](https://doi.org/10.1145/62959.62969)
provides generator context, while the source credits its Haskell coding above.
[Partain](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17) supplies suite context.
The paper references are not correctness proofs of this SML translation.

### Algorithm and workload

Process decimal integer candidates with the source 100-round strong probable-prime

algorithm and inspect up to k repeated squares for its witness. Composite
witnesses stop the remaining trials early.

## pic-lazy

Finite evaluation: lazy.

### Algorithm and workload

Run the source electrostatic particle-in-cell application on a 16-by-16 toroidal
mesh for ten timesteps. Generate deterministic particle positions, accumulate
their charge at neighboring cells, compute potential and electric fields, push
particles and update the timestep. Repeated runs start with fresh particles.
The primary source consumes only the final timestep through formatting/hash.

### History, authorship, revision and variants

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, real/pic, all ten
Haskell modules and Makefile. Headers credit Patricia Fasel, Los Alamos National
Laboratory, August 1990. Pic.hs grants public copying/use provided its full
notice and authorship statements are reproduced. Preserve that complete notice
on the translated kernel and independent reference model, and retain all
original files. Data are generated internally; no external particle dataset is
introduced. Preserve the established pic name with explicit evaluation suffixes.

The directory also retains David E. Culler's 1987 Id code, Olaf Lubeck's Id
implementations and two call graphs. These have different array/accumulator
organization and interpolation code, and are not declared duplicates. The
[historical variant inventory](source-variants.tsv) records their individual dispositions,
authors, source hashes and missing dataflow/setup facilities. Their notices do
not automatically inherit Fasel's Haskell grant. No Id runtime feature is added.

### Source behavior retained

The ACTIVE fineMesh constructs constants: 3 at corners, 4 on horizontal edges,
5 on vertical edges and 6 inside. Its actual interpolation is commented out,
and it never forces the recursive coarse-mesh argument. Retain those constants.

potential calls vCycle rho phi, reversing the names of its first two arguments.
pushParticle returns acceleration/velocity maxima, while timeStep binds them
with swapped names; retain the resulting timestep formula. The top-edge
operator's row-high neighbor is n-2 rather than 1, except at corners. Positions
wrap only once by plus/minus 16. Initial potential uses depth three; timestep
depths cycle through zero, one and two. These are observed source definitions,
not corrections inferred from the physical model.

### Portable translation and evaluation

Immutable meshes use privately constructed SML arrays of memoized numeric cells;
writes stop when construction finishes. Association order, per-particle charge
update order and six-element neighbor LIST arguments remain. Array construction
adds complete/unique-write checks. Position and velocity remain separate finite
lists, with delayed tuple components and shared acceleration/velocity values.
Whole intermediate mesh computations and the coarse solve also remain delayed.

The lazy policy avoids the coarse computation discarded by fineMesh, unused
velocity lists during charge density, and terminal particle lists when only
the timestep is requested. The strict policy eagerly constructs finite cells/
lists and the positive-depth coarse dependency graph. Both retain the depth-zero
and timestep-zero guards before entering further recursion. Infinite recursion
from eager evaluation of an unselected branch is not introduced.

Use binary64 as the source Double requires. Preserve numerical operation order,
indexed stencils, scalar maximum order, truncation and square root. The real-based
genRand formula retains its integer truncate/divide/multiply stage. Selected
seeds stay below 16 and that stage stays below about 504 million, fitting signed
31-bit int; indices, depths and profile counters are also bounded. Explicit
Word64 implements the source 64-bit GHC hash wrapping on every SML host.

The driver reads arguments/reference once, validates each final timestep with
absolute bound 1e-12 plus relative bound 1e-10, and checks finite GEN17 rendering
and exact numerical roundtrip. SML formatting replaces GHC shortest formatting.
The source forward hash is consumed through an independent reverse polynomial
check of the same text; golden GHC/Python hash vectors also test it separately.
A stable particles:checked-runs report omits renderer-dependent hash values.
Numeric/reference I/O, complete hash checking and the added construction checks
are measured costs.

### Inputs, correctness and references

| Profile | Repeated simulations | Particles | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| smoke | 1 | 18 | FAST particle input, fewer repetitions |
| normal | 500 | 80 | unchanged NORM_OPTS |
| large | 1000 | 300 | unchanged SLOW_OPTS |

Original FAST=200/18 remains in Makefile and reference runs. The mesh, ten steps,
depth rules, input formulas and selected normal/large parameters are unchanged.
Default resource limits apply.

All unmodified GHC FAST/NORM/SLOW runs finish with their original empty stdout.
Export-only observers provide timestep prefixes zero through ten and complete
mesh/position/velocity states at particle counts 1,2,3,18,80,300. A separate Python
binary64 model agrees exactly on every recorded number. It uses the constant
fineMesh closed form instead of the unused multigrid dependency graph, providing
an independent calculation of the observable results.

Auxiliary full-state checks use absolute 1e-10 plus relative 1e-10. They add
terminal demand and are separate from the measured timestep-only consumer.
Tests cover every prefix, exact modular hashes, driver rendering, wrong numeric
fixtures, repeat reset, shape errors, source argument/stencil/statistics quirks
and unused coarse/velocity/terminal-list demand. These bounds validate source
results; no physical-accuracy guarantee is claimed.

[Hockney and Eastwood, Computer Simulation Using Particles](https://www.routledge.com/Computer-Simulation-Using-Particles/Eastwood-Hockney/p/book/9780852743928)
provides particle/grid and field-solve context. The pinned program defines the
specific computation checked here; the publication's model properties are not
transferred to its historical quirks. [Partain](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17)
supplies nofib context. The publisher description/contents and source form the
recorded review scope.

### Compiler/runtime diagnostic questions

Investigate persistent arrays, indexing, association lists, memoized payloads,
unused coarse work, finite eager construction, higher-order stencil callbacks,
short circuiting, numeric boxing and retained closures. Separate source analysis,
reference agreement and measured sensitivity. Identical SML is the compiler
comparison; Haskell and the independent model supply correctness references.

## hidden-lazy

Finite numeric evaluation: lazy.

### Algorithm and workload

Remove hidden portions of polygon edges, rotate the selected scene toward the
view direction, scale it onto the page and consume the resulting PostScript.
Preserve the original right-rotated polygon border order, support/heading edge
representation, pairwise overlap, clipping order and triangular visibility memo.

### History, authorship, revision and variants

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, real/hidden.
The retained December 1992 MAIL credits Stef Joosten's original Miranda program
and Mark Ramaer's Haskell translation and memoization. The correspondence
explicitly permits its inclusion in nofib; no broader separate license grant
is inferred. Original modules, Makefile, correspondence, prompts and all eight
scene files remain under hidden-lazy/upstream. Individual scene files state no
separate author or notice. MAIL describes four.plate as a composition of table,
horse, bookcase and houses. Other dataset origins are unstated.

The historical etc/nbpip.c is a pseudo-terminal/Ghostscript interaction wrapper,
not a second hidden-line algorithm. Its excluded support-program disposition,
identity and missing obsolete terminal setup are recorded in source-variants.tsv.
It is retained as provenance and is not linked into the portable benchmark.

The established hidden name is retained with explicit lazy/strict suffixes.
This program is distinct from the suite's other ray tracers and renderers.

### Portable translation and source behavior

All geometry, binary32 rounding, bounded scene parsing, rendering and checks are
SML97. Float arithmetic rounds after each primitive operation, including square
root. The selected computations use finite normal numbers or zero; the helper
does not claim general binary32 subnormal, overflow or transcendental support.
An independent eager binary32 model agrees exactly with GHC on every rotated
vertex and full visible edge in all three profiles. It records 34,715,488
operations, with no nonfinite or subnormal results.

Number's historical comparisons are unusual: equality uses abs(a-b)<epsilon,
while inequality uses abs(a-b)>epsilon. At exactly epsilon both are false.
Less-than and less-or-equal subtract epsilon on different operands; greater-than
and greater-or-equal derive from the source Ord comparison defaults. Preserve
these definitions, including min/max selection. Vector inequality instead
complements vector equality. Epsilon is binary32 word 953267991.

Vectors remain lists of numeric components. Dot products sum from zero in source
order. Keep rotation basis construction and repeated face normal calculations
at their source call sites. View zero or positive z leaves coordinates alone;
negative z negates every coordinate, as the source specifies.

Both policies retain lazy memoized control streams and lazy shared visibility
cells. Lazy numeric components avoid unused cross-product/rotation coordinates;
strict finite numeric construction evaluates them. The array of triangle cells
is freshly constructed inside each bottom-plate iteration, as written upstream.
Do not replace it with one global matrix. Reverse visibility queries retain
the source's cached-reverse test followed by an uncached forward calculation.

The driver retains 20 iterations for normal and large, with file reload, scene
parse and view parse on every iteration. Smoke reduces only repetitions to one.
Replace interactive prompts with explicit parameters and a stable checked-runs:
edge-count report. The parser handles the selected closed three-coordinate
plate grammar; it is not a general Haskell Read implementation.

PostScript keeps source path-continuity decisions using three-coordinate tolerant
vector equality, but prints only x/y. Primary checks compare every emitted x/y
binary32 word and every move/line/path-break command. They do not force an
otherwise irrelevant z coordinate just to validate output. Extra full-edge and
rotated-vertex checks are auxiliary observations.

GEN9 with a decimal minus sign replaces GHC's shortest Float formatting.
Every formatted value must round back to its exact binary32 word, including
signed zero. The full text is consumed by the source polynomial hash modulo
2^64, checked against an independent reverse polynomial calculation.
Golden text hash vectors are tested separately. Accepted results depend on the
coordinate/command oracle rather than compiler-specific decimal spellings.

### Profiles and correctness

| Profile | Original scene | Polygons | Repetitions | Visible edges per run |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Smoke | FAST houses.plate | 14 | 1 | 25 |
| Normal | NORM rad.plate | 51 | 20 | 130 |
| Large | SLOW four.plate | 119 | 20 | 238 |

All profiles use view 2,10,3 and their normal suite resource limits.
The unmodified GHC program runs 20 repetitions on every scene and matches empty
stdout plus its complete upstream stderr fixture. Export-only observers provide
full geometry and PostScript fixtures; the separate Python reference model
independently agrees on binary32 geometry. Command references are decoded from
the original PostScript with binary32 decimal roundtrip.

Primary geometry bounds are exact binary32 word equality, not a loose numerical
tolerance. The source's epsilon controls geometry rather than checker accuracy.
Tests exercise deliberately perturbed coordinates/topology, missing/extra output,
bad references, comparison boundary quirks, rotation special cases, border order,
memo sharing, finite numeric demand and unused z demand.

### Literature and diagnostic questions

[Joosten, The use of functional programming in software development (1989)](https://research.utwente.nl/en/publications/the-use-of-functional-programming-in-software-development/)
is the thesis identified by the original author correspondence. The university
bibliographic record confirms authorship, date and title; the thesis contents
have not been reviewed here.
[Partain's nofib paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17)
provides suite context.

Investigate list/vector representation, binary32 emulation, higher-order clipping,
short circuiting, memo construction versus cell forcing, unused coordinates and
numeric boxing. These are source-based questions, not measured optimization
claims. Compare the identical SML sources across compilers; Haskell supplies a
correctness reference.

Both policies retain lazy memoized control streams and lazy shared visibility
cells. Lazy numeric components avoid unused cross-product/rotation coordinates;
strict finite numeric construction evaluates them. The array of triangle cells
is freshly constructed inside each bottom-plate iteration, as written upstream.
Do not replace it with one global matrix. Reverse visibility queries retain
the source's cached-reverse test followed by an uncached forward calculation.

The driver retains 20 iterations for normal and large, with file reload, scene
parse and view parse on every iteration. Smoke reduces only repetitions to one.
Replace interactive prompts with explicit parameters and a stable checked-runs:
edge-count report. The parser handles the selected closed three-coordinate
plate grammar; it is not a general Haskell Read implementation.

PostScript keeps source path-continuity decisions using three-coordinate tolerant
vector equality, but prints only x/y. Primary checks compare every emitted x/y
binary32 word and every move/line/path-break command. They do not force an
otherwise irrelevant z coordinate just to validate output. Extra full-edge and
rotated-vertex checks are auxiliary observations.

GEN9 with a decimal minus sign replaces GHC's shortest Float formatting.
Every formatted value must round back to its exact binary32 word, including
signed zero. The full text is consumed by the source polynomial hash modulo
2^64, checked against an independent reverse polynomial calculation.
Golden text hash vectors are tested separately. Accepted results depend on the
coordinate/command oracle rather than compiler-specific decimal spellings.

### Profiles and correctness

| Profile | Original scene | Polygons | Repetitions | Visible edges per run |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Smoke | FAST houses.plate | 14 | 1 | 25 |
| Normal | NORM rad.plate | 51 | 20 | 130 |
| Large | SLOW four.plate | 119 | 20 | 238 |

All profiles use view 2,10,3 and their normal suite resource limits.
The unmodified GHC program runs 20 repetitions on every scene and matches empty
stdout plus its complete upstream stderr fixture. Export-only observers provide
full geometry and PostScript fixtures; the separate Python reference model
independently agrees on binary32 geometry. Command references are decoded from
the original PostScript with binary32 decimal roundtrip.

Primary geometry bounds are exact binary32 word equality, not a loose numerical
tolerance. The source's epsilon controls geometry rather than checker accuracy.
Tests exercise deliberately perturbed coordinates/topology, missing/extra output,
bad references, comparison boundary quirks, rotation special cases, border order,
memo sharing, finite numeric demand and unused z demand.

### Literature and diagnostic questions

[Joosten, The use of functional programming in software development (1989)](https://research.utwente.nl/en/publications/the-use-of-functional-programming-in-software-development/)
is the thesis identified by the original author correspondence. The university
bibliographic record confirms authorship, date and title; the thesis contents
have not been reviewed here.
[Partain's nofib paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17)
provides suite context.

Investigate list/vector representation, binary32 emulation, higher-order clipping,
short circuiting, memo construction versus cell forcing, unused coordinates and
numeric boxing. These are source-based questions, not measured optimization
claims. Compare the identical SML sources across compilers; Haskell supplies a
correctness reference.

[Hidden host-result evidence](validation/hidden-host-results.md) distinguishes
legacy nursery-sensitive failures from the constructor-field defect on all
three SML/NJ hosts. Failed correctness checks never provide accepted timings.

## prolog-lazy

Inference engine: explicit backtrack stack. Finite payload evaluation: lazy.

### Algorithm and workload

Parse a Mini Prolog command transcript, extend a sorted predicate database,
unify terms with an occurs check, enumerate query solutions, echo commands and
format answers. Consume and validate the complete interactive transcript through
a modular hash. Every repetition starts with the same immutable standard library.

### History, authorship, revision and variants

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, real/prolog.
Headers credit Mark P. Jones, November 1990. Examples describes an earlier
Orwell interpreter and the Haskell B version. Parse.hs credits Richard Bird's
Orwell parsing library; Interact.hs credits Bird and Wadler. README.nofib records
Will Partain's change from the illegal Haskell constructor operator :- to :==.
Retain all modules, original fixtures, standard library and historical notes
under prolog-lazy/upstream. No separate individual redistribution grant is
stated in those files; do not invent one. The examples and command data come
from the pinned application; no external Prolog corpus is introduced.

The active Engine.hs and excluded StackEngine.hs are byte-identical at the pin.
They share the prolog-lazy/prolog-strict implementation and retain both source
paths. PureEngine.hs is materially different: it builds and searches explicit
proof trees rather than an explicit stack, applies substitutions to remaining
goals at a different point, and has no cut predicate. Preserve it separately
as prolog-tree-lazy/prolog-tree-strict. Its answers for the supplied cut queries
differ from the active stack engine. They are checked against its own Haskell
implementation, not the stack fixtures. The supplementary source-variant
inventory records both relationships.

### Portable translation and evaluation

Keep the list-of-successes parser and all its alternative parse results,
first-success selection, term representation, function-valued substitutions,
composition order, occurs check and first-occurrence variable ordering.
Do not replace the interpreter with an association-map unifier or a different
Prolog engine. Predicate groups remain a sorted association list, keyed by
name rather than arity; clauses retain insertion order.

The stack engine retains explicit backtrack frames, fresh variable levels,
goal application order and the source cut operation, which clears the second
frame's alternatives while retaining the top frame. The proof-tree engine
retains memoized Done/Choice nodes and depth-first search. It does not acquire
the stack engine's cut behavior.

Both policies retain memoized parser alternatives, proof/search control streams
and output character streams. Lazy finite term payloads defer unused children
and substitution results; strict finite payloads construct them eagerly.
Potentially infinite search alternatives are not all forced by the strict
variant. Function-valued substitutions remain functions in both variants.
Difference-list output functions retain the source higher-order ShowS consumer.

Atoms use SML strings and selected input characters are ASCII. Runtime text is
converted to a shared character list once before the repetition loop. Parser
choice streams, terms, substitutions and database extensions are fresh for each
interpretation; the original immutable library/input are reused.

The bounded machine integers store source variable levels, positions and profile
counters; selected profiles fit signed 31-bit integers. Hash arithmetic uses
explicit Word64 modulo 2^64 on every host, matching the selected GHC 64-bit Int.
The driver checks every output character as it computes the forward hash, and
compares the result with an independent reverse polynomial calculation of the
reference transcript. It emits a stable repetition-count:hexadecimal-hash report.

The driver reads the library, input and reference once. Library clauses are
parsed once, as upstream. Remove the sign-on/library progress display from
accepted output, and replace the 200 printed decimal hash lines with the stable
report. The complete echoed/answer transcript being hashed is unchanged.
Retain backspace/delete handling, blank commands, syntax errors, continuation
semicolons, variable printing, database display and quit-tail demand.

The historical parser accepts some unusual empty names/queries and strips
literal spaces rather than arbitrary whitespace. Preserve and test those
behaviors. Command input exhausted without quit raises an error, matching the source's
partial reader under complete consumption. Selected source fixtures end in bye.

### Profiles and correctness

| Profile | Upstream command data | Repetitions |
|---|---|---:|
| Smoke | prolog.faststdin | 1 |
| Normal | prolog.stdin | 200 |
| Large | prolog.slowstdin | 200 |

The normal and large profiles retain their source iteration count and exact
command data. Smoke reduces only repetitions. All use the original standard
library and the suite's default resource limits.

Unmodified GHC runs match all three active-engine stdout fixtures exactly.
The proof-tree reference changes only the selected engine file, then uses its
own complete loop transcript. Export-only observers expose the original loop;
they add no alternate parser, unifier or printer.

All three complete transcripts agree for both SML payload policies and each
engine. Additional source-observed cases cover ambiguous parsing, empty
queries/names, backspaces, arity, aliases, numbered variables, clause order,
cut and quit-tail behavior. Tests cover substitution composition, cyclic
unification rejection, renaming, source cut-frame behavior, bad transcripts,
golden hash vectors and lazy/strict finite payload demand.

### Literature and diagnostic questions

[Bird and Wadler, An introduction to functional programming (1988)](https://www.research.ed.ac.uk/en/publications/an-introduction-to-functional-programming/)
supplies the bibliographic context for the credits in Parse.hs and Interact.hs.
The university record confirms author/title/year; the cited chapter contents
have not been reviewed here. The retained Examples document explains the two
specific inference engines.
[Partain's nofib paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17)
provides suite context.

Investigate parser branching and sharing, substitution closure chains,
higher-order printing, term allocation, retained backtrack frames, proof-tree
construction and early termination of alternative search. These questions
follow from source inspection. Reference agreement establishes selected
correctness; optimization/performance explanations require measurements.

## gamteb-lazy

Finite numeric evaluation: lazy.

### Algorithm and workload

Transport deterministic gamma-ray particles through the source carbon-cylinder
model. Select collisions and surfaces, apply photoelectric absorption, Compton
scattering and pair production, split particles or perform Russian roulette,
and accumulate escape/scatter/transit weights and twelve statistics.

### History, authorship, revision and variants

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, real/gamteb.
Headers credit Patricia Fasel, Los Alamos National Laboratory, August 1990.
GamtebMain.hs grants public copying/use provided the complete Regents of the
University of California 1990 notice and authorship statements are reproduced.
All derived physical modules, the driver and independent model retain it.
Data are generated by the program using the original 35-entry cross-section
tables and fixed initial energy 6; no external particle dataset is introduced.

Retain the established GAMTEB name with explicit lazy/strict suffixes.
All original Haskell modules, Makefile, stdout fixtures, historical LML/Id/
Fortran files and result documents remain under gamteb-lazy/upstream.

The supplementary source-variant inventory accounts for the historical programs
individually. Ordinary LML and its 0.97 traced variant have missing generated
interfaces and unspecified archived Float primitive semantics; their faithful
baseline needs a pinned runtime definition and reproducible fixtures. The
traced variant uses fixed 320 particles, explicit float operators and trace
threading. The Id version additionally needs its original dataflow-array setup
and approximates exp as 2.71828^x. These ports remain deferred with concrete
reconsideration conditions; no compiler/runtime prerequisite is added.

The three complete Fortran reference programs remain distinct additional
coverage candidates outside the initial SML/Haskell/OCaml executable import
set. They are excluded from the initial runnable suite, with source identities,
numeric/RNG/driver differences and individual 1986 notices retained. The older
gamo.f uses 100*scale particles and multiplicative mod-4194304 random numbers;
the other versions use one*scale, affine grand generation and recursive source
splitting. No exact-duplicate claim is made. The headers credit receipt of
Buck Thompson's original program in 1982, without identifying later modifiers.
The fixed factorial experiment, call graph and library symbol listing have
separate non-workload exclusions. Result documents are retained as provenance.

### Portable translation and source behavior

Use SML97 for physics, generation, checking and output. Preserve binary64 Double
operations, named scalar sharing, source branch guards, list order and balanced
source splitting. Both policies keep control/result/statistic streams memoized.
The lazy policy defers finite scalar/point payloads; the strict policy constructs
finite numeric payloads after source branch selection. Both share each transport
call's result/statistic pair rather than recomputing particle paths.

Preserve the source's numerical definitions and historical quirks:
cylLen2 is 30, despite its square comment; surface-distance ties select the
second candidate; the plane guard is independent of direction sign.
The isotropic formula does not normalize the resulting direction vector.
Its rsq>1 rejection branch contains a self-dependent seed binding; an invalid
seed 5.1 produces the original GHC loop exception. The translation retains
cyclic memo demand for that branch. Valid generated source seeds do not demand
it in the recorded profiles. Rotation's pole guard avoids unused divisions.
Zero or negative source counts still generate one particle in the kernel;
the public driver accepts positive profile counts.

The original real-valued random generator keeps its truncate/divide/multiply
remainder stage. Selected integer conversions stay far inside signed 31-bit
range, as recorded by the independent model. Constant tables remain shared
indexed collections; private arrays build accumulations in source association
order. Preserve raw result order and the source's raw output labels, which
call the particle type index and the energy bin type.

Consume raw results first, then accumulated statistics, then the 105-cell result
array. Retain the shared streams across those consumers. Only the first element
of each constant table appears in the output prefix. That prefix is a memoized
lazy constant, forced on its first consumer, as the source CAF requires.

GEN17 formatting replaces GHC's Double spelling. Every observed number is finite
and must roundtrip exactly, including zero sign, before its formatted output is
accepted. The full buffered text keeps the source field/table ordering and is
consumed by a Word64 polynomial hash modulo 2^64, checked by an independent
reverse polynomial. Buffering formatted pieces is an output allocation
adaptation. A stable repetitions:result-count report replaces 200 printed
compiler-dependent decimal hash values.

### Profiles and correctness

| Profile | Source particle count | Repetitions | Raw results per run |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Smoke | FAST 100 | 1 | 118 |
| Normal | NORM 1000 | 200 | 1231 |
| Large | SLOW 5000 | 200 | 5913 |

All profiles use source seed 0.5, energy 6, unchanged cross sections and the
suite's default limits. Smoke reduces only repetitions. Normal and large retain
their original iteration counts.

Unmodified GHC runs match all three complete stdout fixtures. Export-only
observers expose ordered raw results/statistics, output text and accumulated
arrays. A separate eager LIFO event-queue model agrees exactly on every raw
value for 1, 2, 3, 10, 100, 1000 and 5000 particles. Independent ordered sums also
match all twelve GHC statistics and all 105 array cells exactly.

Primary checks require exact result counts, particle kinds, energy bins and the
first ten integer-valued statistics. Raw/accumulated weights and the four table
values use absolute 1e-11 plus relative 1e-10 bounds; zero accumulations remain
exact. These are source-result error bounds. Expected numerical references
retain every raw result and full aggregates. Auxiliary checks additionally
observe raw statistic order and 46 source arithmetic cases.

Tests perturb every result/statistic/array position, check interior tolerance
acceptance, reject nonfinite and malformed references, validate modular hashes
and exercise terminal-field demand and seed sharing. Direct arithmetic
diagnostics use separately documented tighter bounds, and retain host failures
instead of altering source arithmetic or benchmark defaults.

[The host-result note](../validation/gamteb-host-results.md) distinguishes
nursery-sensitive corruption, decimal roundtrip failures, generic real tuples
inside references and ordinary mathematical approximation differences.

### Literature and diagnostic questions

[Burns et al., Vectorization on Monte Carlo particle transport: an architectural
study using the LANL benchmark GAMTEB (1989)](https://doi.org/10.1145/76263.76265)
studies vector implementations and data motion for the historical workload.
The author-uploaded abstract and bibliographic record were reviewed; the full
paper fetch timed out. This port follows the sequential Haskell implementation.
[Partain's nofib paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17)
provides functional-suite context.

Investigate floating-point boxing, shared scalar/point payloads, deferred terminal
coordinates, source-tree shape, paired result/statistic retention, concatenation,
array accumulation and output allocation. These are source-based diagnostic
questions. Reference agreement and measured counts are recorded separately;
the historical paper's vector speedups do not establish SML performance claims.

## gamteb-strict

Finite numeric evaluation: strict.

### Algorithm and workload

Transport deterministic gamma-ray particles through the source carbon-cylinder
model. Select collisions and surfaces, apply photoelectric absorption, Compton
scattering and pair production, split particles or perform Russian roulette,
and accumulate escape/scatter/transit weights and twelve statistics.

### History, authorship, revision and variants

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, real/gamteb.
Headers credit Patricia Fasel, Los Alamos National Laboratory, August 1990.
GamtebMain.hs grants public copying/use provided the complete Regents of the
University of California 1990 notice and authorship statements are reproduced.
All derived physical modules, the driver and independent model retain it.
Data are generated by the program using the original 35-entry cross-section
tables and fixed initial energy 6; no external particle dataset is introduced.

Retain the established GAMTEB name with explicit lazy/strict suffixes.
All original Haskell modules, Makefile, stdout fixtures, historical LML/Id/
Fortran files and result documents remain under gamteb-lazy/upstream.

The supplementary source-variant inventory accounts for the historical programs
individually. Ordinary LML and its 0.97 traced variant have missing generated
interfaces and unspecified archived Float primitive semantics; their faithful
baseline needs a pinned runtime definition and reproducible fixtures. The
traced variant uses fixed 320 particles, explicit float operators and trace
threading. The Id version additionally needs its original dataflow-array setup
and approximates exp as 2.71828^x. These ports remain deferred with concrete
reconsideration conditions; no compiler/runtime prerequisite is added.

The three complete Fortran reference programs remain distinct additional
coverage candidates outside the initial SML/Haskell/OCaml executable import
set. They are excluded from the initial runnable suite, with source identities,
numeric/RNG/driver differences and individual 1986 notices retained. The older
gamo.f uses 100*scale particles and multiplicative mod-4194304 random numbers;
the other versions use one*scale, affine grand generation and recursive source
splitting. No exact-duplicate claim is made. The headers credit receipt of
Buck Thompson's original program in 1982, without identifying later modifiers.
The fixed factorial experiment, call graph and library symbol listing have
separate non-workload exclusions. Result documents are retained as provenance.

### Portable translation and source behavior

Use SML97 for physics, generation, checking and output. Preserve binary64 Double
operations, named scalar sharing, source branch guards, list order and balanced
source splitting. Both policies keep control/result/statistic streams memoized.
The lazy policy defers finite scalar/point payloads; the strict policy constructs
finite numeric payloads after source branch selection. Both share each transport
call's result/statistic pair rather than recomputing particle paths.

Preserve the source's numerical definitions and historical quirks:
cylLen2 is 30, despite its square comment; surface-distance ties select the
second candidate; the plane guard is independent of direction sign.
The isotropic formula does not normalize the resulting direction vector.
Its rsq>1 rejection branch contains a self-dependent seed binding; an invalid
seed 5.1 produces the original GHC loop exception. The translation retains
cyclic memo demand for that branch. Valid generated source seeds do not demand
it in the recorded profiles. Rotation's pole guard avoids unused divisions.
Zero or negative source counts still generate one particle in the kernel;
the public driver accepts positive profile counts.

The original real-valued random generator keeps its truncate/divide/multiply
remainder stage. Selected integer conversions stay far inside signed 31-bit
range, as recorded by the independent model. Constant tables remain shared
indexed collections; private arrays build accumulations in source association
order. Preserve raw result order and the source's raw output labels, which
call the particle type index and the energy bin type.

Consume raw results first, then accumulated statistics, then the 105-cell result
array. Retain the shared streams across those consumers. Only the first element
of each constant table appears in the output prefix. That prefix is a memoized
lazy constant, forced on its first consumer, as the source CAF requires.

GEN17 formatting replaces GHC's Double spelling. Every observed number is finite
and must roundtrip exactly, including zero sign, before its formatted output is
accepted. The full buffered text keeps the source field/table ordering and is
consumed by a Word64 polynomial hash modulo 2^64, checked by an independent
reverse polynomial. Buffering formatted pieces is an output allocation
adaptation. A stable repetitions:result-count report replaces 200 printed
compiler-dependent decimal hash values.

## mkhprog-lazy

Finite text evaluation: lazy.

### Algorithm and workload

Generate a Haskell command-line parser skeleton from flag/type specifications.
Validate flags and duplicates, build default arguments, usage text and data
declarations, and emit parser clauses and auxiliary readers through a
continuation-passing writer. Consume each emitted block separately, as upstream.

### History, authorship, revision and aliases

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, real/mkhprog.
The literate title and author declaration identify N. D. North, National
Physical Laboratory, version 2.4 dated June 23, 1992. Preserve Crown Copyright
1992 on the translation, templates and driver, and retain Main.lhs, the
mkhprog.1 manual and bundled input. No separate redistribution grant is stated
in the individual source; do not invent one.

The manual identifies an earlier C mkprog with related functionality and
manual text, while explicitly calling the implementation different. Its source
is not supplied, so no duplicate implementation is claimed. Keep the established mkhprog name with lazy/strict
suffixes. The input specification comes from the pinned nofib file; its
individual author is unstated.

The generated program is a historical skeleton: System imports, deriving ()
and unresolved ?? defaults remain unchanged. Validation concerns generated
text; it does not require compiling or modernizing that skeleton.

### Portable translation and evaluation

Retain continuation composition, environment lookup, flag order, case-sensitive
duplicate checks and per-block emission. The output is a persistent character
list whose spine uses the selected memoized-lazy or eager finite policy.
String append and concatenation preserve the source expression order.
Four fixed auxiliary templates remain shared.

Literal type comparisons inspect characters only until a mismatch, matching
the source list patterns. They do not flatten the whole type before choosing
a default or reader. The lazy policy leaves unused later text unforced; the
strict policy materializes finite text during construction. Both policies
propagate an output consumer's early stop without continuing emission.
Callbacks preserve the source continuation order and output channels.

Normalize input once using the source words/unlines boundary, then rebuild
the parser/generator work for each repetition. The original GHC allocation
diagnostics grow from about 3.06 MB at one repetition to 10.81 GB at 3800 and
51.22 GB at 18000. These observations support repeated work; the port does
not memoize a complete generated program or its hashes across iterations.
Allocation diagnostics are separate from performance timing claims.

Selected input characters are ASCII. Input tokenization uses portable SML
strings; generated text retains explicit character-list structure. Integer
argument indices and profile counters fit signed 31-bit integers. Explicit
Word64 arithmetic supplies the original GHC 64-bit Int hash wrapping on every
host, regardless of default int size.

The original stdout consumer hashes each writeln/newline block independently
and discards that hash. The driver compares every block with a reviewed
original hash in order, enforces the block count and returns a stable
repetitions:blocks:hexadecimal-sum report. Its final sum wraps modulo 2^64.
It does not replace the source workload with one whole-program hash.

Timed profiles select hashed stdout. Auxiliary captures also retain named-file
channel selection, module changes and literate output. The benchmark driver
accepts the stdout profile contract; named-file content is observed through
the auxiliary capture adapter. Actual append-file timing is not selected.

### Profiles and correctness

| Profile | Source input | Repetitions | Blocks per iteration |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Smoke | bundled 41-flag specification | 1 | 62 |
| Normal | bundled specification | NORM 3800 | 62 |
| Large | bundled specification | SLOW 18000 | 62 |

The fixed specification and its type/flag distribution remain unchanged.
Smoke reduces the original FAST repetition count of 350 to one. Normal and
large retain the source counts, with the suite's default resource limits.

Unmodified GHC runs at 1, 10, 350, 3800 and 18000 repetitions complete with
empty stdout. A consumer-only observer forces the original hash and records
the emitted text and channel. It changes no parser or generator algorithm.
Every full output, block hash and channel agrees for both SML policies across
nine cases: the default specification, auxiliary templates, empty input, integer,
Boolean/toggle, string, literate, inline module and named-file cases.
The default program has 62 blocks and 18794 characters.

Seven invalid specifications match the unmodified program's exact usage text.
Tests cover output ordering, missing/extra/corrupted block references, hash
width, normalization, repetitions, source reader choices, early output stop,
finite text demand, shared consumers and a mismatching type with an undefined
tail. Full output fixtures retain all original spaces and backslashes.

### Literature and diagnostic questions

The retained [literate source](../mkhprog-lazy/upstream/Main.lhs) is also North's
program description, with an annex explaining the continuation style and its
historical compiler context. The [manual](../mkhprog-lazy/upstream/mkhprog.1)
describes the flag interface. These program-specific documents were reviewed.
[Partain's nofib paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17)
provides suite context.

Investigate higher-order continuation specialization, character-list construction,
string sharing, append shape, literal pattern demand, closure lifetimes and
per-block hash consumption. Treat these source-based questions separately from
recorded allocation/count observations and eventual timing reports.

## gg-lazy

Graph mode: activity. Finite numeric evaluation: lazy.

### Algorithm and workload

Parse supplied GRIP runtime logs, collect processor metadata and timing records,
insert records in bucket order, gather activity or spark counters and generate
PostScript graphs. The activity, spark-activity and spark-pool algorithms have
separate benchmark names; each has lazy and strict finite numeric policies.

### History, authorship, revision and variants

nofib b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, real/gg.
The gg.1 manual, dated August 13, 1992, explicitly credits Iain Checkland,
University of York. Retain all nine original modules, manual, report templates,
input/output fixtures, example files and orchestration scripts under gg-lazy/
upstream. No separate individual redistribution notice is stated in these files;
do not infer a grant from another benchmark.

The source report script invokes three computations: -A activity, -S spark
activity and -P spark pool. The scripts in the root and example directories are
byte-identical. Their supplementary exclusions identify report orchestration,
LaTeX/dvips dependencies and temporary-file removal, while the three actual
graph computations are imported separately. The old scripts are retained as
provenance and are not used as suite adapters.

GRIP itself is a parallel graph-reduction machine, but gg is a sequential
postprocessor of existing data. The benchmark neither runs a parallel program
nor requires a GRIP runtime. Supplied traces have no separate dataset authorship
or notice; processor names/times remain unchanged.

The extra gg.stdin-2.Z is a compressed historical trace. Preserve its pinned
compressed identity and a decoded auxiliary fixture. The recorded gzip -cd
adaptation yields 133193 bytes, independently checked against all three source
graph modes. The compressed file is an explicitly reviewed source-data exception
to executable-artifact scans, never a generic binary exemption.

### Portable translation and evaluation

Use SML97 for parsing, insertion, accumulation, plotting, validation and hashing.
Input character lists are read once, then parsed for each interpretation.
Preserve the positional-power strToInt definition, source line splitting,
list insertion rather than a replacement sort, record equality/order behavior,
grouping and recursive outline transposition.

All source counters use explicit IntInf payloads; the recorded profiles stay
within the source integer range. This removes dependence on a host's default
int width without introducing modular changes. Lazy payloads defer unused
numeric fields; strict finite payloads evaluate them. Control streams and the
paired trace/final-state results remain memoized in both policies.

Retain the source's structural equality check before its bucket-order test.
Equal buckets retain insertion order. Activity/spark gathering retains zero
buckets and the source closing sample. Pool accumulation preserves its distinct
bucket sharing, post-update levels and final closing trace. Outline conversion
uses the original recursive transposition and zip structure.

Default filters do not inspect an ignored processor value. Constant PostScript
prefixes, boxes and title can be produced before unrelated input. Processor
configuration, axes, legend percentages and curves retain their source demand
order. The final aggregate is shared with trace generation rather than recomputed.

Percentage and tick labels use the source Float32 arithmetic and custom
printFloat function. Bare scale/moveto operands and centimetre conversion use
the source's defaulted Double arithmetic. Record those widths separately.
The finite binary32 helper handles the selected label domain; it is not a
general floating-point library.

Preserve historical source behavior instead of repairing graphs. FAST and NORM
have only one processor-header entry, so length(pes)-1 is zero and activity
scaling emits positive Infinity. The reference category is checked explicitly.
The larger supplementary trace also exposes the source's finite configuration
position list, which omits a final processor label at sixteen entries.
Those are documented source results.

GEN17 replaces GHC shortest Double spelling only for bare numeric operands.
All commands, literal text, colors, integer coordinates, labels, ordering and
line endings must match exactly. Integer operands remain exact; finite Double
operands use absolute 1e-12 plus relative 1e-12 bounds. Nonfinite operands must
match class and sign. Numeric comparison does not permit whitespace changes.

A streaming checker buffers one line, validates it and combines independently
computed per-line reverse polynomial hashes. The actual character stream also
computes the source forward Word64 hash; both whole-output hashes must agree.
Modified numeric spellings are checked before their actual line hash is used.
The driver emits stable repetitions:checked-lines output instead of source
compiler-dependent decimal hash lines.

### Profiles and correctness

| Profile | Original trace | Repetitions |
|---|---|---:|
| Smoke | gg.faststdin | 1 |
| Normal | gg.stdin | 500 |
| Large | gg.slowstdin | 1500 |

Smoke reduces FAST's 150 repetitions to one. Normal and large retain their source
counts. Each mode uses its own original PostScript reference and the suite's
default resource limits. Landscape is the comparative profile; portrait and
encapsulated output are auxiliary correctness cases.

Unmodified GHC runs match every stdout/stderr fixture. Export-only observers
supply sorted records, parameters and complete output for three graph modes,
portrait, EPS and selected-processor cases. Thirty complete SML outputs agree
under both policies across the three standard traces and five formats, allowing
only equivalent bare numeric operand spelling.

Tests compare all ordered records and full outputs, validate the decoded
supplementary trace, reject modified commands/points/colors/text/line counts/
numeric operands/nonfinite categories, exercise source rounding/scaling quirks,
and verify paired-state sharing and demand. Whole normal profiles are calibrated
under both payload policies. Full SML large repetition validation is recorded
separately when run.

[The host-result note](../validation/gg-host-results.md) retains the reduced
SML/NJ Word64 checker discrepancy. Valid source/checker code and canonical host
settings remain; failing configurations cannot supply accepted timing results.

### Literature and diagnostic questions

The retained [manual](../gg-lazy/upstream/gg.1) documents the interface and modes.
The report templates and README identify the historical application.
[Peyton Jones, Clack, Salkild and Hardie, GRIP: a high-performance architecture
for parallel graph reduction (1987)](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/grip-a-high-performance-architecture-for-parallel-graph-reduction/)
provides machine context. Its abstract and introduction were reviewed; it
describes the parallel machine, not this sequential SML postprocessor.
[Partain's nofib paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17)
provides suite context.

Investigate delayed numeric parsing, insertion shape, selected-field forcing,
state/trace retention, outline transposition, Float32 versus Double operations
and streaming text/hash consumers. These are source-based questions. Reference
agreement and measured configurations are separate from architectural hypotheses.

supply sorted records, parameters and complete output for three graph modes,
portrait, EPS and selected-processor cases. Thirty complete SML outputs agree
under both policies across the three standard traces and five formats, allowing
only equivalent bare numeric operand spelling.
