supplementary trace, reject modified commands/points/colors/text/line counts/
numeric operands/nonfinite categories, exercise source rounding/scaling quirks,
and verify paired-state sharing and demand. Whole normal profiles are calibrated
under both payload policies. Full SML large repetition validation is recorded
separately when run.

SML/NJ Word64 checker discrepancy. Valid source/checker code and canonical host
settings remain; failing configurations cannot supply accepted timing results.

the source's defaulted Double arithmetic. Record those widths separately.

have only one processor-header entry, so length(pes)-1 is zero and activity

match class and sign. Numeric comparison does not permit whitespace changes.

computed per-line reverse polynomial hashes. The actual character stream also
computes the source forward Word64 hash; both whole-output hashes must agree.
Modified numeric spellings are checked before their actual line hash is used.
The driver emits stable repetitions:checked-lines output instead of source
compiler-dependent decimal hash lines.

## fft2-lazy

Numeric policy: lazy.

### Algorithm and workload

Compute fast FFT/inverse distance, general mixed-factor DFT/inverse distance
and the sum of a slow cosine transform over independent ramps. Retain list
algorithms, cyclic roots, the factor sieve, transpose/zip structure, numeric
operation order and separate signal generation for the three measurements.
No result cache or replacement transform is used in the benchmark.

### History, authorship and variants

Rex Page, Amoco Production Research, September 1992. Pinned nofib revision
b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, spectral/fft2. Retain fft2 as distinct
from classic FFT, spectral/hartel/fft and Sandmark FFT, with explicit lazy/strict
suffixes. Complete original modules, MAIL, README.nofib, old platform fixtures
and foreign-language references are retained under fft2-lazy/upstream.

Individual files state no separate redistribution grant; retain all attribution
and do not infer a license from another benchmark. The supplementary inventory
records Rex Page's Miranda and fixed-array Fortran programs as distinct
historical references outside the initial executable language-family set.
Matt Donadio's iterative bit-reversal C FFT is a library fragment without a
standalone workload. No foreign reference is called an exact duplicate.
There are no external datasets; ramp inputs are generated deterministically.
Old platform-specific numeric fixtures remain historical evidence.

### Portable translation and evaluation

All computation and checking uses SML97. Complex coordinates use real arithmetic,
with memoized numeric delays in lazy and eager finite payloads in strict.
Both preserve memoized control streams, shared even-root subsequences, periodic
cyclic lists, the global prime stream and separately delayed transform metrics.
Unused complex coordinates remain demand-sensitive in the lazy policy.

Magnitude/division retain the installed GHC base-4.17.2.0 Data.Complex exponent
scaling and zero-exponent behavior, inspected in its installed interface.
Extreme-value references include the underflow of a tiny coordinate paired with
zero. Integer indices and factors fit portable int in the bounded profile domain.
Floating enumeration retains Haskell's half-step endpoint convention.

For i from one through 100, the source generates base+i/15 and consequently
eight different lengths. Compute each iteration anew. The fast transform assumes
powers of two but source profiles include other lengths: preserve and check its
large nonzero errors instead of silently correcting the source algorithm.

Retain the demand for the length of the quoted result string. GEN17 replaces
shortest decimal spelling; parsed values, escape roundtrips and an independently
computed escaped length validate the consumer. Stable samples:checked output
replaces empty stdout. No hash replaces the formatted-result consumer.

### Profiles and result checks

| Profile | Samples | Base |
|---|---:|---:|
| Smoke | 1 | 70 |
| Normal | 100 | 245 |
| Large | 100 | 490 |

Normal and large retain source counts; smoke reduces FAST's 100 to one.
Original GHC runs match the empty stdout fixture for all full profiles; print
mode supplies all 300 numeric values per profile. An independent eager Python
model agrees on all 300 triples, including non-power-of-two fast-transform errors.
Its reference-only caching of repeated sizes is absent from the SML workload.

For actual length n, fast-transform distance allows absolute 1e-9 plus relative
1e-10. The general-transform residual allows absolute 128*epsilon*n^2*sqrt(n);
the cosine sum allows 128*epsilon*n^3, with binary64 machine epsilon.
These are conservative source-agreement budgets, not a formal proof for all math
libraries. Reject nonfinite values, malformed triples and deliberate perturbations
of each metric; also test an accepted interior point near the bound.
Auxiliary transform vectors use absolute and relative 1e-11.

The semantic target checks all five complex transforms and cosine vectors at
lengths 2,3,4,5,8,16, magnitudes, cyclic lists, factors, floating enumeration,
quoted output, coordinate demand and sharing. Both full normal SML profiles
pass calibration. Full large SML repetition checks remain unrecorded, separately
from validated large fixtures and first-sample checks.

Private Rune, MLton, Poly/ML and ML Kit runs pass 132 checks. Private SML/NJ
runs terminate with bus/segmentation faults or a fatal bogus-overflow diagnostic.
Retain valid source and canonical host settings; the compiler mechanism is
unresolved. Failed correctness checks cannot supply accepted timing samples.
Canonical primary, count and semantic results are recorded as they finish.

### Literature and diagnostic questions

[Cooley and Tukey (1965)](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0025-5718-1965-0178586-1)
provides FFT context; this source's Fourier.lhs and Complex_Vectors.lhs define
the actual algorithms and MAIL records numerical investigations.
[Partain's nofib paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17) supplies suite
context. Investigate higher-order streams, periodic sharing, complex-coordinate
demand, numeric operation order, transform assumptions and formatting cost.
These are source-based hypotheses until supported by measurements.

## fft2-strict

Numeric policy: strict.

### Algorithm and workload

Compute fast FFT/inverse distance, general mixed-factor DFT/inverse distance
and the sum of a slow cosine transform over independent ramps. Retain list
algorithms, cyclic roots, the factor sieve, transpose/zip structure, numeric
operation order and separate signal generation for the three measurements.
No result cache or replacement transform is used in the benchmark.

### History, authorship and variants

Rex Page, Amoco Production Research, September 1992. Pinned nofib revision
b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, spectral/fft2. Retain fft2 as distinct
from classic FFT, spectral/hartel/fft and Sandmark FFT, with explicit lazy/strict
suffixes. Complete original modules, MAIL, README.nofib, old platform fixtures
and foreign-language references are retained under fft2-lazy/upstream.

Individual files state no separate redistribution grant; retain all attribution
and do not infer a license from another benchmark. The supplementary inventory
records Rex Page's Miranda and fixed-array Fortran programs as distinct
historical references outside the initial executable language-family set.
Matt Donadio's iterative bit-reversal C FFT is a library fragment without a
standalone workload. No foreign reference is called an exact duplicate.
There are no external datasets; ramp inputs are generated deterministically.
Old platform-specific numeric fixtures remain historical evidence.

### Portable translation and evaluation

All computation and checking uses SML97. Complex coordinates use real arithmetic,
with memoized numeric delays in lazy and eager finite payloads in strict.
Both preserve memoized control streams, shared even-root subsequences, periodic
cyclic lists, the global prime stream and separately delayed transform metrics.
Unused complex coordinates remain demand-sensitive in the lazy policy.

Magnitude/division retain the installed GHC base-4.17.2.0 Data.Complex exponent
scaling and zero-exponent behavior, inspected in its installed interface.
Extreme-value references include the underflow of a tiny coordinate paired with
zero. Integer indices and factors fit portable int in the bounded profile domain.
Floating enumeration retains Haskell's half-step endpoint convention.

For i from one through 100, the source generates base+i/15 and consequently
eight different lengths. Compute each iteration anew. The fast transform assumes
powers of two but source profiles include other lengths: preserve and check its
large nonzero errors instead of silently correcting the source algorithm.

Retain the demand for the length of the quoted result string. GEN17 replaces
shortest decimal spelling; parsed values, escape roundtrips and an independently
computed escaped length validate the consumer. Stable samples:checked output
replaces empty stdout. No hash replaces the formatted-result consumer.

## lambda-simple-lazy

Interpreter: simple. Numeric/syntax policy: lazy.

### Algorithm and workload

Evaluate a lambda-calculus program that sums zero through n using an explicit
fixed-point combinator, closures, variable lookup, integer addition and a
zero conditional. Compare a directly recursive interpreter with a state-monadic
interpreter. Preserve both implementations and their original environments,
call-by-name argument closures, association-list lookup and pretty printers.

### History, authorship and variants

The source says From Mark: marku@cs.waikato.ac.nz, November 2001; no surname
is inferred from the address. Pinned nofib revision
b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, spectral/lambda. Individual source
and generated fixture files state no separate redistribution notice. Retain
their complete attribution and historical observations under
lambda-simple-lazy/upstream; do not infer a grant from another benchmark.

Original main runs direct and monadic evaluation, each 100 times, interleaving
their output. The suite splits the styles into separately named simple and monad
workloads so each comparison measures one implementation. Each retains its
individual source repetition count. Explicit lazy/strict variants retain
materially different finite syntax/result evaluation and allocation behavior.
No external datasets are required; all selected syntax is source-generated.

The source's historical timing comments concern old Hugs/GHC implementations.
They explain the comparison's motivation and are not measurements of Rune.

### Translation and runtime behavior

Kernel, generators, consumers and checks use SML97. The lazy policy memoizes
term fields, numeric payloads, closure environments and delayed results.
The strict policy evaluates finite payloads eagerly. Both retain the interpreted
language's explicit call-by-name closures: a strict host policy does not turn the
interpreted program into call-by-value or memoize interpreted variable results.

Translate erased Identity directly and keep the direct interpreter's recursive
calls. The other interpreter retains explicit state computations, return/bind,
lookup, current environment, push and withEnv. withEnv evaluates a computation
in a supplied environment while returning the caller's environment; its result
can remain delayed. The source Incr is intentionally a no-op returning zero.

Preserve the fixed-point and partial-sum syntax as shared global source terms.
Construct each selected application anew per repetition. No result cache,
algebraic replacement of evaluation or source transformation eliminates the
interpreted recursion. Indices and source Int arithmetic fit even 31-bit signed
ints for selected sizes; the driver bounds n at 20000 to keep the independent
triangular-number checker portable.

Retain the source direct Con output and monadic pretty-printed value plus final
environment, including its two spaces and trailing newline. Selected source
terms always return Con; the direct derived-Show adapter documents that bounded
domain instead of pretending to implement every unused Read/Show operation.
Full text equality consumes and validates every selected result. Stable
repetitions:checked-characters output replaces repetitive stdout.

### Inputs and correctness

| Profile | Repetitions of each selected style | Summation bound |
|---|---:|---:|
| Smoke | 1 | 80 |
| Normal | 100 | 260 |
| Large | 100 | 550 |

Smoke reduces source FAST's 100 repetitions to one; normal/large retain their
upstream bounds and counts. Independent n*(n+1)/2 arithmetic checks every result,
while the original GHC program reproduces all three complete 200-line fixtures.

An export-only original observer checks 33 term/environment cases: arithmetic,
zero branches, nonnumeric tests, unused arguments, shadowing, captured lexical
environments, explicit Thunk environments, fixed-point recursion and caller
state restoration. The 241-check target additionally covers independent sums,
formatting/brackets, invalid applications, modified output, zero repetitions,
syntax-field demand and sharing.

All six native hosts and Rune pass the private semantic target. Final canonical
matrices/counts are recorded with the import wave. Full normal calibration
covers both styles and both policies; large fixtures are checked independently,
while full SML large repetition runs remain unrecorded. No failing correctness
case can supply accepted measurements.

### Literature and diagnostic questions

The retained source gives the direct-versus-state-monadic experiment and
historical observations. [Partain's nofib paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17)
supplies suite context. Investigate closure allocation, environment traversal,
higher-order state composition, restored lexical scope, evaluation/sharing and
pretty-print consumers. These questions follow source inspection; host-specific
performance conclusions require measurements of the selected implementation.

## para-lazy

Finite numeric policy: lazy.

### Algorithm and workload

Format paragraphs at maximum width 70 and preferred width 63 using the source
linear-time par3. Retain right-fold scan1, candidate cost/width/length summaries,
symmetric lists as two lists, both rebalance operations, add/breakpoint pruning,
drop_nofit, trim, tile and source parse/unparse. The implementation does not
replace candidate maintenance with dynamic programming or a mutable queue.

### History, authorship and known variants

Oege de Moor and Jeremy Gibbons, 1995--1999; the article header dates its benchmark
program September 1999. Pinned nofib revision
b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, spectral/para. This is paragraph
formatting, with no parallel runtime requirement.

The literate source contains its paper, experiments and intermediate algorithms:
exhaustive par0, quadratic par1, cached/pruned par1'/par2 forms, final linear par3
and greedy parg. Original main selects par3. Preserve all definitions as upstream
source; quadratic par1 is an independent original-language reference for a
documented counterexample, not a substituted timed algorithm. No separate
redistribution grant is stated in the Haskell/C++ sources.

The C++ Part2.C comparison has its own bounded buffers, command-line width and
Para/Queue/Thin modules. It remains a distinct future candidate outside the
initial SML/Haskell/OCaml executable set. Retain its source and data; omit the
pinned precompiled i386 part2 executable and record its SHA-256/disposition.
No original executable is imported or executed. The complete article warns
against treating its clarity-first historical comparison as modern performance
evidence.

### Dataset origins and notices

The full input is the supplied Project Gutenberg February 1994 e-text #107,
Far From the Madding Crowd by Thomas Hardy, named crowd10a.txt in its header.
Its individual historical notice includes Charles B. Kramer's Small Print
version 04.29.93, the public-domain statement and distribution terms.
Retain the entire original text/header/notice byte-for-byte in full.input and
upstream/runtime_files/input-data. Preserve the separate CRLF C++ crowd/cout
copies unchanged; do not silently equate their raw identities.

Formatted references retain all original words, including the complete historical
header/notice, with only the benchmark's line wrapping and blank-line formatting.
The original ASCII file is supplied alongside them. Smoke selects complete
novel-body paragraphs after the historical header, with no Gutenberg references;
its exact byte range, source identity and adaptation are recorded. Synthetic
auxiliary cases have deterministic origins. The novel-body counterexample keeps
its original author/source attribution here.

### SML97 translation and evaluation

Lazy and strict names identify memoized versus eager finite numeric summaries
and state/candidate payloads. Both retain memoized list spines, head sharing,
queue shape, scanning order, candidate selection and source right-fold grouping.
The lazy policy can inspect a candidate length without forcing unrelated fields.
No input, formatted output or parsed paragraph is cached across repetitions.

The driver reopens the input each iteration. Portable TextIO.inputAll replaces
hGetContents and produces a memoized character stream; record this eager file
read separately from the source's lazy file IO. Reading fixed ASCII data keeps
word/character classification within the reviewed common domain.
All selected integer widths, costs and lengths fit signed 31-bit int; no
arbitrary-precision or modular-arithmetic substitution is introduced.

The original consumes length of the formatted string and prints nothing. The
driver consumes the same output stream while comparing every character against
the reviewed fixture, then reports repetitions:checked-characters. It buffers
neither an extra full output list nor a parsed-result cache. This validation adds
character comparison to the source length consumer; document it in comparisons.

### Profiles and correctness

| Profile | Repetitions | Text |
|---|---:|---|
| Smoke | 1 | 10005-byte complete body-paragraph selection |
| Normal | 8 | original 789112-byte text |
| Large | 40 | original 789112-byte text |

Normal/large retain source inputs and counts. Smoke keeps FAST's one repetition
and reduces its dataset for bounded routine checks. Original GHC runs finish
all source profiles with empty stdout; there is no supplied para.stdout fixture.
An export-only original formatter produces complete reviewed formatted text:
784213 bytes for the original input and 9969 bytes for smoke.

An independent quadratic dynamic-programming reference verifies preserved word
order, maximum widths and layout costs for all 3574 original paragraphs.
Source costs agree with the optimum on 3573. Paragraph 483, a 23-word quotation,
has source par3 cost 5 versus optimum 1. Original quadratic par1 confirms cost 1.
Preserve par3's three-line layout exactly; this is an established property of
the pinned source, not evidence against the paper's general algorithm.
Partial source behavior on whitespace-only input and overlong words is retained.

The 112-check target compares 41 complete original cases under both policies,
small full text, the source counterexample, output corruption/length rejection,
zero iterations, front/back queue rebalancing and unused-field demand.
Both policies agree with the complete original text in a guarded streaming
pilot. Full normal calibration and canonical primary/count/semantic runs are
recorded separately as they finish. Full large SML repetition checks remain
unrecorded. An earlier development consumer materialized an extra full output
list and exceeded a private 1-GiB guard; retain that development observation
separately from the final streaming consumer's checks.

### Literature and diagnostic questions

[De Moor and Gibbons, Bridging the Algorithm Gap: A Linear-Time Functional
Program for Paragraph Formatting (1999)](https://www.cs.ox.ac.uk/publications/publication2361-abstract.html)
is the source article; the full literate text is preserved. It motivates the
functional derivation and concrete queue representation.
[Partain's nofib paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17) supplies suite
context. Investigate summary-field demand, symmetric-list sharing/rebalancing,
candidate pruning, paragraph lifetimes, text parsing and output consumption.
These are source-based diagnostic questions; current-host performance claims
need separate measurements.

program September 1999. Pinned nofib revision
b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, spectral/para. This is paragraph
formatting, with no parallel runtime requirement.

The literate source contains its paper, experiments and intermediate algorithms:
exhaustive par0, quadratic par1, cached/pruned par1'/par2 forms, final linear par3
and greedy parg. Original main selects par3. Preserve all definitions as upstream
source; quadratic par1 is an independent original-language reference for a
documented counterexample, not a substituted timed algorithm. No separate
redistribution grant is stated in the Haskell/C++ sources.

The C++ Part2.C comparison has its own bounded buffers, command-line width and
Para/Queue/Thin modules. It remains a distinct future candidate outside the
initial SML/Haskell/OCaml executable set. Retain its source and data; omit the
pinned precompiled i386 part2 executable and record its SHA-256/disposition.
No original executable is imported or executed. The complete article warns
against treating its clarity-first historical comparison as modern performance
evidence.

### Dataset origins and notices

The full input is the supplied Project Gutenberg February 1994 e-text #107,
Far From the Madding Crowd by Thomas Hardy, named crowd10a.txt in its header.
Its individual historical notice includes Charles B. Kramer's Small Print
version 04.29.93, the public-domain statement and distribution terms.
Retain the entire original text/header/notice byte-for-byte in full.input and
upstream/runtime_files/input-data. Preserve the separate CRLF C++ crowd/cout
copies unchanged; do not silently equate their raw identities.

Formatted references retain all original words, including the complete historical
header/notice, with only the benchmark's line wrapping and blank-line formatting.
The original ASCII file is supplied alongside them. Smoke selects complete
novel-body paragraphs after the historical header, with no Gutenberg references;
its exact byte range, source identity and adaptation are recorded. Synthetic
auxiliary cases have deterministic origins. The novel-body counterexample keeps
its original author/source attribution here.

### SML97 translation and evaluation

Lazy and strict names identify memoized versus eager finite numeric summaries
and state/candidate payloads. Both retain memoized list spines, head sharing,
queue shape, scanning order, candidate selection and source right-fold grouping.
The lazy policy can inspect a candidate length without forcing unrelated fields.
No input, formatted output or parsed paragraph is cached across repetitions.

The driver reopens the input each iteration. Portable TextIO.inputAll replaces
hGetContents and produces a memoized character stream; record this eager file
read separately from the source's lazy file IO. Reading fixed ASCII data keeps
word/character classification within the reviewed common domain.
All selected integer widths, costs and lengths fit signed 31-bit int; no
arbitrary-precision or modular-arithmetic substitution is introduced.

The original consumes length of the formatted string and prints nothing. The
driver consumes the same output stream while comparing every character against
the reviewed fixture, then reports repetitions:checked-characters. It buffers
neither an extra full output list nor a parsed-result cache. This validation adds
character comparison to the source length consumer; document it in comparisons.

### Profiles and correctness

| Profile | Repetitions | Text |
|---|---:|---|
| Smoke | 1 | 10005-byte complete body-paragraph selection |
| Normal | 8 | original 789112-byte text |
| Large | 40 | original 789112-byte text |

Normal/large retain source inputs and counts. Smoke keeps FAST's one repetition
and reduces its dataset for bounded routine checks. Original GHC runs finish
all source profiles with empty stdout; there is no supplied para.stdout fixture.
An export-only original formatter produces complete reviewed formatted text:
784213 bytes for the original input and 9969 bytes for smoke.

An independent quadratic dynamic-programming reference verifies preserved word
order, maximum widths and layout costs for all 3574 original paragraphs.
Source costs agree with the optimum on 3573. Paragraph 483, a 23-word quotation,
has source par3 cost 5 versus optimum 1. Original quadratic par1 confirms cost 1.
Preserve par3's three-line layout exactly; this is an established property of
the pinned source, not evidence against the paper's general algorithm.
Partial source behavior on whitespace-only input and overlong words is retained.

The 112-check target compares 41 complete original cases under both policies,
small full text, the source counterexample, output corruption/length rejection,
zero iterations, front/back queue rebalancing and unused-field demand.
Both policies agree with the complete original text in a guarded streaming
pilot. Full normal calibration and canonical primary/count/semantic runs are
recorded separately as they finish. Full large SML repetition checks remain
unrecorded. An earlier development consumer materialized an extra full output
list and exceeded a private 1-GiB guard; retain that development observation
separately from the final streaming consumer's checks.

### Literature and diagnostic questions

[De Moor and Gibbons, Bridging the Algorithm Gap: A Linear-Time Functional
Program for Paragraph Formatting (1999)](https://www.cs.ox.ac.uk/publications/publication2361-abstract.html)
is the source article; the full literate text is preserved. It motivates the
functional derivation and concrete queue representation.
[Partain's nofib paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17) supplies suite
context. Investigate summary-field demand, symmetric-list sharing/rebalancing,
candidate pruning, paragraph lifetimes, text parsing and output consumption.
These are source-based diagnostic questions; current-host performance claims
need separate measurements.

## sphere-lazy

Numeric policy: lazy.

### Algorithm and workload

Trace a square image of ten source spheres with point lights, shadows, diffuse
and specular shading and recursive reflection. Retain vector/scalar operation
order, the source intersection-list construction, right-associated vector sums,
fold-right nearest-hit selection and contribution-based recursion cutoff.

### History, authorship and variants

David J. King, July 16, 1998, Haskell port of the Impala Id sphere tracer.
The retained October 1 correspondence explicitly supplies a sequential program
for the SCOFPIG challenge. No Impala runtime or parallel facility is needed.
Pinned nofib revision b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798,
spectral/sphere. The individual source/correspondence states no separate
redistribution grant; retain its complete attribution without inferring another
benchmark's license or inventing the earlier Id author's identity.

This program differs from the other ray tracers in scene, camera, surfaces,
intersection selection and recursive shading. Keep its established sphere name.
Lazy and strict numeric payload policies have separate names. The original
source is retained under sphere-lazy/upstream; the scene and lights are generated
constants, with no external dataset or image-file dependency.

### Translation and source behavior

All kernels, drivers, scene generation and checks use SML97. Memoized control
streams and vector nodes preserve demand and sharing; numeric coordinate
payloads are memoized in lazy and eager in strict. The finite source scene,
surface and light constant lists use immutable SML lists. Fresh camera/image
computation occurs on every repetition; no rendered image is cached.

Both policies retain lazy branch selection and recursive ray controls. Unused
numeric coordinates can remain unforced in lazy. Source integer indices fit
portable int. Floating operations use Double-compatible real arithmetic.
The source signed machine-Int hash is made explicit modulo 2^64 with Word64;
selected quantized colors fit portable signed int. Round color*255 to nearest
with ties to even. Preserve negative/out-of-range colors rather than clamp them.

Preserve historical quirks: the zero-vector cutoff tests signed components
against epsilon instead of absolute values; shadow intersection is not bounded
by light distance; nearest-hit folding has the source tie order; transmitted
rays return a false TIR flag even though refractray computes one.
The selected scene has zero transmission, so transmission behavior is a
source-inspection observation, separate from measured standard profiles.

### Inputs and result checks

| Profile | Repetitions | Square image size |
|---|---:|---:|
| Smoke | 1 | 30 |
| Normal | 100 | 100 |
| Large | 100 | 250 |

Smoke reduces source FAST's 100 repetitions to one. Normal/large retain the
source dimensions and counts. Every pixel checks its coordinates, all three
raw color channels and exact quantized colors against reviewed reference rows.
Use absolute 1e-9 plus relative 1e-9 for each finite raw channel. These are
source-agreement bounds, not a formal proof for all host math libraries.
Quantized colors remain exact, including ties-to-even controls.

A streaming forward weighted polynomial reproduces the source right-fold hash
modulo 2^64 while validating the complete image. Report repetitions:checked-pixels
and the final hexadecimal Word64 hash instead of repeated signed decimal hashes.
No early stopping, random seed or source algorithm change is introduced.

Unmodified GHC reproduces every 100-line profile fixture. An export-only observer
records all 73400 pixels across the three image sizes; an independent eager
tracer agrees on every quantized channel, with maximum raw difference below
5.7e-12. The independent model computes camera normalization and closest-hit
selection separately rather than duplicate the stream implementation.

The 69-check target covers original vector/shader fixtures, complete smoke
images, intersections/tangency, surface defaults, TIR, source cutoff/tie/sum
quirks, numeric perturbations, quantization, invalid reference data and sharing.
All six native hosts and Rune pass private semantic checks. Both full normal
SML profiles pass guarded final-source calibration. Canonical matrices/counts
are recorded with the import wave. Full SML large repetition runs remain
unrecorded, separately from their complete reference pixels and source fixtures.

### Literature and diagnostic questions

The retained source and correspondence establish algorithm and translation
history. The refractray comment cites Foley and van Dam, page 757; retain that
limited source attribution without inferring an edition or a reviewed passage.
[Partain's nofib paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17) provides suite
context. Investigate coordinate demand, recursive-ray allocation, scene-list
traversal, nearest-hit sharing, shading math and the pixel/hash consumer.
These are source-based hypotheses until supported by measurements.

## almabench

### Algorithm and workload

Calculate heliocentric planetary positions/velocities and derive right ascension,
declination and distance for eight planets at daily Julian epochs. Retain the
source nested loops, mutable epoch/state/result arrays, mean-element coefficient
tables, trigonometric corrections and iterative Kepler solver.

### History, authorship and source

ALMABENCH 1.0.1 OCaml version by Shawn Wagner, from Scott Robert Ladd's C++/Java
versions. Its individual header explicitly dedicates the program to the public
domain with no rights reserved. Retain that complete notice and attribution.
Pinned Sandmark revision 5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507,
benchmarks/almabench/almabench.ml. The runnable name has no collision and is
almabench. There are no external datasets; all coefficients and epochs are
source constants. No foreign implementation is bundled in this upstream folder.

The source cites J. L. Simon, P. Bretagnon, J. Chapront, M. Chapront-Touze,
G. Francou and J. Laskar, Astronomy & Astrophysics 282, 663 (1994).
The comments' year-range descriptions differ; the executable epoch loop
actually starts at J2000 and advances 36525 days. Describe that concrete loop.

### Portable implementation and numerical choices

All computation, state generation and result checks use SML97. Leaf floating
arrays use RealArray and nested arrays use Array, retaining mutable unboxed
real storage and the original two-by-three state shape. Fixed coefficient
tables retain the same values and nesting; index bounds and integer counters
fit portable signed int for the selected profiles.

Preserve arithmetic association, Real.rem as the source mod_float operation,
Math.atan2 argument order and floating constants. The angle-normalizer comment
claims a half-open range, but exact negative pi maps to positive pi while
positive pi maps to negative pi. Preserve and explicitly test those endpoints.

Keep the Kepler loop's original OR condition: perform at least ten corrections
and continue until the residual condition also holds. Do not replace it with a
maximum-iteration interpretation. The independent reference has its own stopping
rule; agreement on selected states does not justify changing the benchmark.

The source initially computes all eight planets at J2000+1 before timing loops.
Keep and validate those calls too. Reuse the original state/output arrays across
all calls; no ephemeris/result cache is introduced. The optional OCaml GC-stat
file hook is outside the computation contract; OS/runtime statistics belong to
the suite's separate adapters.

### Profiles, consumption and correctness

| Profile | Outer repetitions | Days per repetition | Planet calls |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Smoke | 1 | 32 | 264 |
| Normal | 5 | 36525 | 1461008 |
| Large | 20 | 36525 | 5844008 |

Normal retains the complete source workload. Smoke reduces days/repetitions.
Large selects twenty repetitions, the historical count mentioned in the source,
while retaining the same epoch domain. Each profile includes the eight initial
test calls. Parameters are explicit instead of a universal size argument.

The original mutates arrays and prints nothing. Consume all six state coordinates
and three derived values on every call. For each of nine components accumulate
sum, sum of absolute values and sum of squares, preserving accumulation order.
All values must be finite. Compare all 27 moments to export-only original OCaml
references using absolute 1e-6 plus relative 1e-10 bounds. These are conservative
source-agreement bounds, not an astronomical accuracy guarantee or formal
floating-point error proof. Report planet-calls:27. The added moment consumer
is an explicit adaptation and prevents unused-result elimination.

Original OCaml completes its unmodified full workload with empty stdout.
Its observer produces all profile moments and 64 complete state/result samples
across eight epochs and eight planets. The separate ERFA Plan94 implementation
at revision 9915ba38c9365f8b0738269b8c2ac1fdd5f8dee3 (v2.0.1) agrees exactly
with all 384 sampled state coordinates. ERFA is a reference-only C program:
its complete source notices, pinned files and observer remain in the evidence
archive; the SML benchmark has no C/FFI dependency.

The 163-check target compares 64 original states, 64 independent states,
angle/remainder semantics, smoke moments, every individually perturbed moment,
nonfinite values and malformed/short references. Point comparisons use absolute
and relative 1e-11. Full normal final-source Rune calibration passes; canonical
host/count checks are recorded as they finish. Full large SML repetition checks
remain unrecorded, separately from the original observer's complete large
moments. Incorrect results cannot supply accepted measurements.

### Literature and diagnostic coverage

[Simon et al. (1994)](https://articles.adsabs.harvard.edu/full/1994A%26A...282..663S)
is the original algorithm citation retained in the source. The historical paper
link was unavailable during this import; detailed claims are based on the
reviewed benchmark and independent
[ERFA Plan94 source](https://github.com/liberfa/erfa/blob/9915ba38c9365f8b0738269b8c2ac1fdd5f8dee3/src/plan94.c).
Its limitations and stopping conditions remain distinct from ALMABENCH's.
Investigate scalar math calls, mutable real-array access, bounds elimination,
coefficient reuse, correction loops and result-consumer cost. These are
source-based hypotheses until supported by recorded measurements.

## kb

### Algorithm and workload

Complete the seven source equations for a geometric group using term matching,
substitution, unification, recursive path ordering, critical-pair generation,
rule deletion and normalization. Retain association lists, immutable term trees,
rule numbering, list concatenation/order and the improved completion recursion.
Both source programs produce the same ordered 24-rule canonical system.

### History, authorship, notices and naming

Xavier Leroy, projet Cristal, INRIA Rocquencourt. Individual headers state
Copyright 1996 INRIA and Q Public License version 1.0, with terms/equations/
orderings/kb source revisions dated 1999 and kbmain dated 2005.
Pinned Sandmark revision 5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507,
benchmarks/kb/kb.ml and kb_no_exc.ml. These individual notices take precedence
over assumptions based on the collection's top-level license.

Keep both original files unchanged under kb/upstream. The Rune SML97 translation
is distributed in separate files with original authorship/notices retained.
The canonical QPL-1.0 text is included; its official SPDX source revision and
identity are recorded in the evidence. Historical compiler licensing is retained
only as context; no additional compiler-specific exception is inferred.

The established upstream names kb and kb_no_exc are distinct from the classic
knuth-bendix and knuth-bendix-smlnj programs. Document their related algorithm,
without claiming identical source workloads or replacing the classic names.
No external dataset is required; the geometric group equations are source data.

### Differences between the executable variants

kb uses Failure exceptions for matching and top-level reduction; its pretty_term
and pretty_close are complete stubs. kb_no_exc returns option values from matching
and top-level reduction, while retaining exceptions in deeper rewriting,
unification and completion. Its name does not mean all exception use is removed.

The second source also traverses term structure in its printer despite stub
print functions. Preserve that separate traversal and its infix-arity checks.
Do not attribute every performance difference solely to exceptions versus
options. The exact original output remains empty for both programs.

### Portable translation and runtime behavior

All computation, fixed equations, checks and consumers use SML97.
Shared term/unification, ordering, completion and input modules retain a single
implementation. Separate rewriting modules preserve ordinary versus optional
matching and reduction, including the source membership-then-association lookup
rather than silently combine two traversals into one.

A shared completion functor receives the selected rewriting/printer module.
This module boundary is a translation choice: compiler specialization/inlining
can affect its runtime cost. Record it when interpreting comparisons.
The code retains the source fold-left paired traversal, right-recursive
partition, nested handler scopes, list ordering, variable standardization,
critical-pair namespace offsets and failure categories.

Source integer fields and selected rule/variable counters fit portable signed
int. There is no arbitrary precision substitution, floating arithmetic, random
input, parallel facility or FFI. Optional OCaml GC-stat output belongs to
measurement adapters rather than the portable kernel.

Original kb_complete returns unit after printing the completed rules. The port
returns the already-computed list after preserving the same printer traversal.
Validate its complete canonical serialization, including every rule number,
variable count and term. This is an explicit additional result consumer; it
does not replace completion with a cached rule set.

### Profiles and correctness

| Profile | Completion repetitions |
|---|---:|
| Smoke | 1 |
| Normal | 100 |
| Large | 1000 |

Normal retains the source count; smoke reduces it and large selects ten times
the source repetitions. Every iteration computes a fresh completion over the
source's shared immutable input equations, validates all completed rules and
reports repetitions:checked-rules. No completed-result cache is used.

Unmodified OCaml runs finish both 100-iteration programs with empty stdout.
Export-only observers expose all completed records; their complete canonical
text is byte-identical across variants. Final-source normal Rune calibration
passes both variants. Full SML large repetitions remain unrecorded.

The 1285-check target compares full original rule text and count, checks every
final rule's orientation and irreducible right side, normalizes every input
equation, and verifies all 576 ordered final critical-pair combinations for each
variant. It also covers substitution/unification, occurs/arity checks, path
replacement, repeated/conflicting variables, source standardization, zero
iterations and corrupted-result rejection. Rune and all six native hosts pass
the private target; canonical matrices/counts are recorded with the import wave.

### Literature and diagnostic questions

[Knuth and Bendix, Simple Word Problems in Universal Algebras (1970)](https://doi.org/10.1016/B978-0-08-012975-4.50028-X)
provides completion context.
[Dershowitz, Orderings for Term-Rewriting Systems (1982)](https://www.math.tau.ac.il/~nachumd/papers/Orderings4TRS.pdf)
describes recursive path orderings and termination criteria.
The retained Leroy source establishes this benchmark's concrete algorithm.
Investigate structural equality, association-list lookup, exception/option
propagation, printer traversal, list allocation and higher-order specialization.
These are source-based questions; the finite critical-pair checks and measured
configurations do not establish a general theorem or a performance explanation.

## graph500-gen

### Algorithms and distinct workloads

The efficient sequential generator constructs integer endpoint arrays by
interleaving two random Float draws per edge/bit, generates weights afterward,
permutes vertex labels and then permutes edges. Preserve the source's zero-based
labels and stable Array.fast_sort ordering for equal random keys.

Kernel 1 constructs an array of adjacency lists from supplied edges. It removes
self-loops, retains duplicate edges, inserts both directions and prepends in
source order. Its allocated extent is the observed maximum vertex plus one.
The normal fixture requests 4096 possible labels but allocates 4095 rows because
the largest label is absent. Preserve that source behavior.

The standalone kronecker prototype differs materially. It draws a full first-bit
array before the second-bit array, repeatedly appends/copies float arrays,
keeps one-based coordinates, independently permutes the two coordinate rows,
transposes, permutes edge rows and transposes back. Its List.sort compares the
whole random-key/payload pair, including numeric payloads on ties. Preserve the
quadratic append construction and distinguish it from the efficient generator.

### History, names, provenance and notices

Pinned Sandmark revision 5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507,
benchmarks/graph500seq. Audit all three executables: gen.exe, kernel1_run.exe and
kronecker.exe, plus interfaces and the pure GraphTypes interface located under
graph500par. That shared interface defines numeric types; it requires no parallel
execution facility. The prototype comment credits support from PRISM Lab,
IIT Madras and OCaml Labs without naming an individual author.

Rune names graph500-gen and graph500-kernel1 retain the published run-plan
aliases graph500_gen and graph500_kernel1/graph500_seq_kernel1. Original executable
aliases gen and kernel1_run remain documented. kronecker keeps its original name.
The three programs share provenance and suitable support, not an implementation
that erases their different workloads.

All original programs/interfaces and the collection license remain under
graph500-gen/upstream. Sandmark's collection license is the Unlicense.
Individual graph files state no additional grant. Imported OCaml stdlib sorting,
random and Marshal-format material keeps its separate INRIA 1996 LGPL 2.1 notices
and OCaml linking exception, complete original files and license text.
Sorting is attributed to Xavier Leroy; the existing random helper retains its
Damien Doligez attribution. Do not replace these notices with the collection
license. Stock OCaml 4.14.1 revision/source identities are recorded.

### SML97 translation and evaluation

All kernels, input generation, formatting, binary translation and checking use
SML97. Preserve nested arrays, unboxed RealArray rows, association-list adjacency,
source mutation and copying, sort algorithms/cutoffs and tie behavior.
The stdlib Array.stable_sort and alternating List.stable_sort are translated
rather than replace them with a different sorting algorithm.

Reuse the reviewed OCaml Random draw implementation with a fresh default-state
snapshot for every benchmark invocation. The gen fixture adapter removes
Random.self_init to make its input reproducible. The prototype already uses
the default state. Record the complete state identity; no profile result or
generated graph is cached across invocations.

The efficient generator's dimensions use integer shifts; the prototype derives
them with floating power followed by truncation. Keep both numeric choices.
Selected labels and 30-bit random keys fit signed 31-bit SML int. Hashes use
explicit Word64 modular arithmetic, and binary weights use binary64 semantics.

A portable codec handles the actual finite, unshared edge-array Marshal shape:
small header with both receiver-word counts, compact/32/64-bit block headers,
nonnegative selected integer labels and finite Double fields. It validates
header lengths, object counts, shape, minimum body size and EOF. It is a bounded
translation module rather than an OCaml object runtime.

Optional packing structure names differ across hosts. The codec therefore uses
one common SML97 decomposition/scaling and IntInf/Word64 representation algorithm.
Its valid exact-integer TO_NEAREST conversion and header word literal are identical
on every compiler. Separate optional-API and numeric-control failures remain
in the evidence. No host-conditioned arithmetic or tolerance change is used.

Unix clocks and volatile progress/timing messages are replaced by suite process
measurements and stable result reports. Generation still writes edges.data;
kernel 1 reads its original binary input; the prototype writes kronecker.txt.
Its source exits from the CSV writer, whereas the adapter closes the file and
returns so the complete output can be validated. Filenames and working directories
are fixed by the runner.

### Profiles, source parameters and data origins

| Profile | Efficient generator / kernel 1 | Prototype |
|---|---|---|
| Smoke | scale 6, edge factor 4 | scale 3, edge factor 1 |
| Normal | scale 12, edge factor 16 | scale 8, edge factor 4 |
| Large | scale 14, edge factor 16 | scale 10, edge factor 4 |

The efficient normal profile retains gen's command-line defaults.
The source build/run plans also select 21/16 for gen/kernel 1 and 12/10 for the
prototype. Those larger parameter sets remain explicit future calibration/data
candidates, separately from the practical fixed profiles above. Keep both scale
and edge factor as meaningful upstream parameters. The ignored sequential
-ndomains flag is not a new parallel workload.

Kernel inputs are generated by the original OCaml 4.14.1 serializer using the
reviewed default state. DATA-IDENTITIES.json records every file's source revision,
origin, size, SHA-256 and format magic. These are narrowly reviewed binary source
data. Executable/object/cache artifacts are excluded. Data is synthetic; there
is no separate dataset notice. Preserve the original code and its notices.

### Correctness and measured observations

Generation hashes every encoded output byte and reports edge/byte counts.
Kernel 1 reports edge, vertex and arc counts plus an ordered hash of endpoint
labels and floor(weight*1e8). Every consumed weight must be finite in [0,1).
This numeric check also detects incorrect float interpretation when a broken
encoder/decoder could otherwise cancel in a byte roundtrip.
The prototype validates its complete six-decimal CSV by byte count and hash.
All result checks are exact; no numerical tolerance permits different integer
dimensions, endpoint order, encoded weight bits or source CSV.

Original generated files and all selected prototype CSV outputs agree
byte-for-byte with final portable Rune pilots, including normal and large.
Original Kernel1Seq observations agree with an independent Python decoder and
append/reverse adjacency model on all profiles. Full normal and selected large
Rune calibration passes in a recorded memory/time guard.

The 312-check target covers every smoke edge and weight, complete binary/CSV
fixtures, empty and integer-boundary codecs, malformed/truncated/extra data,
duplicate/self-loop/order controls, 31 list/array sort sizes and forced key ties.
Standalone numeric probes separate source dimension sensitivity, integer-rounding
differences and word construction. Canonical host/count results are recorded as
they finish. Failed primary checks cannot supply accepted timing samples.

Current controls observe SML/NJ Math.pow(2,3) just below eight, so the source
truncation chooses seven; Poly/ML TO_NEAREST changes some already integral
53-bit reals; legacy 32-bit SML/NJ changes the header word in literal/shift
constructions. Preserve the valid program operations and exact findings.
Do not infer one common compiler mechanism from these different observations.

### Literature and diagnostic questions

The [Graph500 specification](https://graph500.org/?page_id=12) provides generator
and graph-construction context. The retained Sandmark source defines these
particular sequential implementations and their differences. Suite reports use
the common SML process-measurement contract; specification-wide search/TEPS
measurements belong to a separate protocol.

Investigate random draw cost, float representation, sorting stability, repeated
array copying, binary translation, adjacency-list allocation and degree-driven
object lifetimes. These are source-based hypotheses until supported by separate
measurements. Complete source agreement is a correctness finding, not an
explanation of a performance difference.

## graph500-kernel1

### Algorithms and distinct workloads

The efficient sequential generator constructs integer endpoint arrays by
interleaving two random Float draws per edge/bit, generates weights afterward,
permutes vertex labels and then permutes edges. Preserve the source's zero-based
labels and stable Array.fast_sort ordering for equal random keys.

Kernel 1 constructs an array of adjacency lists from supplied edges. It removes
self-loops, retains duplicate edges, inserts both directions and prepends in
source order. Its allocated extent is the observed maximum vertex plus one.
The normal fixture requests 4096 possible labels but allocates 4095 rows because
the largest label is absent. Preserve that source behavior.

The standalone kronecker prototype differs materially. It draws a full first-bit
array before the second-bit array, repeatedly appends/copies float arrays,
keeps one-based coordinates, independently permutes the two coordinate rows,
transposes, permutes edge rows and transposes back. Its List.sort compares the
whole random-key/payload pair, including numeric payloads on ties. Preserve the
quadratic append construction and distinguish it from the efficient generator.

## linear-lazy

### Algorithm and workload

Run the source Cg iterative linear-system solver over generated sparse matrices
whose entries are dense four-by-four Float blocks. Retain block-diagonal scaling,
the pseudofactor preconditioner, dense pivoted inversion, forward/back substitution
and the x/r/p/q state updates. Main's historical header calls the method Bi-CGSTAB;
this port follows the actual Cg equations rather than substitute a textbook solver.

### History, authorship, revision and variants

Brian D. Moe wrote the solver/support code in summer 1990; Kamini Shenoi modified
it in summer 1991. Ian R. McLelland and Cordelia V. Hall converted it to Haskell
in November 1992. Input.lhs credits Roger L. Wainwright's data representation and
Dan Vasicek's reader code. Original individual credit/notice headers are retained;
no separate dataset redistribution grant is inferred from another workload.

Pinned nofib revision b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798,
real/linear and gc/linear. Both complete original module trees remain under
linear-lazy/upstream-real and upstream-gc, including the common NofibUtils helper
used by real. Generated hard_data needs no external dataset.

The application variant caps the state sequence at ten and hashes the complete
formatted result 200 times. The GC variant caps it at fifty and prints the result
once. Preserve both consumers and stopping conditions, sharing one reviewed
numerical implementation. Names linear-lazy/strict select the application;
linear-nofib-gc-lazy/strict disambiguate the GC source category. Each retains its
upstream linear alias.

### Translation, data structures and evaluation

All kernels, generation, checks and formatting use SML97. Dense blocks/vectors
and sparse row/entry lists retain the original list structures through memoized
streams. Scalar Float calculations round to binary32 after every operation;
representation uses the common binary64 real type with explicit normal/subnormal,
nearest-even and overflow handling. Selected integer indices fit signed 31-bit int.
No arbitrary-precision replacement of source arithmetic is introduced.

Preserve the scale/preconditioner function parameters, shared partial conditioner
application, higher-order maps/folds and exact accumulation order. A recorded
original GHC interface gives precond arity three. The translation computes each
pseudofactor at that source full-call boundary and adds no cross-call factor cache.

The factor matrix is tied recursively through memoized block/list controls.
Forward substitution retains function-based y calls and its shared sumparts;
back substitution retains the source shared ps lookup and termss. Preserve these
different sharing patterns rather than memoize every recursive function.
Final p/q fields remain outside the displayed metric demand. Numeric payloads
are memoized in lazy and eager in strict; structural controls remain memoized in
both policies, allowing finite strict evaluation to change allocation/forcing.

Keep source diagonal handling, pivot ties, row/column swaps, indexing checks,
empty/singleton block operations, tuple-variable shadowing and block-multiplication
association. The mixed-size well branch is ported and checked against an original
synthetic case, even though the timed generated workload has zero wells.

### Inputs, known modes and profiles

| Source family | Profile | Repetitions | Grid side | State cap |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Application | Smoke | 1 | 2 | 10 |
| Application | Normal | 200 | 4 | 10 |
| Application | Large | 200 | 7 | 10 |
| GC | Smoke | 1 | 2 | 50 |
| GC | Normal | 1 | 14 | 50 |
| GC | Large | 1 | 16 | 50 |

The block grid has side^2 rows; every block is four-by-four.
Application normal/large and GC normal retain source parameters. Smoke reduces
work for routine correctness; GC large is an explicit scaling selection.
Keep the stopping predicate sqrt(norm r) < Float(0.0000004), inclusive takeuntil
behavior, initial state and source cap. The fifty-state normal GC result reaches
its cap with nonzero residual; this is the reviewed source result.

Source test-function options also discuss easy_data, no scaling/preconditioning
and a reservoir gcomp_data mode. The published mains select bilu/hard_data/conv2.
Generic scale/preconditioner callbacks remain, with demand controls in tests.
The reservoir readers currently use literal abc strings and their Data/gcomp.mat*
files are absent. Supplementary inventory entries defer those inactive data
modes until deterministic licensed fixtures and reviewed readers are available.
No prerequisite compiler/runtime feature is added.

### Result consumers and correctness

Validate every demanded iteration index, norm(x-soln) and norm(r) against an
original metric table. Results must match the reviewed binary32 values exactly;
there is no additional numerical error allowance. GEN9 formatting must roundtrip
to the same binary32 value and retains source column widths, headers and START/END
framing. The stable report counts repetitions, checked states and formatted
characters rather than expose platform-dependent shortest decimal hashes.

Application mode still performs the source forward modular Word64 hash over
the adapted text, with an independent reverse polynomial check. GC mode consumes
the formatted text without adding that hash workload. The adapter buffers bounded
formatted rows for validation instead of repetitive stdout. These consumer and
decimal-spelling adaptations are recorded separately from numerical algorithms.

Unmodified GHC matches every supplied application fixture and the GC normal
fixture. Export-only observers expose demanded metrics, inverse/scaled blocks,
preconditioned vectors and a mixed-size well case. Small and full normal Rune
pilots agree under both evaluation policies. Final canonical source checks follow
the explicit callback signature needed for portable SML record resolution.

The 69-check target compares original dense/scaled/preconditioned values and
small metric sequences, verifies a mixed well branch, checks source hash/framing,
roundtrip formatting and incorrect-row rejection, and exercises binary32 ties,
subnormals and overflow. It also proves unused scale/conditioner callbacks remain
delayed. Native host findings and complete canonical matrices are recorded as
they finish. Full SML large repetition checks remain unrecorded unless explicitly
listed in the validation archive.

### Literature and diagnostic coverage

The retained source establishes this particular solver and preconditioner.
[Saad, Iterative Methods for Sparse Linear Systems](https://www-users.cse.umn.edu/~saad/IterMethBook_2ndEd.pdf)
provides general iterative-method/preconditioning context.
[Partain's nofib paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17) supplies suite
context. Do not identify a general accuracy or convergence theorem from the
source's historical method label.

Investigate callback specialization, sparse/dense list traversal, Float rounding,
factor recomputation, recursive sharing, live state lifetimes and adapted text/hash
consumers. These are source-based hypotheses; original metric agreement and
measured compiler configurations are separate findings.

## linear-nofib-gc-lazy

### Algorithm and workload

Run the source Cg iterative linear-system solver over generated sparse matrices
whose entries are dense four-by-four Float blocks. Retain block-diagonal scaling,
the pseudofactor preconditioner, dense pivoted inversion, forward/back substitution
and the x/r/p/q state updates. Main's historical header calls the method Bi-CGSTAB;
this port follows the actual Cg equations rather than substitute a textbook solver.

### History, authorship, revision and variants

Brian D. Moe wrote the solver/support code in summer 1990; Kamini Shenoi modified
it in summer 1991. Ian R. McLelland and Cordelia V. Hall converted it to Haskell
in November 1992. Input.lhs credits Roger L. Wainwright's data representation and
Dan Vasicek's reader code. Original individual credit/notice headers are retained;
no separate dataset redistribution grant is inferred from another workload.

Pinned nofib revision b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798,
real/linear and gc/linear. Both complete original module trees remain under
linear-lazy/upstream-real and upstream-gc, including the common NofibUtils helper
used by real. Generated hard_data needs no external dataset.

The application variant caps the state sequence at ten and hashes the complete
formatted result 200 times. The GC variant caps it at fifty and prints the result
once. Preserve both consumers and stopping conditions, sharing one reviewed
numerical implementation. Names linear-lazy/strict select the application;
linear-nofib-gc-lazy/strict disambiguate the GC source category. Each retains its
upstream linear alias.

### Translation, data structures and evaluation

All kernels, generation, checks and formatting use SML97. Dense blocks/vectors
and sparse row/entry lists retain the original list structures through memoized
streams. Scalar Float calculations round to binary32 after every operation;
representation uses the common binary64 real type with explicit normal/subnormal,
nearest-even and overflow handling. Selected integer indices fit signed 31-bit int.
No arbitrary-precision replacement of source arithmetic is introduced.

Preserve the scale/preconditioner function parameters, shared partial conditioner
application, higher-order maps/folds and exact accumulation order. A recorded
original GHC interface gives precond arity three. The translation computes each
pseudofactor at that source full-call boundary and adds no cross-call factor cache.

The factor matrix is tied recursively through memoized block/list controls.
Forward substitution retains function-based y calls and its shared sumparts;
back substitution retains the source shared ps lookup and termss. Preserve these
different sharing patterns rather than memoize every recursive function.
Final p/q fields remain outside the displayed metric demand. Numeric payloads
are memoized in lazy and eager in strict; structural controls remain memoized in
both policies, allowing finite strict evaluation to change allocation/forcing.

Keep source diagonal handling, pivot ties, row/column swaps, indexing checks,

association. The mixed-size well branch is ported and checked against an original

## bspt-lazy

### Algorithm and workload

Port the complete two-dimensional binary space partitioning modeller: polygon
construction, segment splitting, region classification, area, rendering,
complement and Boolean union/intersection/subtraction. The timed batch builds
and renders the source polygon of sixty vertices from Input.temp0 through temp5.
The other source polygons remain in the upstream snapshot. Interactive commands
are also ported and covered by original output fixtures.

### History, authorship and variants

Source: [nofib real/bspt](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/real/bspt), pinned at
b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798. Preserve the nineteen original modules,
including the common NofibUtils source, under bspt-lazy/upstream. No individual
program author or copyright notice is stated in those files; the _YORK module
suffix alone is insufficient attribution. The original emits an MGR command
stream as text; the benchmark does not require an actual graphical display.
The established name is bspt. Explicit -lazy and -strict suffixes distinguish
numeric evaluation policies while retaining common provenance and algorithms.

### Translation and evaluation decisions

The lazy version memoizes rational numeric fields. The strict version computes
those fields eagerly; both retain delayed tree/control structures, character
streams and unused area roots where source demand matters. Preserve recursive
region/face data, partition projections, simplifications and Boolean merges.
Libfuns.par is the local sequential dummy function returning its second argument;
there is no parallel-runtime dependency. Prelude.seq really forces the left
subtree to weak head normal form during tree construction and is preserved.
Tests distinguish that force from an unused right-hand partition calculation.

Rationals use the source signed 64-bit Int semantics, not unbounded mathematical
rational arithmetic. IntInf storage explicitly wraps machine addition,
multiplication and negation modulo 2^64. Preserve floor division, exceptional
minBound operations, gcd simplification and unit-denominator fast paths.
Derived equality is structural, including noncanonical fractions. Ordering uses
the source wrapped cross-products and its Eq/Ord defaults. Source rounding is
floor(x+1/2), with ties toward positive infinity. All numeric checks are exact;
there is no floating-point tolerance or host-dependent default integer width.

GHC's recorded interface identifies Prog.prog1 as an updatable global thunk for
the batch modeller. The SML batch body is likewise memoized globally, including
across repeated Benchmark.run calls in one process. Geometry is computed and
rendered on demand once; subsequent repetitions traverse shared output and copy
the source per-call mouse/screen prefix. Do not interpret 25,000 repetitions as
25,000 independent geometry builds. Preserve command parsing, mouse coordinate
offsets, clipping, formatting and command quirks. Small individual MGR command
strings are materialized before lazy stream assembly; this buffering adaptation
is distinct from the geometric algorithms.

### Inputs and result validation

All profiles read the deterministic source input batch followed by a newline.
Smoke uses one repetition rather than source FAST's 2,500. Normal retains
25,000 repetitions and large retains 125,000. Every result contains 9,761 bytes
and has source modular hash 2674C83CE2E76A07 (decimal 2771059834570107399).
Every repetition checks all characters against the reviewed original batch.render
and computes the original forward Word64 hash. The expected hash is independently
reconstructed by a reverse polynomial calculation. Comparing characters adds
validation work to the source hash consumer; report it as part of this adapter.
The report is repetitions, total characters, final hexadecimal hash. Its total
character counter uses IntInf solely for portable checking: the large total
1,220,125,000 exceeds the maximum signed 31-bit integer.

Unmodified GHC 9.4.7 agrees with every supplied FAST/NORM/SLOW hash fixture;
export-only observers supply complete batch and eleven interactive command
outputs plus rational arithmetic cases. Run sh tests/benchmarks/check-bspt.sh for the 89-check target. It exercises these
outputs, wrapped arithmetic, noncanonical ordering, ties, known areas,
incorrect-result rejection, subtree demand and numeric sharing across calls.
See the validation archive for actual host/configuration outcomes. Full SML
large-profile runs are unrecorded unless explicitly listed there.

### Runtime behavior and literature

Investigate memoization, recursive trees, rational simplification, stream
allocation, sharing across calls and consumer costs. These are hypotheses from
source inspection. Original-output agreement establishes correctness for the
recorded inputs, not a causal explanation of compiler performance. Fresh-process
runs include the initial cached geometry computation. Repeated in-process runs
retain that cache; preserve warmup samples without assuming steady state.

[Fuchs, Kedem and Naylor, On visible surface generation by a priori tree structures](https://doi.org/10.1145/800250.807481)
provides background on partition-tree rendering, not authorship or an exact
algorithmic specification for this two-dimensional modeller.
[Partain's nofib paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17) supplies suite
context. The pinned source and recorded GHC interface support the specific
evaluation and sharing explanations above.

See [bspt-lazy/PROVENANCE.md](bspt-lazy/PROVENANCE.md) for the per-program record.

## knights-lazy

### Algorithm and workload

Find closed knight tours with depth-first search over the source queue/list of
starting squares. Keep move order UL, UR, DL, DR, LU, LD, RU, RD; detect isolated
squares, select a unique single-descendant move, or order candidates by onward
degree with the source list-comprehension quicksort. All boards compare equal
under the source Eq instance; degree ties therefore retain traversal order.
The printed backtracking-moves counter increases with depth, not with the total
number of nodes searched. Preserve this historical output label and behavior.

### History, authorship and upstream variants

[Jonathan Hill's knights source](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/spectral/knights), version 1.4 with 1992 module
headers, is pinned at b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798. README declares
Hill's authorship and distinguishes this sequential search from a separate
parallel demonstration. All original literate modules, README and bibliography
are retained under knights-lazy/upstream. No separate individual redistribution
grant is stated in these files; retain the source notices and suite provenance.
The active program imports ChessSetList. The unused ChessSetArray alternative
has materially different storage, copying, deletion metadata and formatting;
its -array variants have separate names and reference outputs.

### Translation, representation and evaluation

List variants retain a persistent reversed trail, lazy init/last operations,
size, move number and starting square. Array variants retain immutable boxed
arrays and copying updates; portable memoized vectors store delayed element
values. No mutable in-place board replaces the source persistent structure.
The array's tileIndex is (x-1)*size+y. Preserve its unused indexTile's original
quotient/remainder quirk and deleteFirst's unchanged move count/reset first
square. The board render layouts differ between representations.

-lazy memoizes numeric metadata and candidate degrees. -strict evaluates those
fields eagerly. Both preserve the lazy search frontier, finite child streams,
trail/array roots and first-square field. A deleted singleton can have an unused
undefined first square in the list source; forcing it eagerly changes behavior.
The degree enumeration for singles and the fresh enumeration for sorting remain
separate calls, as in the source. Search, output streams and demanded prefixes
are memoized explicitly. Both variants preserve the source quicksort rather
than replace it with a host library sort.

The inactive array renderer contains logTen 1 = 0 and otherwise recurses with
x div 10. Original spaces 64 1 overflows its stack after reaching zero repeatedly.
For the array variants only, change this formatting base case to logTen 0 = 0.
The reference observer makes exactly that repair and selects ChessSetArray;
retain the failing original and bounded diagnostic. Search, board updates,
numeric values and stopping conditions are unchanged. This is a documented
source repair, not an exact duplicate of the active list program.

### Inputs, profiles and checks

Smoke uses one repetition on an 8-by-8 board and asks for one tour. Normal retains
100 repetitions on a 14-by-14 board; large retains 100 on a 20-by-20 board.
Source FAST also uses 100 repetitions; reducing only the smoke repetition count
keeps routine checks practical. Source normal and large parameters are retained.
All indices, coordinates and search counters fit signed 31-bit arithmetic for
these profiles. The total checked-character counter uses IntInf as metadata.

The original program prints the length of its rendered tour in each repetition.
The port compares every rendered character with an original full-tour fixture,
and reports repetitions plus total checked characters. This extra validation
and character forcing are explicit consumer adaptations. Every repetition
restarts the search; no memoized result is added across Benchmark.run calls.
Original GHC 9.4.7 matches all active FAST/NORM/SLOW fixtures. Export-only
observers record seven full-tour cases, including three tours, no solution and
zero requested solutions. Array fixtures use the separately reviewed repair.
No floating-point tolerance applies.

## knights-strict

### Algorithm and workload

degree with the source list-comprehension quicksort. All boards compare equal
under the source Eq instance; degree ties therefore retain traversal order.
The printed backtracking-moves counter increases with depth, not with the total
number of nodes searched. Preserve this historical output label and behavior.

### History, authorship and upstream variants

[Jonathan Hill's knights source](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/spectral/knights), version 1.4 with 1992 module

grant is stated in these files; retain the source notices and suite provenance.

has materially different storage, copying, deletion metadata and formatting;
its -array variants have separate names and reference outputs.

### Translation, representation and evaluation

List variants retain a persistent reversed trail, lazy init/last operations,
size, move number and starting square. Array variants retain immutable boxed
arrays and copying updates; portable memoized vectors store delayed element
values. No mutable in-place board replaces the source persistent structure.
The array's tileIndex is (x-1)*size+y. Preserve its unused indexTile's original
quotient/remainder quirk and deleteFirst's unchanged move count/reset first
square. The board render layouts differ between representations.

-lazy memoizes numeric metadata and candidate degrees. -strict evaluates those
fields eagerly. Both preserve the lazy search frontier, finite child streams,
trail/array roots and first-square field. A deleted singleton can have an unused
undefined first square in the list source; forcing it eagerly changes behavior.

separate calls, as in the source. Search, output streams and demanded prefixes
are memoized explicitly. Both variants preserve the source quicksort rather
than replace it with a host library sort.

The inactive array renderer contains logTen 1 = 0 and otherwise recurses with
x div 10. Original spaces 64 1 overflows its stack after reaching zero repeatedly.
For the array variants only, change this formatting base case to logTen 0 = 0.
The reference observer makes exactly that repair and selects ChessSetArray;
retain the failing original and bounded diagnostic. Search, board updates,
numeric values and stopping conditions are unchanged. This is a documented
source repair, not an exact duplicate of the active list program.

All indices, coordinates and search counters fit signed 31-bit arithmetic for
these profiles. The total checked-character counter uses IntInf as metadata.

The port compares every rendered character with an original full-tour fixture,

restarts the search; no memoized result is added across Benchmark.run calls.
