## mate-lazy

### Algorithm and workload

Search the source AND–OR chess end-game tree to depth 2*N-1: select the first
winning attacking move, then prove a winning continuation for every legal reply.
Retain list-based boards, legality checks, line-move continuations, source move
order, pawn promotion and king threats. The program's move rules omit castling
and en passant; do not substitute a different full-chess engine. Compact equal
printed reply subtrees and print the source descriptive notation and ordering.

### History, authorship and data

The pinned [nofib mate source](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/spectral/mate) is revision
b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798. README describes AND–OR search and a
historical nhc98 timing example. No individual program author is stated in its
five Haskell modules or README. Preserve all originals, puzzle data and historical
solution files under mate-lazy/upstream. The README's 2017 fixture note predates
the current FAST/NORM/SLOW Makefile selections; use the pinned manifests and
actual runs as evidence rather than assuming that note is current.

Puzzle comments declare individual composition history: G. Heathcote's Reading
Observer problem (1904), Kohtz and Kockelkorn's Schachaufgaben problem (1875),
and the Holzhausen problem, plus other retained composers/dates. Preserve each
input's comments and notices; do not treat a puzzle composer as program author.
The simple problem's comment describes a castled king trapped behind pawns.
New tiny validation positions are generated deterministic test data, separately
identified by cases.py. No separate dataset redistribution notice is stated in
these puzzle headers; retain the complete pinned files and suite provenance.

### Variants and portable translation

-lazy uses memoized board-list spines, move generation and result trees with
source short-circuiting. -strict additionally materializes each position's finite
legal-move list eagerly; it does not exhaustively evaluate the whole search tree.
Both retain attacking disjunction and defending conjunction stopping rules.
They must agree on the selected move and complete printed solution. Each
Benchmark.run starts the source computation from its input; no cross-call result
cache is added.

Keep persistent board removal/insertion and source ray/sift ordering. Explicit
callbacks preserve moveLine's difference-list continuations. Preserve default
constructor order for pieces, moves and promotions. Compaction compares printed
subtrees; the stable natural mergesort used by the source Data.List.sortBy is
translated with its run detection and equal-key ordering. The foldr attacking
selection is exposed as choose for a negative demand test; it uses the same
move stream and source search rules. Portable pair type annotations resolve
record selectors on all SML hosts without changing representations.

Read the fixed problem and reviewed expected text once per run. Materialize the
bounded final textual report before comparison, replacing repetitive stdout;
record this output buffering/validation adaptation separately from the search.
The source parser's comments, ranks, piece colours and goal convention remain.
All board coordinates, depths and selected problem counts fit signed 31-bit
integers; no arbitrary-precision or floating-point arithmetic is needed.

### Inputs, profiles and exact validation

Smoke selects upstream runtime_files/simple.prob, a one-move problem. This is an
explicit smaller source problem than FAST's three-move heathcote3.prob, whose
full output is also validated in private calibration and reference fixtures.
Normal retains runtime_files/kohtz.prob; large retains
runtime_files/holzhausen.prob. The timed program processes one named problem,
not a synthetic universal size parameter. Preserve the relative runtime_files
path because the original File header includes it.

Compare the complete source output byte for byte and report its checked length:
212 characters for smoke, 374 for normal and 2159 for large. There is no numerical
tolerance. Original GHC 9.4.7 matches all published FAST/NORM/SLOW fixtures.
The selected smaller smoke has its own original complete output. Historical
.soln files can use older notation and are retained as provenance rather than
silently promoted to current exact expectations.

The 48-check target compares nine original legal-move/updated-board fixtures and
six small solutions, verifies promotion choices, stable sorting, constructor
order, persistent boards, unused-opponent demand and a winning alternative's
unforced tail, and rejects incorrect output. These controls distinguish intended
search pruning from accidental evaluation. Earlier draft demand probes and
relative-path/type-annotation failures remain development evidence, not reported
compiler bugs. See the recorded validation for actual host configurations and
profile limits. Full large SML runs are claimed only where explicitly recorded.

### Literature and diagnostic interpretation

[The source README](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/spectral/mate/README) describes this particular AND–OR workload;
[Partain's nofib paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17) provides suite
context. The puzzle headers supply their historical references. Do not infer
alpha–beta pruning, transposition tables or a chess-correctness theorem from a
generic game-search literature citation: these facilities are absent here.

Investigate persistent board traversal, short-circuit search, eager legal-list
allocation, continuation specialization, repeated printing during compaction and
stable sorting. These are source-based diagnostic questions. Exact agreement
with original outputs establishes results for the selected inputs; timing/count
records are measured evidence and do not alone identify performance causes.

## expert-lazy

### Algorithm and workload

Run the source animal-identification expert system: parse relations and rules,
rename variables, unify phrases with an occurs check, search and/or goals and
request answers as part of the result stream. Keep the binary-search-tree
knowledge/environment tables, lazy information table, fresh-variable stream,
duplicate-question filtering and solution/environment display. The information
table is built from the questions produced by the same inference computation;
this feedback is part of the workload, not ordinary eager input lookup.

### History, authorship and input origins

[Ian Holyer's expert source](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/spectral/expert), pinned at
b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, declares a March 1993 translation and
adaptation from his Functional programming with Miranda (Pitman, 1991).
Preserve all six Haskell modules and the README under expert-lazy/upstream.
Search.hs also records S. L. Peyton Jones's November 1999 extraction of shared
question text to avoid dependence on accidental compiler common-subexpression
elimination. Preserve that shared value explicitly.

The source runtime_files/animals and expert.stdin provide the fixed knowledge
and answer data. Retain their contents and source paths; no separate individual
dataset notice is stated. The supplied answer No is intentionally positive:
only a line whose words are exactly lowercase no is negative. Do not normalize
case or substitute a different interpretation of yes/no.

### Variants and translation decisions

-lazy memoizes phrase trees and child streams. -strict eagerly traverses each
finite phrase's children when its term is demanded. Both preserve lazy search,
question/answer feedback, table roots and delayed answer values: eager feedback
would force a question's answer before that question can be emitted. Explicit
control delays also preserve unused replies after a negative More answer.
The two policies have separate names and count records, with a poison-child
check demonstrating their intended evaluation difference.

The generic source table's key domain is specialized to the String keys used by
this program; retain lexical comparison and its binary tree, rather than replace
it with a host map/hash table. enterList remains lazy and first duplicate wins;
updateList retains insertion sorting, last-new-duplicate selection, sorted merge
and median balancing. Single updates, lookup, delete and entry enumeration are
also translated and checked. Retain unification's source zip truncation for
mismatched term arities; do not silently impose a new arity check.

Source strings are portable SML strings where bounded words/question formatting
need a complete value. Character, rule, answer and result streams retain explicit
memoized spines. Knowledge lines and answer words use their ASCII fixture
semantics. The driver builds one shared input-character stream and takes the
source i+9999 prefix separately for each repetition. Line splitting and answer
values remain delayed; no per-iteration full input conversion forces unused
answers. Each repetition rebuilds inference and its feedback table as in Main.
The question string is shared between display and information lookup.

### Inputs, profiles and result checks

Smoke uses one repetition instead of source FAST's 1000. Normal retains 10000
repetitions and large retains 50000. Preserve the source per-repetition prefix
parameter i+9999, fixed animal knowledge and exact answer bytes. This input is
shorter than every selected prefix, but the prefix computation is still present.
Selected indices and generated variable suffixes fit signed 31-bit arithmetic;
the total checked-character report uses IntInf as validation metadata.

The source prints length(process ...) each repetition: 526 for the supplied
answers. The port instead compares all 526 dialog characters on every repetition
and reports repetitions plus their total. This adds exact character validation
to the source length consumer and explicitly forces character values as well as
spines. Original GHC 9.4.7 matches every supplied FAST/NORM/SLOW length fixture;
an export-only observer provides the complete original dialog and five additional
answer scenarios. All checks are exact, with no numerical tolerance.

The 45-check target covers those six original dialogs, positive/negative answer
case, first/last duplicate behavior, update/lookup/delete/order, substitution,
occurs rejection, source arity behavior, question-before-answer demand, unused
answers, policy-specific phrase forcing, repetition and corrupt-dialog rejection.
Normal pilots use the original repetition count under explicit resource guards.
See the validation archive for actual compiler/engine results; full SML large
repetitions remain unrecorded unless listed explicitly.

### Literature and diagnostic questions

The source README credits Holyer's Functional programming with Miranda (1991).
Record this as its stated ancestry; the source, not an assumed textbook algorithm,
defines the exact unification, table and feedback behavior.
[Partain's nofib paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17) provides suite
context. Search.hs's dated shared-string comment is source evidence for that
adaptation; it does not establish a current compiler performance cause.

Investigate phrase traversal, repeated substitution, table balance, delayed
input, knot tying, string sharing and stream allocation. These are source-based
hypotheses. Original-dialog agreement and explicit demand checks establish
correctness for the recorded cases. Runtime/count measurements are separate
observations, and fresh versus repeated execution retains its recorded mode.

## expert-strict

### Algorithm and workload

Run the source animal-identification expert system: parse relations and rules,
rename variables, unify phrases with an occurs check, search and/or goals and
request answers as part of the result stream. Keep the binary-search-tree
knowledge/environment tables, lazy information table, fresh-variable stream,
duplicate-question filtering and solution/environment display. The information
table is built from the questions produced by the same inference computation;
this feedback is part of the workload, not ordinary eager input lookup.

### History, authorship and input origins

[Ian Holyer's expert source](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/spectral/expert), pinned at
b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798, declares a March 1993 translation and
adaptation from his Functional programming with Miranda (Pitman, 1991).
Preserve all six Haskell modules and the README under expert-lazy/upstream.
Search.hs also records S. L. Peyton Jones's November 1999 extraction of shared
question text to avoid dependence on accidental compiler common-subexpression
elimination. Preserve that shared value explicitly.

The source runtime_files/animals and expert.stdin provide the fixed knowledge
and answer data. Retain their contents and source paths; no separate individual
dataset notice is stated. The supplied answer No is intentionally positive:
only a line whose words are exactly lowercase no is negative. Do not normalize
case or substitute a different interpretation of yes/no.

### Variants and translation decisions

-lazy memoizes phrase trees and child streams. -strict eagerly traverses each
finite phrase's children when its term is demanded. Both preserve lazy search,
question/answer feedback, table roots and delayed answer values: eager feedback
would force a question's answer before that question can be emitted. Explicit
control delays also preserve unused replies after a negative More answer.
The two policies have separate names and count records, with a poison-child
check demonstrating their intended evaluation difference.

The generic source table's key domain is specialized to the String keys used by
this program; retain lexical comparison and its binary tree, rather than replace
it with a host map/hash table. enterList remains lazy and first duplicate wins;
updateList retains insertion sorting, last-new-duplicate selection, sorted merge
and median balancing. Single updates, lookup, delete and entry enumeration are
also translated and checked. Retain unification's source zip truncation for
mismatched term arities; do not silently impose a new arity check.

Source strings are portable SML strings where bounded words/question formatting
need a complete value. Character, rule, answer and result streams retain explicit
memoized spines. Knowledge lines and answer words use their ASCII fixture
semantics. The driver builds one shared input-character stream and takes the
source i+9999 prefix separately for each repetition. Line splitting and answer
values remain delayed; no per-iteration full input conversion forces unused
answers. Each repetition rebuilds inference and its feedback table as in Main.
The question string is shared between display and information lookup.

case, first/last duplicate behavior, update/lookup/delete/order, substitution,
occurs rejection, source arity behavior, question-before-answer demand, unused
answers, policy-specific phrase forcing, repetition and corrupt-dialog rejection.
Normal pilots use the original repetition count under explicit resource guards.

## regexredux2

### Algorithm and workload

Run the regex-redux pipeline: strip FASTA headers/newlines, count nine DNA motif
patterns one at a time and apply the five source substitutions in order. Print
all pattern/count pairs and the original, stripped and final lengths. Preserve
case-folded motif counting, case-sensitive substitutions and the source count
loop's next search position at match-start+1, including overlapping matches.
Global substitution resumes at the previous match end.

### History, names and notices

Source [Sandmark benchmarksgame/regexredux2.ml](https://github.com/ocaml-bench/sandmark/blob/5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507/benchmarks/benchmarksgame/regexredux2.ml), pinned
at 5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507. Christophe Troestler contributed the
regex-dna ancestor; Roman Kashitsyn adapted mutation to Bytes. The established
workload is regex-redux; retain regexredux2 as the pinned executable variant name
and document regex-dna as ancestry rather than an exact duplicate. The required
source pipeline differs from other historical regex-dna substitution programs.

The pinned fasta3 generator credits Troestler, Mauricio Fernandez and Tony
Tavener. Preserve both original programs, Dune, README, Revised BSD LICENSE and
the Sandmark root notice. The individual BSD notice names Brent Fulgham and
Isaac Gouy. All input profiles are generated from the pinned fasta3 source with
its fixed initial random state and original probability tables. Record full
file hashes and byte lengths in DATA-IDENTITIES.json; these are generated text
data, not embedded executable artifacts.

### Portable library replacement

The original uses OCaml Str's native library. A portable SML97 adapter implements
the precise fragment used here: literal characters, enumerated/negated character
sets, dot excluding newline, greedy star with backtracking, ordered escaped
alternatives, line anchors, ASCII case folding, forward search and constant
replacement. It preserves regular-expression matching instead of replacing
motif searches with direct nucleotide counts or a combined scan. Compile each
motif at its source call site and run one pattern at a time. This adapter is
scoped to these fixed expressions; it does not claim the full Str API, grouping,
backreferences, ranges or empty-match replacement support.

The engine uses immutable expression lists and explicit substring indices;
OCaml Str's internal engine/representation is not reproduced. Record this
library replacement when interpreting measurements. Read the selected fixed
file with portable TextIO.inputAll rather than the original incremental
Bytes/Buffer input loop. Preserve complete input materialization, strict
pipeline order, original replacement strings and immutable intermediate text.
The driver suppresses repetitive stdout, compares the complete report exactly
and returns its checked length. All byte lengths and counts fit signed 31-bit
integers for these profiles. No numerical tolerance applies.

### Inputs and profiles

Smoke generates FASTA with N=100 (1095 bytes). Normal uses N=50000 (508411 bytes),
and large uses N=500000 (5083411 bytes). The pinned program expects an input
named input5000000.txt generated with N=5000000. These are explicit smaller
profile selections, retaining the generator, seed, sequence proportions and
line widths; they do not claim to measure the published 50 MB input. Profile
filenames are manifest parameters rather than a hardcoded working-directory
filename. The source is processed as a whole file, with no universal size loop.

Expected complete reports contain 259, 274 and 286 characters respectively.
Original OCaml 4.14.1 supplies all three results. A private full large SML pilot
also matches its original; canonical smoke/normal checks and configurations
are recorded separately. Further edge cases include empty input, case changes,
adjacent substitutions, an unterminated header and overlapping motifs.

### Validation

The 23-check target compares twelve original Str-library observations and five
full original program reports, plus the smoke fixture, bad-output rejection,
negative indices, literal/escaped pipe distinction, malformed classes and empty
replacement rejection. Library cases cover ordered alternatives, greediness,
backtracking, line/end anchors, negated sets, overlapping counts and ASCII
case folding. The original executable and its generator remain correctness
references. Measurements compare identical SML sources across SML compilers.

### Literature and diagnostic interpretation

[The Benchmarks Game description](https://benchmarksgame-team.pages.debian.net/benchmarksgame/description/regexredux.html)
defines the motif/replacement sequence and notes that regex libraries can use
different algorithms. [The OCaml 4.14 Str manual](https://ocaml.org/manual/4.14/api/Str.html)
documents the matching, anchors and replacement interface used for the adapter;
actual original-library observations establish the selected edge cases.

Investigate regex compilation, literal/class scanning, greedy backtracking,
intermediate string allocation and buffered input. These are source-based
questions. Exact original report agreement establishes the selected results;
current timings or allocations alone do not attribute differences to a regex
engine, library implementation or compiler transformation.

## multiplier-lazy

### Algorithm and workload

Simulate the source binary shift/add multiplier as streams of bit signals.
Preserve combinational gates, balanced wide gates, full-adder carry chains,
word multiplexors, latches, shifting registers and the ready-driven input
interface. Inputs are the infinite pairs (2+3*i,11+2*i), starting at i=1,
truncated to the selected input width. The product register has twice that
width. Do not replace the bit-level circuit with arithmetic multiplication.

### History, authorship and consumers

[John T. O'Donnell's July 1992 multiplier source](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/spectral/multiplier/Main.hs), University
of Glasgow, is pinned at b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798. Preserve the
Copyright (c) 1992 header and original Main/Makefile/fixtures under
multiplier-lazy/upstream. No separate individual redistribution grant is stated.
This is a sequential functional stream simulation; no hardware or parallel
runtime is required.

The active go function selects verbose traceMult. Its inactive runMult driver
instead sums the ready signal and prints the count. Preserve that materially
different consumer as multiplier-count-lazy/strict, with a supplementary source
inventory entry. It does not demand the product register/adder; source inspection
and a pending-product test establish that boundary. It is a ready/control-path
workload, not a claim to force the complete product calculation. Generic component
utilities without a selected simulation driver remain in the original snapshot;
they are support code rather than additional executable workloads.

### Evaluation and translation

-lazy preserves the active source lift21: its two input spines are matched but
its output bit is delayed. -strict adds output-head forcing at that binary
combinator, corresponding to the source's commented strict alternative. Both
retain source headstrict on unary and three-/four-input lifting. Truth-table
gates inspect both input bits; AND/OR are not replaced by short-circuit boolean
operators. The source forceBit predicate and strictness points remain explicit.

Use memoized bit and word spines, paired adder outputs and the original mutually
recursive signals. Word combinators delay both tail access and wire arguments;
forcing either while constructing a future word node creates an invalid circular
demand. wideGate's length traverses only outer spines. Carry-chain matching and
zero-width adder base-case demand follow the source. The independent clock model
is a correctness oracle and is not the measured circuit implementation.

Word-to-integer display uses modular Word64 accumulation and signed conversion,
preserving the source's 64-bit Int behavior for long bit vectors. The fixed
input generator, cycle counters and observed register values fit signed 31-bit
integers in the selected profiles. Preserve explicit wire widths even where
leading zeros make the output identical across widths. Numeric validation is
exact; no floating-point tolerance applies.

### Inputs and profiles

| Profile | Input bit width | Clock cycles |
|---|---:|---:|
| Smoke | 32 | 16 |
| Normal | 256 | 2000 |
| Large | 512 | 2000 |

Normal and large retain the original width/cycle parameters. Smoke reduces
FAST's 2000 cycles to sixteen, using its exact header and trace prefix. Every
trace result is compared character by character with the original full output:
1093 bytes for smoke, 132037 for normal/large. The stable report gives width,
cycles and checked characters. Buffer each bounded formatted row before lazy
character assembly, replacing repetitive stdout with exact validation.

Count variants preserve runMult's sum of the first requested ready bits. The
original and independent model give three for smoke and 222 for normal/large.
The report gives width, cycles and that validated sum. The source count consumer's
limited demand is intentional and differs from the full trace contract. The
driver rejects nonpositive widths and bounds selected cycles to 2000, making
the original valid-input precondition explicit rather than entering its empty
wide-gate recursion on zero width.

### Correctness and recorded scope

Unmodified GHC 9.4.7 matches every supplied FAST/NORM/SLOW fixture. Export-only
observers expose complete traces and count results at eight width/cycle choices.
An independent masked shift/add state machine matches all those original outputs,
including small-width truncation and all published 2000-cycle profiles.

The 56-check target covers five small original traces/counts under both policies,
truth tables, unary/binary strictness, non-short-circuit AND, latch delay, lazy
word callbacks/tails, spine-only length, zero-width adder demand, signed 64-bit
wrap, incorrect output, memoization and the count consumer's unforced product.
Native host checks and canonical matrices are recorded separately. Earlier
recursive-forcing failures and snapshots are translation-development evidence,
not compiler bugs. Full normal trace pilots match original text under resource
guards; final canonical source identities remain distinct from older pilots.
Full SML large traces are unrecorded unless explicitly listed in validation.

### Literature and diagnostic questions

[O'Donnell's research bibliography](https://www.dcs.gla.ac.uk/~jtod/research/)
lists Hardware description with recursion equations (1987), providing functional
circuit-simulation context. It is not an exact specification of this benchmark.
[Partain's nofib paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17) supplies suite
context. The pinned program defines the actual circuit and strictness points.

Investigate higher-order gate specialization, memoized feedback, bit-stream
allocation, carry propagation, wide-gate traversal and the consumer's forcing.
These are source-based diagnostic questions. Original/model agreement and demand
controls establish recorded behavior; allocation or timing differences alone do
not identify a compiler or collector cause.

integers in the selected profiles. Preserve explicit wire widths even where
leading zeros make the output identical across widths. Numeric validation is
exact; no floating-point tolerance applies.

### Inputs and profiles

| Profile | Input bit width | Clock cycles |
|---|---:|---:|
| Smoke | 32 | 16 |
| Normal | 256 | 2000 |
| Large | 512 | 2000 |

Normal and large retain the original width/cycle parameters. Smoke reduces
FAST's 2000 cycles to sixteen, using its exact header and trace prefix. Every
trace result is compared character by character with the original full output:
1093 bytes for smoke, 132037 for normal/large. The stable report gives width,
cycles and checked characters. Buffer each bounded formatted row before lazy
character assembly, replacing repetitive stdout with exact validation.

Count variants preserve runMult's sum of the first requested ready bits. The
original and independent model give three for smoke and 222 for normal/large.
The report gives width, cycles and that validated sum. The source count consumer's
limited demand is intentional and differs from the full trace contract. The
driver rejects nonpositive widths and bounds selected cycles to 2000, making
the original valid-input precondition explicit rather than entering its empty
wide-gate recursion on zero width.

### Correctness and recorded scope

Unmodified GHC 9.4.7 matches every supplied FAST/NORM/SLOW fixture. Export-only
observers expose complete traces and count results at eight width/cycle choices.
An independent masked shift/add state machine matches all those original outputs,
including small-width truncation and all published 2000-cycle profiles.

The 56-check target covers five small original traces/counts under both policies,
truth tables, unary/binary strictness, non-short-circuit AND, latch delay, lazy
word callbacks/tails, spine-only length, zero-width adder demand, signed 64-bit
wrap, incorrect output, memoization and the count consumer's unforced product.
Native host checks and canonical matrices are recorded separately. Earlier
recursive-forcing failures and snapshots are translation-development evidence,
not compiler bugs. Full normal trace pilots match original text under resource
guards; final canonical source identities remain distinct from older pilots.
Full SML large traces are unrecorded unless explicitly listed in validation.

### Literature and diagnostic questions

[O'Donnell's research bibliography](https://www.dcs.gla.ac.uk/~jtod/research/)
lists Hardware description with recursion equations (1987), providing functional
circuit-simulation context. It is not an exact specification of this benchmark.
[Partain's nofib paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17) supplies suite
context. The pinned program defines the actual circuit and strictness points.

Investigate higher-order gate specialization, memoized feedback, bit-stream
allocation, carry propagation, wide-gate traversal and the consumer's forcing.
These are source-based diagnostic questions. Original/model agreement and demand
controls establish recorded behavior; allocation or timing differences alone do
not identify a compiler or collector cause.

## event-lazy

### Algorithm and workload

Simulate the source thirteen-wire circuit with timed three-state NAND events.
Merge the two periodic input clocks, process pending events in time order,
discard unchanged signals, update persistent state lists and schedule dependent
NAND outputs three simulated time units later. NAND results capture the state
snapshot at scheduling time. Stable merges process existing pending events before
new events at the same time; sorting preserves dependency order for equal times.

The source simulator returns changed events. A second source pass, findLastState,
reapplies those changes to an initial state for display. Retain both update passes;
do not replace them with the simulator's internal final state or a mutable-array
simulation. The independent heap-based model is only a correctness oracle.

### History, provenance and related workloads

Source [nofib spectral/hartel/event](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/spectral/hartel/event), pinned at
b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798. No individual author or separate notice is
stated in Main.hs; the collection name alone is insufficient program attribution.
Preserve the complete generated Haskell module, Makefile and fixtures under
event-lazy/upstream/event, with the parent Fast2haskell.hs compatibility shim.
This is a timed event-queue simulator, distinct from the stream multiplier and
other circsim topologies/consumers. Names -lazy/-strict identify finite-state
policies, not exact duplicates of those programs.

### Translation and evaluation decisions

-lazy memoizes finite state/dependency list heads and spines. -strict evaluates
those finite lists eagerly when their root is requested. Both preserve lazy
infinite clock streams, pending-event streams, event values and control roots.
A state update's outer delay keeps unused state unforced at the horizon cutoff.
Persistent prefix copying, dependency construction, duplicate suppression,
stable mergesort and function-valued gate definitions remain.

Check time >= horizon before forcing an event's wire/value or previous state.
Preserve NAND's three-state pattern order: a low left input can yield high
without demanding the right input. The strict finite-state variant may evaluate
more state fields but does not turn event/control streams into infinite eager
lists. Retain the source reconstructed output event and its shared field values.

Fast2haskell's pinned miraseq is a no-op implemented through seq_const, despite
the strict terminology in generated fold helpers. Do not translate that stub as
an actual strict accumulator operation. The lazy dependency fold preserves its
behavior; the strict finite-list policy is a separately named port choice.
Global initial clock/dependency/state values retain source sharing across
repetitions and repeated Benchmark.run calls; simulation state updates remain
fresh persistent values. Every numeric profile value fits signed 31-bit integers.
No floating-point or OS-clock dependency is required.

### Inputs and exact result validation

| Profile | Repetitions | Exclusive event horizon |
|---|---:|---:|
| Smoke | 1 | 200 |
| Normal | 100 | 100000 |
| Large | 100 | 500000 |

Normal and large retain original parameters. Smoke reduces FAST's hundred runs
at horizon ten thousand to one run at horizon two hundred. These are deterministic
simulated-time bounds, not wall-clock search limits. The two clocks and thirteen
initial unknown states are the original fixed input. Wire two remains unused.

Validate every thirteen-symbol state and trailing newline exactly; the selected
profiles yield HHxLLHHLLHHLH. Return repetitions, checked characters and final
state instead of source repeated stdout. Input argument lookup is outside the
repetition loop; the event computation and both update passes remain inside it.
All checks are exact, with no numerical tolerance. Full SML large repetitions
remain unrecorded unless explicitly listed in validation.

### Correctness and runtime observations

Original GHC 9.4.7 matches all supplied FAST/NORM/SLOW fixtures. Export-only
observers record complete states, changed-event traces at twelve boundary
horizons and the dependency table. An independent stable-priority-queue model
agrees with every observed state/trace, including startup, equal timestamps and
exclusive cutoffs. The port matches those traces and the full normal profile.

The 72-check target also covers the NAND table/short circuit, cutoff demand,
persistent states, overwritten lazy fields, strict finite-state behavior,
unneeded initial states, gate callbacks, cached clocks with fresh simulation
state and wrong-result rejection. Recorded native/engine outcomes are separate
from the private development pilots.

### Literature and diagnostic questions

[Hartel and Langendoen, Benchmarking implementations of lazy functional languages](https://doi.org/10.1145/165180.165230)
(1993) supplies collection context for translated workloads. It does not establish
individual authorship of this module. The pinned program defines this circuit,
its stable event ordering and compatibility-shim behavior.

Investigate queue/list allocation, persistent updates, dependency sharing,
finite-state strictness, gate callbacks and retained clock prefixes. These are
source-based diagnostic hypotheses. Original/model traces establish selected
behavior; counts/timings alone do not identify compiler or collector causes.
Fresh and repeated execution retain the recorded sharing/measurement modes.

## typecheck-lazy

### Algorithm and workload

Infer polymorphic types for the source's eight fixed functional programs:
recursive ones, length, map, SKK, increment, sum, recursive Y and succ. Preserve
unification with occurs checking, scheme instantiation/generalization, recursive
bindings, deterministic split name supplies and printed type variables. The succ
case reports failure under the source algorithm. The original consumer sums
printed character codes and returns (sum+character-count)/character-count.

Substitutions remain callable name-to-type functions composed by higher-order
closures. Environments remain ordered association lists, with shadowing and
source lookup costs. Do not replace them with union-find variables, mutable
substitution tables or a host typechecker.

### History, authorship and naming

Source [nofib spectral/hartel/typecheck](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/spectral/hartel/typecheck), pinned at
b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798. Preserve Main.hs, Makefile, all fixtures
and the parent Fast2haskell.hs under typecheck-lazy/upstream. No individual author
or separate program notice is stated in Main.hs. Collection-paper authorship is
context rather than evidence of individual program authorship. Names retain the
established typecheck workload and separate -lazy/-strict evaluation policies.

### Source details and portable adaptation

-lazy memoizes type constructors and finite children; -strict demands those
children when a type constructor is requested. Both preserve lazy expression,
environment, scheme and control structures where failure can leave work unused.
Names use bounded atomic SML strings rather than lazy character lists. Keep the
eight immutable input ASTs global, but add no cross-repetition inferred-row cache.
Each source repetition maps inference over the flattened program list.

Unification of equation lists proceeds right to left, as the source foldr;
it can skip an earlier equation payload after a later failure. Preserve source
zip truncation for mismatched constructor arities. Source noDuplicates reverses
first-occurrence order. Environment range maps first-match lookup over every
name, so shadowed duplicate names repeat the first scheme's unknowns. Keep those
behaviors rather than substitute customary library implementations.

Preserve name-supply splitting/depletion, the same scheme supply across a group
of declarations, function substitution composition and the source recursive-let
stages, including applying the next substitution to already substituted bounds
and environments. Fast2haskell's miraseq stub is a no-op; a generated strict
helper name is not proof of strict evaluation. These choices matter to structure,
sharing and printed type-variable names.

### Profiles and result consumers

Smoke uses one repetition instead of source FAST's 500. Normal retains 5000
repetitions and large retains 25000. Every repetition processes the original eight
ASTs and 239 printed characters. Preserve the original checksum, while adding an
exact comparison of each inferred row with the reviewed original rows before its
characters enter the checksum. The validation callback adds observable work and
is documented separately from the inference algorithm.

Original GHC 9.4.7 gives 14522/239 for one repetition,
72610000/1195000 for normal and 363050000/5975000 for large. Every selected counter
fits signed 31-bit integers; even a conservative ASCII upper bound for the large
checksum is 764800000. Driver counts are bounded to the selected range 0..25000.
No arbitrary-precision or floating-point arithmetic/tolerance is required.
The stable report retains the original checksum without its trailing newline.
Full final SML large repetitions remain unrecorded unless listed in validation.

### Validation and compiler behavior

Original GHC matches all FAST/NORM/SLOW fixtures. Export-only observers provide
all eight exact inferred rows, six further expressions and substitution/name/
generalization edge cases. Both ports reproduce the rows and original checksum.
Full normal private pilots also validate every row. The recorded optimized GHC
core retains the source mapping/checking pipeline; timings are not used as proof
of a particular optimization or memoization decision.

The 28-check target covers these observations, right-fold failure demand,
constructor-arity behavior, shadowed environments, occurs rejection, a skipped
later expression, memoized function substitution, quantified-variable exclusion,
zero repetitions and exact per-row validation. A deliberately changed int to nit
row has the same weak checksum and is rejected by the new validator. Native and
Rune O0/O2 canonical outcomes are recorded separately from development pilots.

### Literature and diagnostic interpretation

[Milner, A theory of type polymorphism in programming](https://doi.org/10.1016/0022-0000(78)90014-4)
(1978) supplies polymorphic-inference context; the pinned source defines this
particular implementation and ordering. No soundness theorem is inferred for
its source-specific arity/shadowing behavior.
[Hartel and Langendoen's collection paper](https://doi.org/10.1145/165180.165230)
(1993) supplies translated-benchmark context. Publisher/institution metadata and
abstracts were reviewed; this does not claim a full paper-derived proof.

Investigate higher-order substitution composition, repeated environment lookup,
type reconstruction, generalization, memoized fields, strict children and text
consumption. These are source-based questions. Exact original type agreement and
negative controls support correctness for the selected cases; measured counts
and times are distinct evidence and do not alone establish performance causes.

## dom-lt

### Algorithm and workload

Compute immediate dominators of rooted flow graphs with the source Lengauer–Tarjan
algorithm: prune unreachable nodes, renumber vertices, build predecessors, perform
DFS, update semidominators, link/compress the balanced ancestor structure and
resolve final dominators. Retain Patricia maps, 64-bit bitmap sets, mutable integer
arrays, persistent environment records and continuation/state callbacks.

### History, authorship and pinned dependencies

[The nofib dom-lt snapshot](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/spectral/dom-lt) is revision
b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798. Dom.hs credits Matt Morrow, copyright
2009, and declares BSD3, with ancestry in the dom-lt package. Its exact historical
package version is not stated; the pinned module is the program source identity.
The benchmark wrapper's individual author is unstated. Keep original Main,
Dom, Makefile and fixtures under dom-lt/upstream.

The original GHC 9.4.7 environment uses containers 0.6.7. DEPENDENCIES.json pins
its official source archive by URL/version/SHA-256; selected complete original
map/set/bit modules, package metadata and full LICENSE are retained. Their notices
credit Daan Leijen, Andriy Palamarchuk, wren romano, Joachim Breitner, Clark Gaebel
and Johan Tibel as declared in those files. Preserve these individual notices.

The fixed ghc-examples.in contains seventeen real GHC control-flow graphs,
according to the source Makefile. Its producing GHC version/program names and
individual dataset authorship/notice are not supplied. Preserve the original
CRLF bytes and unterminated last line. DATA-IDENTITIES.json records graph/reference
file hashes and lengths.

### Reviewed source repair and portable adaptations

[The source issue](validation/dom-lt-source-issue.md) proves that the pinned
kernel reuses a stale semidominator threshold and returns wrong parents on
fifteen supplied graphs. Its length-only consumer conceals the error. The port
uses the reviewed minimum-threshold correction; the exact patch, failing original
O0/O2 results and independent model remain. Corrected original and SML results
agree on all 86 checked graphs. The unrepaired source variant is deferred, with
its concrete correctness blocker and refresh condition in source-variants.tsv.

Port the required containers algorithms rather than substituting a balanced-tree
or association-list dictionary. Retain big-endian Patricia branching, strict map
insertion, bitmap-leaf union/difference/filter, signed enumeration and fold order.
Use fixed Word64 masks/leaves on every host. Portable bit-index routines replace
GHC's native bit-scan operations; finite list enumeration is strict in SML.
Original IntSet.fold is foldr; descending callback execution matters to renumbering.

Translate the continuation/state layer with an answer type specialized to this
program's pair-list result, preserving higher-order callbacks and immutable
sixteen-field environment updates. Standard SML mutable arrays replace STUArray
operations. Array.array initializes storage to zero where unsafeNewArray_ leaves
it unspecified; retain all explicit source initialization loops and document that
additional allocator cost. The standard bounds-checked API is used; compilers may eliminate proved checks. A separate semantic
instance tracks source writes and rejects uninitialized reads; instrumentation
is disabled in the measured instance. No compiler/runtime prerequisite is added.

### Inputs, profiles and consumers

| Profile | Source repetition argument | Actual full passes |
|---|---:|---:|
| Smoke | 0 | 1 |
| Normal | 400 | 401 |
| Large | 2000 | 2001 |

The source loops inclusively over 0..argument. Normal and large retain its
parameters; smoke reduces FAST's argument fifty to zero, still processing all
seventeen graphs once. Parse graph data once per Benchmark.run and retain it
through the repetition loop, as in Main. The source subset reader accepts tuple,
list and decimal-integer data with whitespace/CRLF; validate rooted closed graphs.

For each graph and pass, compare every ordered parent pair with the reviewed
corrected-original reference, then retain the source i+length result and final
sum. This adds validation to the length consumer; no explicit result cache is
introduced across passes. Source GHC disables full laziness; there is no claimed
identical portable SML optimization switch. Record compiler options and inspect
optimization effects rather than assume an exact execution count across hosts.

Reported results are 2183 for smoke, 2238783 for normal and 38385183 for large.
They match all source fixtures despite the repaired parent values. Profile graph
labels, indices and sums fit signed 31-bit arithmetic; bitmap semantics remain
explicitly 64-bit. All checking is exact, with no floating-point tolerance.
Full final SML large-profile runs remain unrecorded unless listed in validation.

### Correctness and host findings

The 119-check target covers all 86 ordered graph results with initialized-read
tracking; original containers set/map/fold observations; signed keys, bitmap bit
63, duplicate semantics and noncommutative map union; the three-node threshold
counterexample; same-length wrong-parent rejection; inclusive repetitions;
initialization negative/positive controls; invalid graphs and source checksum.

Private Rune and five native hosts pass every assertion. Native 32-bit SML/NJ
110.99.9 fails because its documented runtime Word64 shift-by-zero operation
produces the wrong bit mask. An isolated unchanged-helper probe reproduces it.
Retain actual failures and reject their measurements; do not hide them by changing
valid arithmetic. Canonical profile/engine results are recorded separately.
The source threshold defect and external host arithmetic defect are distinct.

### Literature and diagnostic interpretation

The source cites [Lengauer and Tarjan's A Fast Algorithm for Finding Dominators in
a Flowgraph](https://www.cs.princeton.edu/courses/archive/fall03/cs528/handouts/a%20fast%20algorithm%20for%20finding.pdf) (1979), Muchnick's Advanced Compiler Design and Implementation (1997)
and Brisk/Sarrafzadeh's 2007 interference-graph work. These are its declared
references, not a claim to have independently reviewed every paper. The pinned
code, minimal counterexample and model comparisons establish this repair's scope.

Investigate Patricia/bitmap operations, DFS, path compression, balanced linking,
CPS specialization, persistent environment updates, array initialization/bounds
and complete-result validation. These are source-based diagnostic questions.
Reference agreement and recorded counts/timings are separate evidence; do not
infer a compiler or collector cause from performance ratios alone.

## rewrite-lazy

### Algorithm and workload

Complete the three free-group axioms with Knuth–Bendix completion, recursive
path ordering with lexicographic extension, substitutions and unification,
critical-pair generation and a cost-sorted agenda. Index rewrite rules in the
source discrimination net. Normalize repeated queries proving
I(a*b)=I(b)*I(a). Preserve the generated ten-rule theory, equation numbers,
rule order, variable-standardization suffixes and source left-biased tactics.

### History, names and notices

[The nofib spectral/rewrite source](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/spectral/rewrite) is pinned at
b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798. Its April 23, 1991 correspondence
and Orwell heading credit Mike Spivey, Programming Research Group, University
of Oxford; the Haskell conversion is credited to partain. Preserve those
credits and the complete literate source, Makefile and fixtures. No separate
program copyright/license declaration or dataset notice is stated there;
do not invent one or infer authorship from the collection name.

The name rewrite has no collision in the pinned naming inventory, so the
ports are named rewrite-lazy and rewrite-strict. This is a free-group
completion workload, distinct from classic theorem-proving/rewriting programs
and Sandmark's separately sourced completion programs. Similar algorithm
families do not establish exact duplication.

### Translation and variant decisions

The lazy variant memoizes expression roots, finite child-list heads/spines,
substitutions, discrimination-net branches, agendas, candidate streams and
computed agenda costs. A singleton agenda need not evaluate its unused cost.
The source map/zip classification is expressed as shared lazy tagged pairs;
filter order and predicate sharing remain, while its separate Boolean-map
spine is omitted.
The strict variant forces finite expression children when their constructor
root is requested. Both retain lazy net/control roots and short-circuit
search. Lexicographic comparison skips unused tails; matching/unification
retain the source zipped-arity truncation and association-list lookup order.
Substitution composition, persistent replacement and higher-order parser/
rewriting callbacks remain. No hash-consing or union-find replacement is added.

Keep the source global completion as a shared memoized delay across queries
and repeated Benchmark.run calls. Zero queries leave both axioms and completion
undemanded. Each call constructs the source finite take/repeat query stream;
the repeated pair is shared within it. No normalized-query result cache is
introduced. Global source completion sharing is deliberate and matters to
fresh versus repeated-process measurements.

SML strings represent finite atomic names and source text, with portable
substring operations in the same backtracking parser combinators. This changes
character-list representation/allocation, not the grammar or prefix parsing.
Inactive multiset ordering and generic helpers remain in the archived source;
the benchmark uses recursive path ordering's lexicographic extension.
The source NOINLINE annotation has no claimed identical portable SML switch;
record options and investigate optimizer effects instead of asserting that all
compilers perform identical work.

### Inputs and exact checks

Smoke selects one query, reducing source FAST's 20000; normal retains 250000
and large retains 1200000. Inputs are fixed source axiom/query strings, with
no external dataset, random seed or clock-dependent stopping condition.
The driver accepts canonical decimal counts from zero through 1200000;
other arguments are outside its fixed-profile contract. Driver counts fit
signed 31-bit integers.

The source Boolean True remains the reported result. Additionally check the
entire normalized query tree on every successful repetition and the number of
observed results; an incorrect term cannot contribute a measurement.
Original GHC 9.4.7 matches all FAST/NORM/SLOW fixtures. An export-only original
observer records the complete ten-rule theory and sixteen normalization cases.
An independent signed-letter cancellation model and original normalization
agree on 128 depth-bounded generated terms (seed 19790601).

The 344-check target covers both variants: exact numbered theory, 144 full
normal forms, source substitution/matching/unification behavior, occurrences,
persistent replacement, field demand, short-circuiting, unneeded zero-query
completion and incorrect-result rejection. Native/compiler outcomes are
recorded separately from development pilots. Full final SML large repetitions
remain unrecorded unless explicitly listed in validation.

### Literature and diagnostic interpretation

[Knuth and Bendix (1970)](https://www.cs.tufts.edu/~nr/cs257/archive/don-knuth/knuth-bendix.pdf)
gives the completion/common-normal-form foundation, including group equations.
[Dershowitz (1982)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0304397582900263)
discusses orderings used to justify rewrite termination. These give context;
the pinned program determines its specific ordering extension, agenda and demand.

Spivey's preserved 1991 description establishes the program's Orwell history,
free-group problem and use of Maybe/combinators. Partain's nofib paper supplies
suite context, not measured conclusions about this port. The source defines
this particular completion strategy and ordering; exact theory and independent
normal forms support the recorded behavior.

Investigate higher-order specialization, lazy allocation/sharing, persistent
substitutions, discrimination-net traversal, backtracking parser allocation
and repeated-query optimization. These are source-based diagnostic hypotheses.
Measurements must establish their actual costs; ratios alone do not identify
a compiler or collector cause. Retain all samples and distinguish fresh runs
from repeated execution with cached completion.

## ida-lazy

### Algorithm and workload

Solve deterministically shuffled sliding-tile puzzles by the source
iterative-deepening/branch-and-bound search. Retain Manhattan bounds, forced
single moves, persistent movable/fixed tile lists, reversed hole histories,
the source best-solution tie rule and its two-level branch partitioning.
Do not substitute the independent breadth-first checker for the benchmark.

### History, authorship and variants

[The Hartel ida source](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/spectral/hartel/ida) is pinned at
b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798. No individual author or separate
program notice is stated in its generated module; preserve the complete
Main.hs, Makefile, FAST/NORM/SLOW fixtures and parent Fast2haskell shim.
The collection name alone does not establish individual program attribution.
No external dataset is required.

Names ida-lazy and ida-strict distinguish the finite tile-list policy.
Both are sequential ports of this pinned source: its sandwich helpers use
the compatibility shim's no-op miraseq, not an active parallel primitive.
No runtime/compiler prerequisite is introduced by preserving those helpers'
sequential result computation and source constructor matching.

### Translation and demand

The lazy variant memoizes finite tile-list heads/spines and their field
transformations; strict evaluates these finite lists when requested.
Coordinate pairs and bounded numeric metadata are strict SML values. Search
records, bounds, distances, board roots, solution fields, branch-control
streams and hole histories retain explicit memoized delays in both variants.

Preserve source reversed random-prefix consumption, list rotation and stable
partition ordering. Shared delayed recursive partition pairs avoid testing each tile twice;
retain the source paired-result structure rather than allocating a separate
list of tagged classifications. Keep the source right-recursive total Manhattan distance rather
than introducing a strict accumulator. The shim's fold annotations are no-ops;
best-candidate folds defer their accumulator. Do not demand a branch entry
before an already achieved cutoff, or calculate an unused pruned fold before
the source sandwich branch. Collect matches both solution constructors before
building its lazy best-state/count fields.

All arithmetic fits signed 31-bit integers for these profiles. The generator
is seed six with multiplier 4663 and modulus 46199, adding one after remainder.
Its largest intermediate product fits that bound. A hundred random shifts are
applied in the source's reversed generation order; no random-distribution or
initial tile-order replacement is made. Every repetition computes a fresh
configuration and search; no result cache across repetitions is introduced.
Read/validate arguments and the result reference once outside the loop, replacing
the original repeated getArgs lookup inside its IO repetition.

### Inputs, checks and profiles

Smoke selects one repetition at width two and height four, reducing FAST's
1500 repetitions. Normal retains 600 repetitions at width three/height four;
large retains 3000 at the same dimensions. Keep shuffle length 100, branch
delta seven and worst bound 101. These are deterministic work bounds, not
wall-clock searches. Source solutions report bound/partitions 12/13 for smoke
and 22/994 for normal and large.

Validate each original two-line result, including exact ordered shuffled tiles,
against a reviewed original reference. Additionally replay the complete solution
history, check adjacent legal moves and solved tile positions, and compare the
move count with the final bound and zero residual distance. Return repetitions
and checked source bytes instead of printing every repeated result. This
additional checker has a separate list traversal cost; the kernel remains
the original persistent list search. All checks are exact.

Original GHC 9.4.7 matches the supplied FAST/NORM/SLOW fixtures. Export-only
observers record 37 full configurations, bounds, partition counts and solution
histories. An independent model checks ordered shuffles and all legal complete
paths; independent breadth-first search verifies optimal lengths for 33 small
cases. The twelve-tile normal optimum is an original-reference agreement, not
an independently exhaustive breadth-first proof.

The 108-check target covers both variants, source observations, reversed PRNG
prefix, tie/cutoff/constructor demand, solved-state field avoidance, zero work,
finite-list policy and incorrect-result rejection. Full final SML large
repetitions remain unrecorded unless listed in validation. Private calibration
and earlier demand refinements are development scopes, separate from final
registered source identities and canonical checks.

### Literature and diagnostic interpretation

Hartel and Langendoen's 1993 collection paper supplies translated-workload
context, not individual authorship evidence or measured claims about this port.
The pinned program and shim establish the particular bound, tie, partition and
evaluation rules. Exact original paths and independent checks support the
recorded behavior.

Investigate search-tree allocation, persistent list updates, lazy finite fields,
shared classifications, higher-order candidate folds and demand at cutoffs.
These are source-based hypotheses. Counts and timings must be interpreted in
their recorded engine, instrumentation and fresh/repeated process modes; they
do not by themselves identify a compiler or collector cause.

## map_add

### Algorithm and workload

Build an integer map by inserting descending keys and values into an empty tree.

Retain the source assertion that key size is absent from the global baseline. Check every final ordered key/value and the cardinality.

The source OCaml 4.14.1 library uses height-balanced persistent binary trees,
with child heights differing by at most two. Preserve rotations, cached heights,
ordered comparisons, unchanged paths and fold/traversal order. Maps and sets
retain their distinct node payloads, rather than using one map representation
for both.

### History, variants and notices

The benchmark is selector map_add in [Sandmark's stdlib collection](https://github.com/ocaml-bench/sandmark/tree/5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507/benchmarks/stdlib),
pinned at 5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507. Its Dune source notes adaptation from OCamlPro's benchmark
repository; no individual benchmark author or separate notice is stated in the
selected .ml/.inc files. Preserve those files and the suite LICENSE.md under
map_iter/upstream. The suite notice and the separate OCaml library grant remain
separate; do not infer identical licensing for the two components.
Other selectors in this executable are separate workloads; they do not become
duplicates merely because they share a library or baseline.

The installed OCaml 4.14.1 map/set source snapshot is pinned independently by
complete-file hashes in map_iter/DEPENDENCIES.json. The library modules credit Xavier
Leroy and INRIA, copyright 1996, and declare LGPL 2.1 with the OCaml linking
exception. Complete selected .ml/.mli files, full LGPL text and the distribution's
full exception text are retained under map_iter/upstream-library. Benchmark and
library authorship are distinct. No external dataset is required.

### Translation and library adapters

Port the active integer library operations in SML97. Invoke one ordered
comparison adapter per visited node; Int.compare replaces the source integer
Ord.compare implementation. Specialized integer keys/values replace the
library's generic types. Higher-order iteration, folding, predicates and
mapping callbacks remain. No compiler/runtime prerequisite is introduced.

The portable code evaluates constructor arguments from left to right.
This can change the allocation order of the two children in a double rotation
relative to OCaml's argument evaluation; exact optimized allocation order is
compiler-dependent. Explicit source let/sequence order remains in map, iter
and fold. Tree-shape agreement establishes structure, rather than identical
allocation lifetimes.

Source physical-equality checks avoid rebuilding unchanged paths. Portable
NONE/SOME change results preserve that decision and sharing; their temporary
option allocation is an explicit representation cost. Do not use structural
tree equality or substitute a different balanced-tree algorithm. Host compilers
may optimize these temporary values differently.

Preserve the map's source tail-recursive ascending association-list generator
and global ten-thousand-entry baseline. The source fields remain global in the
portable map wrapper; a compiler may change retention through whole-program
analysis. Set construction remains inside each run, creating a thousand entries
in descending order. Do not cache a per-run set or a rebuilt map result.

Sys.opaque_identity has no claimed identical SML97 barrier. Add explicit result
consumption, callback checks and full-content checks where the source ignored a
result. This increases validation work; it does not establish identical costs
to OCaml's runtime primitives or optimizer. The common SML sources are the
standard compiler comparison.

### Fixed profiles and result checks

| Profile | Iterations | Published iterations | Expected digest |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| smoke | 1 | 1000000 | 2 |
| normal | 100000 | 1000000 | 540D6AA0 |
| large | 1000000 | 1000000 | D4B45240 |

The tree sizes remain fixed upstream parameters. Normal iteration counts are
selected explicitly for practical comparative runs, with reductions from the
published run plan shown by the retained source/configuration records. Large
is supplied only for selected selectors and uses the corresponding published
count. Smoke membership cases cross the successful/unsuccessful lookup boundary.
No universal tree-size argument replaces the source's iteration parameter.

Source fold results, keys, values and iteration controls fit signed 31-bit
integers in these profiles. The added aggregate digest uses explicit Word32
modular addition; it is a consumer/check format, not a change to source kernel
arithmetic. Check exact scalar results, expected booleans or full ordered
contents and cardinalities on each relevant result. No floating-point tolerance
is used, and incorrect contents cannot contribute measurements.

Original-library observers agree with independent sorted-map/set models on
78 operation sequences, including complete tree shapes and invariants.
Instrumented source selectors agree with independent digest models at 44
edge-count combinations and all 28 selected profiles. Observer callbacks use
Obj only in the original OCaml reference process; the runnable SML programs
require no FFI or representation inspection.

The broader semantic target checks the recorded shapes, contents, balance,
fold ordering and every selector at boundary counts. A deliberately swapped
pair of map values has the same digest and is rejected by the full checker. Recorded configuration/
profile checks are separate from private pilots. Full final SML large runs
remain unrecorded unless listed explicitly in validation.

### Literature and diagnostic interpretation

The pinned library source establishes this particular balancing, identity and
traversal policy. Sandmark's suite documentation supplies collection context.
These source inspections and original/model observations support the port;
they are not a newly claimed review of a balanced-tree paper.

Investigate comparison specialization, persistent node allocation, cached
heights, duplicate-path reuse, callback specialization, global baseline
retention and the cost of explicit consumers. Treat these as source-based
hypotheses until supported by compiler analysis or measurements. Report fresh
and repeated modes separately and retain all samples and resource failures.

### Translation and library adapters

Port the active integer library operations in SML97. Invoke one ordered
comparison adapter per visited node; Int.compare replaces the source integer
Ord.compare implementation. Specialized integer keys/values replace the
library's generic types. Higher-order iteration, folding, predicates and
mapping callbacks remain. No compiler/runtime prerequisite is introduced.

The portable code evaluates constructor arguments from left to right.
This can change the allocation order of the two children in a double rotation
relative to OCaml's argument evaluation; exact optimized allocation order is
compiler-dependent. Explicit source let/sequence order remains in map, iter
and fold. Tree-shape agreement establishes structure, rather than identical
allocation lifetimes.

NONE/SOME change results preserve that decision and sharing; their temporary
option allocation is an explicit representation cost. Do not use structural
tree equality or substitute a different balanced-tree algorithm. Host compilers
may optimize these temporary values differently.

Preserve the map's source tail-recursive ascending association-list generator
and global ten-thousand-entry baseline. The source fields remain global in the
portable map wrapper; a compiler may change retention through whole-program
analysis. Set construction remains inside each run, creating a thousand entries
in descending order. Do not cache a per-run set or a rebuilt map result.

Sys.opaque_identity has no claimed identical SML97 barrier. Add explicit result
consumption, callback checks and full-content checks where the source ignored a
result. This increases validation work; it does not establish identical costs
to OCaml's runtime primitives or optimizer. The common SML sources are the
standard compiler comparison.

## map_remove

### Algorithm and workload

Repeatedly remove the original baseline map minimum, including later absent-key attempts.

The source recomputes min_binding of the original map, so it always targets zero. After the first removal, 9999 entries remain; the tree does not empty or refresh. Preserve this behavior and check the full final range.

## bytes_blit

### Algorithm and workload

Copy thirty-two source characters into a newly filled byte destination.

The source loop starts at one. Get/set use i mod 574; sub uses i mod 572 and blit i mod 542, deliberately retaining the excluded last valid start. Smoke crosses these modulo boundaries.

### History, aliases and notices

This is selector bytes_blit in [Sandmark's stdlib collection](https://github.com/ocaml-bench/sandmark/tree/5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507/benchmarks/stdlib),
pinned at 5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507. Other selectors are separate workloads.
The Dune source credits adaptation from OCamlPro's benchmark repository;
the selected .ml/.inc files state no individual benchmark author or notice.
Preserve them and the suite Unlicense under bytes_get/upstream.

Pin OCaml 4.14.1 library source independently in bytes_get/DEPENDENCIES.json.
Bytes credits Xavier Leroy/INRIA, copyright 1996; String's implementation
credits Damien Doligez/INRIA, copyright 2014. Complete selected .ml/.mli
headers, LGPL 2.1 text and the linking exception are retained under
bytes_get/upstream-library. The library and benchmark notices are distinct.
The 574-byte Latin-like text is an embedded source literal, with no separate
dataset author or notice stated; INPUT-IDENTITY.json records its exact identity.

### Translation and variants

Use portable SML97 strings and Word8Array byte storage. Preserve operation
order, loop bounds, source text and per-call/global construction scopes.
Global text/byte input is shared; mutable bytes_set copies it per call.
No full OCaml library compatibility or identical storage/primitive cost is claimed.

Portable byte arrays may use different host packing and initialization.
Copy/sub/map use tabulation; blit/cat/concat use explicit element loops and
filled destinations in place of OCaml runtime block operations. Bytes.concat
retains one length pass and ordered segment copies. String.concat interleaves
separator list cells before the host String.concat, adding a temporary list.
String.split_on_char retains the source backward scan and empty fields.
ASCII uppercase and the exact five trim whitespace characters remain explicit.

OCaml's Sys.opaque_identity has no claimed identical SML97 barrier.
Full consumers and result checks add work and may expose constant results to
compiler specialization or hoisting. They do not establish equal work to the
original OCaml runtime. Standard comparisons use identical SML sources.

### Fixed inputs and checks

| Profile | Iterations | Published iterations | Expected count and digest |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| smoke | 575 | 2500000 | 575:1DB491D0 |
| normal | 20000 | 2500000 | 20000:4CD88C58 |

The source parameter is an operation count; input text remains fixed.
Normal reductions and selected large counts are explicit rather than a
universal size argument. Full final large SML runs are unrecorded unless
listed separately in validation.

Check every scalar, complete produced string/byte sequence or split word list.
bytes_set additionally checks every final byte. FNV-1a-style Word32 mixing
consumes the checked observations; it is an added modular result format,
not source kernel arithmetic. Counts and source character operations fit
signed 31-bit integers. No floating-point tolerance applies.

### Validation and runtime concerns

Original OCaml function observers and independent byte/word models agree on
100 edge-count results and all 55 selected profiles. Observer-only hooks
capture discarded blit/callback results without adding an FFI requirement to
the SML program. The semantic target checks overlapping copies, isolation,
trim/ASCII behavior, empty split fields, cyclic boundaries, all selectors,
unchanged global input and rejection of corrupt character/final-array results.
Private pilot evidence and canonical wrapper checks have separate scopes.

### Literature and diagnostic interpretation

The preserved benchmark and OCaml library sources establish these algorithms
and adaptations. Original observations and independent models establish the
reviewed expected results. No separate string-algorithm paper review is claimed.
Packing, bounds checks, byte/string conversions, callback specialization,
temporary allocation, source barriers and the added complete consumers are
performance questions inferred from source; timing alone does not isolate them.

## string_sub

### Algorithm and workload

Copy two characters at cyclic source positions.

## str_regexp

### Algorithm and workload

Compile the original nonempty literal regular expression on each iteration.

Preserve test_regex Novum Site and the exact 574-byte source text. The source
starts its loop at one. Compile on every iteration only for str_regexp;
other selectors compile once per call. str_split uses @ instead of test_regex.
The fixed text starts with In, so both initial-match selectors return false.
Forward search finds position 274; replacement substitutes that ten-byte phrase.

### History, variants and notices

Selector str_regexp comes from [Sandmark stdlib](https://github.com/ocaml-bench/sandmark/tree/5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507/benchmarks/stdlib),
pinned at 5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507. These are separate configured selectors, not duplicates.
The Dune source credits adaptation from OCamlPro's repository; the individual
source states no author or separate notice. Preserve it, str.inc and the
Sandmark Unlicense in str_regexp/upstream.

Pin the OCaml 4.14.1 Str implementation, interface, C matcher and full LICENSE
independently under str_regexp/upstream-library; DEPENDENCIES.json records their
identities. Those sources credit Xavier Leroy/INRIA, copyright 1996, under
LGPL 2.1 with the linking exception. The original Str engine and benchmark
notices are distinct. The input literal and its attribution limits are recorded
with bytes_get/string_get; no external dataset is required.

### Translation decisions

Reuse the suite's portable regex adapter, with literal compilation, ordered
matching, leftmost search and nonempty constant replacement. Add a
literal-sequence partial matcher, source-style split control and explicit
last-match position state. Partial matching succeeds when text ends at a
matching prefix. Split removes one leading delimiter match and a trailing
empty field while preserving empty fields between adjacent single delimiters.
No full Str API, captures, backreferences or empty-pattern support is claimed.

OCaml's internal bytecode engine, native matcher and packed regexp representation
are replaced by SML expression lists and substring indices. Explicit position
vectors represent the source last-search-result array. Preserve compile/call
scopes and search/replace order; record this library replacement when comparing
implementations. No FFI or compiler/runtime prerequisite is introduced.

### Inputs and correctness

| Profile | Iterations | Published iterations | Expected count and digest |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| smoke | 1 | 1000000 | 1:F5C2FBE8 |
| normal | 20000 | 1000000 | 20000:432E51A5 |

Counts are explicitly selected source parameters; input text and expressions
remain fixed. Normal reductions and selected large counts are documented.
Full final large SML repetitions remain unrecorded unless listed separately.

Check exact booleans/positions, complete replaced text and split lists.
Compiled regex consumers inspect the complete portable literal representation.
Added Word32 mixing consumes the checked observations. Original compile
observers verify matching behavior and source compile counts without claiming
an identical internal regexp representation. Added consumers and the missing
identical Sys.opaque_identity barrier can affect specialization or hoisting.

### Recorded and planned validation

Original OCaml functions agree with independent literal models on eighteen
edge-count and fourteen selected profile results. Twenty-one further original
library observations cover complete/partial matches, offsets, absent/overlapping
searches, repeated replacement and split boundaries. The 42-check target also
rejects a corrupt position and a negative partial-match index. Canonical wrapper
results are distinguished from private pilots in the validation ledger.

### Literature and diagnostic interpretation

The preserved Str implementation establishes the original call scopes and
split/match state behavior. The suite regex adapter documentation describes
its bounded replacement. Original observations and independent literal models
support correctness. No separate regex-engine paper review is claimed.
Compilation, literal scanning, result-vector allocation, substring copying and
consumer specialization are source-based performance hypotheses; measurements
do not isolate the cost of an individual mechanism.
