## int_find1

### Algorithm and workload

Run inclusive batches of lookups in the original empty generic integer-key table.

Preserve source bucket insertion, first-binding replacement/removal, duplicate
entries, three unrolled lookup comparisons, ascending bucket traversal and
growth when binding count exceeds twice the bucket count. Initial capacity is
the power of two at least sixteen and at least the requested size. Resizing
retains bucket-chain order, tail arrays and the traversal-dependent choice
between reusing cells and copying them.

### History, variants and notices

Selector int_find1 is from [Sandmark stdlib](https://github.com/ocaml-bench/sandmark/tree/5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507/benchmarks/stdlib),
pinned at 5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507. The source notes adaptation from OCamlPro's repository;
no individual benchmark author or separate notice is stated. Preserve the
benchmark, build include and Sandmark Unlicense under hashtbl_iter/upstream.

Pin OCaml 4.14.1 hashtbl.ml/.mli, runtime/hash.c and full LICENSE under
hashtbl_iter/upstream-library, with complete identities in DEPENDENCIES.json.
The selected library/runtime headers credit Xavier Leroy/INRIA, copyright
1996, and declare LGPL 2.1 with the linking exception. hash.c identifies its
MurmurHash3 ancestry. Library/runtime and benchmark notices remain separate.
There is no external dataset.

### Translation and numeric decisions

Use SML97 mutable bucket links, arrays and callbacks. Refs replace inline
mutable OCaml fields, adding allocation/indirection; equal integer keys are
immutable because replacement cannot change an equal integer's value.
Specialize key equality/comparison to integers. Preserve traversal flags and
restore them on exceptions. No FFI or compiler/runtime feature is required.

Generic key hashing retains the exact tagged-integer MurmurHash3 mixing,
tuple header, field order, final avalanche and nonnegative thirty-bit result.
Explicit Word32 operations preserve modular arithmetic. The two known domains
specialize away the generic C runtime object queue, object tags and count/limit
dispatch; no identical generic hashing primitive or runtime overhead is claimed.
The specialized IntHash path uses low key bits at the table mask, preserving
the source key-and-max_int result for these indices. Randomized tables are not
part of this deterministic seed-zero workload.

Only filter_map values use IntInf with explicit signed 63-bit modular doubling,
matching the pinned 64-bit OCaml semantics even on 31-bit SML hosts. This changes
numeric representation and allocation costs; it does not substitute unbounded
mathematical growth for wrapping arithmetic. Other source counters/keys/values
fit signed 31-bit integers in the selected profiles. Added result mixing uses
Word32 independently of source arithmetic.

### Source quirks, inputs and correctness

Main's generic and specialized tables are created empty before dispatch.
The find1/find2 selectors do not invoke their sibling replace closures, so every
lookup misses. Replace closures fill zero through 999 on the first batch and
reuse those tables on subsequent calls. These four selectors and both hash
selectors run outer loops from zero through iterations inclusive: zero still
performs a thousand operations. Other operation loops start at one.

Remove always performs iterations div 1000 + 1 complete build/remove batches.
Filter_map retains a thousand entries; signed overflow and eventual zero
values are part of the source workload. Find crosses the populated 1..1000
range. Duplicate insertion retains both bindings rather than overwriting one.

| Profile | Iterations | Published iterations | Expected count and digest |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| smoke | 0 | 20000 | 0:6D0D00D7 |
| normal | 1000 | 20000 | 1000:E92AE3F7 |

Profiles select explicit source counts; they do not change the thousand-entry
baselines or use a universal size argument. Normal reductions and selected
large counts are recorded. Full final large SML runs remain unrecorded unless
listed separately in validation.

Full binding multiplicities, values and cardinalities are checked after builds;
lookups, fold scalars and callback counts are checked as consumed. Filter_map
checks every final signed value. Hash consumers use the reviewed original
results and independent modular model. Extra full consumers, reference cells,
domain specialization and absence of an identical Sys.opaque_identity barrier
are explicit adaptations.

### Validation evidence

Original snapshots and independent duplicate-binding models cover 23 update
sequences, including resizing and signed keys. Exact original bucket layouts
before/after filtering and 1005 integer/tuple hash pairs support the port.
Original source observers and independent iteration/binding/modular models
agree on 56 edge-count cases and all 33 selected profiles. Tests cover the
unrolled lookup tail, exact traversal order across callback-triggered resizing,
duplicate removal, exception restoration, corrupted
bindings and both signed63 boundary transitions. The validation ledger separates
private pilots from canonical wrapper checks and resource failures.

### Literature and diagnostic interpretation

Preserved OCaml source establishes these bucket and hash algorithms; its
MurmurHash3 pointer records ancestry rather than a newly claimed paper review.
Independent models and exact source observations support correctness.
Bucket distribution, resize/cell reuse, indirect mutable fields, key/hash
specialization, tagged arithmetic and added consumers are source-based
performance questions. Recorded counts and timings do not isolate their costs.

no individual benchmark author or separate notice is stated. Preserve the
benchmark, build include and Sandmark Unlicense under hashtbl_iter/upstream.

Pin OCaml 4.14.1 hashtbl.ml/.mli, runtime/hash.c and full LICENSE under
hashtbl_iter/upstream-library, with complete identities in DEPENDENCIES.json.
The selected library/runtime headers credit Xavier Leroy/INRIA, copyright
1996, and declare LGPL 2.1 with the linking exception. hash.c identifies its
MurmurHash3 ancestry. Library/runtime and benchmark notices remain separate.
There is no external dataset.

### Translation and numeric decisions

Use SML97 mutable bucket links, arrays and callbacks. Refs replace inline
mutable OCaml fields, adding allocation/indirection; equal integer keys are
immutable because replacement cannot change an equal integer's value.
Specialize key equality/comparison to integers. Preserve traversal flags and
restore them on exceptions. No FFI or compiler/runtime feature is required.

Generic key hashing retains the exact tagged-integer MurmurHash3 mixing,
tuple header, field order, final avalanche and nonnegative thirty-bit result.
Explicit Word32 operations preserve modular arithmetic. The two known domains
specialize away the generic C runtime object queue, object tags and count/limit
dispatch; no identical generic hashing primitive or runtime overhead is claimed.
The specialized IntHash path uses low key bits at the table mask, preserving
the source key-and-max_int result for these indices. Randomized tables are not
part of this deterministic seed-zero workload.

Only filter_map values use IntInf with explicit signed 63-bit modular doubling,
matching the pinned 64-bit OCaml semantics even on 31-bit SML hosts. This changes
numeric representation and allocation costs; it does not substitute unbounded
mathematical growth for wrapping arithmetic. Other source counters/keys/values
fit signed 31-bit integers in the selected profiles. Added result mixing uses
Word32 independently of source arithmetic.

### Source quirks, inputs and correctness

Main's generic and specialized tables are created empty before dispatch.
The find1/find2 selectors do not invoke their sibling replace closures, so every
lookup misses. Replace closures fill zero through 999 on the first batch and
reuse those tables on subsequent calls. These four selectors and both hash
selectors run outer loops from zero through iterations inclusive: zero still
performs a thousand operations. Other operation loops start at one.

Remove always performs iterations div 1000 + 1 complete build/remove batches.
Filter_map retains a thousand entries; signed overflow and eventual zero
values are part of the source workload. Find crosses the populated 1..1000
range. Duplicate insertion retains both bindings rather than overwriting one.

| Profile | Iterations | Published iterations | Expected count and digest |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| smoke | 33 | 6000000 | 33:E705E1E5 |
| normal | 100000 | 6000000 | 100000:D04873FF |
| large | 1000000 | 6000000 | 1000000:5DBEAE5F |

Profiles select explicit source counts; they do not change the thousand-entry
baselines or use a universal size argument. Normal reductions and selected
large counts are recorded. Full final large SML runs remain unrecorded unless
listed separately in validation.

Full binding multiplicities, values and cardinalities are checked after builds;
lookups, fold scalars and callback counts are checked as consumed. Filter_map
checks every final signed value. Hash consumers use the reviewed original
results and independent modular model. Extra full consumers, reference cells,
domain specialization and absence of an identical Sys.opaque_identity barrier
are explicit adaptations.

### Validation evidence

Original snapshots and independent duplicate-binding models cover 23 update
sequences, including resizing and signed keys. Exact original bucket layouts
before/after filtering and 1005 integer/tuple hash pairs support the port.
Original source observers and independent iteration/binding/modular models
agree on 56 edge-count cases and all 33 selected profiles. Tests cover the
unrolled lookup tail, exact traversal order across callback-triggered resizing,
duplicate removal, exception restoration, corrupted
bindings and both signed63 boundary transitions. The validation ledger separates
private pilots from canonical wrapper checks and resource failures.

### Literature and diagnostic interpretation

Preserved OCaml source establishes these bucket and hash algorithms; its
MurmurHash3 pointer records ancestry rather than a newly claimed paper review.
Independent models and exact source observations support correctness.
Bucket distribution, resize/cell reuse, indirect mutable fields, key/hash
specialization, tagged arithmetic and added consumers are source-based
performance questions. Recorded counts and timings do not isolate their costs.

## lexifi-g2pp

### Algorithm and workload

Calibrate the source five-parameter G2++ model against its 196 embedded
swaption quotes. Retain Gregorian-minute dates, fixed schedules, the
error-function approximation, Brent-style root search, eleven-point Gaussian
quadrature and differential-evolution least-squares optimization. Each
calibration creates its pricer closures and mutable work arrays; do not cache
a completed calibration across Benchmark.run calls.

### History, aliases and notices

[LexiFi's Sandmark workload](https://github.com/ocaml-bench/sandmark/tree/5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507/benchmarks/lexifi-g2pp),
pinned at 5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507, credits LexiFi SAS, copyright 2000-2013, under GPL version
3 or later. Preserve all selected .ml/.mli files, README, Dune, output fixture
and COPYING under upstream. The supplied 196 quote records remain in source
order. No separate quote-provider credit or dataset notice is stated there;
the fixture is historical input rather than current market data.

The executable main.exe is named lexifi-g2pp by its established collection
name. It is distinct from unrelated main executables. The source README
describes a stripped-down calibration application; do not replace it with a
small root-finding or optimizer-only kernel.

### Translation, parameters and numeric behavior

Use portable SML97 records, arrays, closures, exceptions and default binary64
reals. Read-only schedule/quadrature/quote containers use vectors; mutable
population and pricer arrays retain their update scopes and ordering.
Methods of the OCaml modules become explicit SML structures and functions.
The fixed Random.State.make [|0|] state is independently observed and stored as
55 initial words; all subsequent source draws, rejection loops and their order
remain in the common OCaml-random adapter. Precomputation replaces the source
seed-expansion work, not the generated sequence.

Preserve tuple/right-operand order where callbacks affect observations.
Original observations establish initial Brent evaluation order and complete
sphere-optimizer improvement traces. Population mutation/recombination order,
strict improvements, source best/random base selection and inclusive stopping
conditions remain. A full generation precedes the maxf < ncalls check:
the published budget 2000 finishes at 2040 evaluations.

The source black_price variable sqrtt contains a year fraction without a
square root; preserve its actual expression. Source date division truncates
toward zero, including negative-epoch helper observations. Profiles retain
today 2012-01-01 and finite bounded dates. Integer calculations fit signed
31-bit values; floating operations remain binary64. Source feedback text and
optional OCAML_GC_STATS file output are suppressed; complete checked numerical
results replace rounded progress printing. No compiler/runtime prerequisite
is introduced.

### Fixed inputs and result checks

| Profile | Evaluation-budget parameter | View of the source workload |
|---|---:|---|
| Smoke | 40 | All 196 quotes; reduced optimizer budget. |
| Normal | 2000 | Original published budget and quote set. |
| Large | 20000 | Explicit optimizer scaling selection; same quotes. |

The parameter is the source optimizer budget, not a universal data size.
Profiles include reviewed reference files containing all five parameters,
RMS, and every calibrated/market price pair. All values must be finite.
Parameters use 1e-8 absolute plus 1e-8 relative error; RMS uses 1e-7 absolute
plus 1e-8 relative error; both price arrays use 1e-9 absolute plus 1e-8
relative error. The shared price bound is much narrower than the original
0.01/10000 printed-price resolution. CDF support observations use 1e-10
absolute plus relative tolerance; exact dates, counters and draw sequences
remain exact.

Original export-only observers supply full precision, and a separate model
recomputes RMS from all 196 price pairs. Independent calendar differences,
erf/square-root observations and original optimizer traces support smaller
components. Checker controls reject two-bound perturbations, NaN, infinity,
wrong model parameters and wrong RMS; small roundoff remains accepted.
Raw original stdout is preserved separately from the full-precision oracle.

### Compiler/runtime behavior and validation

Investigate closure specialization, shared scratch arrays, transcendental
operations, root-search branches, numeric boxing and population updates.
These are source-based questions rather than attributed timing explanations.
Compare identical SML sources on the standard host set; use OCaml as an
independent correctness reference.

The private Rune smoke and original normal-budget pilot validates complete
results. Final semantic probes distinguish the known native 32-bit SML/NJ
bounded-random Overflow from legacy 64-bit numerical/GC failures. Five
default legacy diagnostics fail and five 64 MiB nursery diagnostics pass;
this is consistent with the existing GC report, not a causal reduction or a
changed suite default. SML/NJ 2026.2 passes the uniform price bounds. Retain
all default failures and exclude incorrect results from measurements.
The initial tighter market-price-only bound and optional diagnostics remain
development evidence. Full final SML large runs remain unrecorded unless
listed explicitly in the validation ledger.

### Literature and evidence scope

[Storn and Price (1997)](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1023/A:1008202821328),
publisher abstract inspected, supplies global-optimization context.
[Brigo and Mercurio, second edition](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-540-34604-3),
publisher metadata inspected, records 2006; the source comment gives 2005.
No full article/book derivation review is claimed. Preserved source, independent
numerical observations and measured validation results remain distinct from
these literature anchors and from performance hypotheses.

## contrast

### Algorithm and workload

Run the eight source image contrast pipelines in their original order:
adaptive contrast spreading; Niblack global RGB, local RGB and local monochrome;
Sauvola global RGB, global monochrome, local RGB and local monochrome.
Each method receives the same original RGB image and builds a fresh output.
Do not combine the passes or substitute integral-image statistics.

### History, names and notices

[Sandmark sauvola/contrast.exe](https://github.com/ocaml-bench/sandmark/tree/5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507/benchmarks/sauvola),
pinned at 5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507, credits Andreas Romeyke, copyright 2009-2012,
under GPL version 2 or later. contrast is the executable name; Sauvola and
Niblack describe constituent algorithm families, not duplicate executables.
Preserve contrast.ml, its build files and complete LICENSE.

The input derives from the source example2_small.ppm, 267 by 200 RGB pixels.
The individual image states no separate author or dataset notice; record this
attribution limit alongside its pinned source path and original byte hash.
The JPEG example is an alternative encoding, not a separate runnable workload.

CamlImages 5.0.4 is pinned independently by archive SHA-256 in
LIBRARY-ARCHIVE.json. Selected source headers credit Francois Pessaux, Pierre
Weis and Jun Furuse/INRIA, copyright 1999-2004. Preserve those full headers and
License.txt, which supplies Library GPL version 2 and its linking exception.
The OCaml 4.14.1 hash adapter has its separate LGPL 2.1/linking-exception notices
under hashtbl_iter/upstream-library. Do not conflate these grants with the
contrast program's GPL notice.

### Portable translation and source variants

Use SML97 Word8Array RGB storage, records, loops, arrays, memoized thresholds
and portable PPM I/O. The original reference builds against pinned CamlImages
core with PPM support; the unused external image formats are not prerequisites
of the SML program. No FFI/compiler/runtime feature is introduced.

Contiguous byte storage replaces CamlImages' managed block storage. Subimages
are still materialized and RGB records are still returned from pixel reads.
Additional initialization, record construction and SML library costs are explicit.
Pixel brightness retains the active integer weights (54R+182G+19B)/255.
The source statistics scan columns before rows. Three squared sums use IntInf
to preserve source 64-bit integer values on 31-bit hosts; other selected integer
operations fit signed 31-bit values. Exact truncating division remains explicit.

Keep the source window radius fifteen, RGB subimage upper-border exclusion,
monochrome inclusive windows and rolling cache update, retained cache counts,
strict comparisons and bright-pixel skips. Preserve the distinct global and
local Sauvola formulas and constants. They are literal source variants rather
than claimed canonical formulas from a paper.

Threshold memoization retains one 1024-bucket table per method call, first-match
lookup and the source rule that the next miss clears a table with more than
1000 bindings. At most 1001 entries are possible, so table resizing and traversal
mutation are unreachable in this fragment. Integer/float tuple hashing retains
tag/header order, Murmur mixing, signed-zero and NaN normalization. Optional
packed-real structure names differ across hosts; a common SML97 binary64-word
encoder replaces the native reinterpretation. This adds arithmetic/conversion
cost and is explicitly a library representation adapter.

### Fixed profiles, input conversion and validation

| Profile | Image | Origin |
|---|---|---|
| Smoke | 32 by 32 | Original crop at (0,0). |
| Normal | 64 by 48 | Original crop at (40,40). |
| Large | 267 by 200 | Complete original image. |

Profiles select input files, retaining the source image parameter rather than
a universal size argument. A portable SML generator re-encodes pixels as ASCII
P3. Independent byte comparisons establish exact RGB preservation and crop
coordinates; the original OCaml program produces identical complete-image
outputs from P3 and P6. Encoding changes I/O cost, not pixel values.
INPUT-IDENTITIES.json records original/converted data and RGB identities.

Validate every RGB channel of all eight complete binary output images, with
exact geometry and reviewed zero/255 reference bits. No floating tolerance
is applied to these final discrete values. Additional checker work replaces
source progress/timing output and eight PPM filesystem writes. Returned
dimensions/pass counts consume only fully checked outputs.

Original reference programs establish all profile rasters, 81 float-pair hash
values and memo hit/clear traces. An independent bit/Murmur model agrees with
those hashes. Tests cover cache sharing, source window edges, brightness
weights, copy isolation, invalid colors, corrupted output, wrong reference
lengths and nonbinary reference data. The smoke and normal Rune pilots match
all eight original rasters; final configuration evidence and large runs are
recorded separately.

### Compiler/runtime behavior

Investigate repeated subimage allocation, boxed versus packed channel access,
wide squared-sum arithmetic, real-key encoding, memo collisions/clearing,
cache reuse and branch behavior on bright pixels. Source inspection motivates
these questions. Recorded measurements do not attribute individual costs.
The common SML sources are the standard compiler comparison; OCaml remains
a correctness reference.

### Literature and evidence scope

[Sauvola and Pietikainen (2000)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0031320399000552),
publisher abstract and opening material inspected, supplies adaptive document
binarization context. The source additionally cites Niblack (1986) and
Sezgin/Sankur (2004); these are declared references, not newly claimed full
reviews. The particular eight formulas, window boundaries and caches come
from source inspection. Original raster/hash observations and independent
models support the translation; performance explanations remain hypotheses.

## minilight

### Algorithm and workload

Render the original roomfront triangle scene with sequential Monte Carlo
path tracing, emitter samples, Russian-roulette reflection, an octree and
progressive RGB accumulation. Preserve camera jitter, shadow rays, triangle
tests, material/sky handling and the source image tone-map/gamma/quantizer.
The complete application remains, rather than a triangle-intersection kernel.

### History, aliases and notices

[Sandmark's sequential MiniLight](https://github.com/ocaml-bench/sandmark/tree/5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507/benchmarks/multicore-minilight/sequential),
pinned at 5605805954a00497ed197c930641cddd580e1507, identifies MiniLight 1.5.2 OCaml and credits Harrison
Ainsworth/HXA7241, copyright 2006-2008. Preserve all modules, original CRLF
roomfront.ml.txt, build files and the BSD three-clause LICENSE.txt.
The individual scene states no separate author or dataset notice.
Later author-site downloads advertise CC0; that does not replace the notice
on this pinned historical source.

The sequential program contains no Domain/Task call. Its unused Dune
domainslib link dependency is omitted; the original also builds with plain
ocamlopt. Parallel MiniLight variants retain their separate feature-policy
disposition and are not silently represented by this sequential executable.

### Translation, demand and numeric decisions

Use SML97 RealArray three-vectors and ordinary arrays for vertex/frame/item
containers and image pixels. Records/datatypes/functions replace objects and
method dispatch. Explicit per-frame tracer environments and surface records
retain their construction scopes. Triangle identity uses a unique reference;
equal geometry does not make two triangles the same last-hit object.

Normal, tangent and area retain separate memoized delays. Original Lazy.is_val
observations establish their independent forcing order; repeated forces share
the result. Keep source octree depth/leaf limits, bounds/tolerances, stable
item order, subdivision controls and nearest-hit tie decisions.

Original observations establish OCaml's evaluation order. Preserve stochastic
tuple draws explicitly: camera y before x, triangle r2 before sqrt(r1), and
hemisphere radius before angle. Simultaneous let-and groups remain left first.
Pure operand/constructor allocation order and temporary representation can
differ under SML evaluation; record this when interpreting allocation costs.
The fixed Random.State.make [|1|] state is precomputed as 55 words; subsequent
draws and rejection logic use the common unchanged OCaml-random adapter.

Model parsing uses portable text tokens instead of Scanf; selected coordinates,
materials, light and camera values remain unchanged. Default reals are binary64
on the configured hosts. Selected indices/frame counts fit signed 31-bit
integers. No parallelism, FFI or compiler/runtime prerequisite is introduced.

### Fixed profiles, deterministic checkpoints and checks

| Profile | Frames | Viewport | Original scene |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Smoke | 1 | 8 by 5 | Unchanged geometry/material/light/camera records. |
| Normal | 2 | 81 by 50 | Unchanged scene; original 1.62 aspect ratio. |
| Large | 4 | 162 by 100 | Unchanged scene; original 1.62 aspect ratio. |

The source model requests 100 frames at 324 by 200. These are explicit smaller
frame/viewport selections, not a universal size loop. A portable SML generator
replaces only those header parameters and retains the original geometry suffix.
Input identities and original references accompany the profiles.

Replace wall-clock periodic saves with deterministic first/last-frame
checkpoints, merging them for a one-frame run. This retains the source start/
end image work without clock-dependent extra saves. Intermediate files and UI
progress are suppressed; both complete checkpoint images are consumed and
checked. The stopping rule remains a fixed frame count.

References contain every first/final linear RGB accumulation, both complete
quantized rasters and the exact final 55-word random state/index. Linear values
must be finite and within 1e-8 absolute plus 1e-8 relative error; quantized bytes,
header, geometry and random state are exact. Incorrect output contributes no
measurement. Original export-only observations agree byte-for-byte with the
unmodified executable's final P6 images. The initial exploratory byte tolerance
was tightened to exact equality before final validation.

### Validation and compiler/runtime interpretation

The private Rune smoke/normal pilots validate complete original results.
Controls cover demand sharing, exception caching, independent geometry identity,
known intersections, parallel misses, octree last-hit handling, numerical
perturbations, NaN, wrong byte/length and all source geometry forcing states.
Native 32-bit SML/NJ retains the known bounded-random Overflow; do not rewrite
its arithmetic or accept an alternate result.

Investigate method/closure specialization, vector and temporary allocation,
memoized geometry, octree traversal, object identity, random draws, recursion
and tone-map operations. These are source-based hypotheses; measurements alone
do not identify their individual costs. Complete target/profile outcomes and
full large-run coverage are recorded separately.

### Literature and evidence scope

[The author's description](https://www.hxa.name/minilight/), algorithm section
inspected, supplies renderer context and identifies its sampling, spatial
index and tone-mapping components. The current page and historical source have
different release/license contexts, recorded above.

[Moller and Trumbore (1997)](https://my.eng.utah.edu/~cs6965/papers/MT97.pdf),
abstract and opening page inspected, describes finding ray distance and
triangle coordinates without storing plane equations. This is an algorithm
anchor rather than a full review of its performance claims. The port's actual
tolerances, octree, sampling order and demand policy come from source analysis
and original/model observations.

## sched-lazy

### Algorithm and workload

Enumerate the source non-delay schedules of fork/join job graphs on two
simulated processors. Preserve job phases, owner affinity for joins, processor/
queue reversal, all allocation alternatives, event-step advancement and the
source zero-sentinel minimum. This is sequential simulation and search, with
no operating-system parallelism.

### History, naming and notices

[The nofib Hartel sched source](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/spectral/hartel/sched)
is pinned at b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798. Its generated Main.hs states no individual author
or separate program license. Preserve the complete source, Makefile, original
FAST/NORM/SLOW fixtures and parent Fast2haskell shim. Collection attribution
does not establish an individual program author.

sched-lazy and sched-strict retain the established sched name and distinguish
finite data policies. They are not duplicates of a task scheduler using real
threads. The shim's miraseq is a no-op; sandwich metadata are never demanded.
No compiler/runtime prerequisite is introduced.

### Translation, sharing and variants

Explicit memoized delays preserve the search tree and its branch-control
structure in both variants. Finite job definitions/status fields, processor
records and list heads/spines use lazy or strict policies. Global definitions
and the initial processors remain shared across repetitions; each search is
fresh. Strict initialization forces the finite definition graphs, while lazy
initialization demands only reachable fields. The 55 named definitions are
emitted in dependency order to express source forward references in SML.

The existing reviewed finite-list support from IDA is reused. Paired outputs
of selection/processing remain shared, with separate memoized projections.
Keep unused processor IDs, parents, join durations and child selectors pending
in the lazy policy. Preserve empty/phase-one short circuits and no-op sandwich
hint demand, including in the strict finite variant. Bounded numeric search
controls are strict SML values; hint expressions retain explicit delays.

Original graph labels are selectors, not a recomputed node count: the inputs
labelled ten and fourteen contain nine and thirteen defined jobs respectively.
Keep their actual topology, durations and IDs. All selected kernel arithmetic
fits signed 31-bit integers. Added observation totals use IntInf and ordered
tree hashes use Word32. No floating tolerance is involved.

### Fixed profiles and correctness

| Profile | Repetitions | Source graph selector | Checked minimum cycles |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Smoke | 1 | 3 | 60 |
| Normal | 100 | 11 | 218 |
| Large | 1 | 14 | 267 |

Smoke reduces the source FAST 200-by-10 setting. Normal retains its original
100-by-11 setting. Selected large studies the larger supplied search tree;
the original SLOW 500-by-11 fixture is retained as a separate scale reference.
Preserve independent repetition and graph parameters, rather than introducing
a universal size argument.

Each repetition checks the exact minimum against reviewed original and
independent values. The source ASCII sumcode is not the sole oracle: different
numbers can share it. The driver returns the count and sum of verified minima,
suppresses repeated stdout and reads arguments once outside the loop instead
of repeated getArgs. Zero repetitions leave search computation undemanded.

Original export-only observers record complete tree counts, min/max/sums and
ordered hashes at 23 graph/threshold combinations. The larger labelled graph
has 287625 leaves. An independent event/DAG model with affinity and non-delay
assignment agrees on all seven supplied graphs, using state memoization rather
than the benchmark's schedule tree. Full-tree observations validate the port's
ordering separately from minimum agreement.

### Compiler/runtime behavior and validation

Investigate persistent list rebuilding, paired-result sharing, suspended finite
fields, search-tree lifetimes, branch choices, closure specialization and
strict versus delayed initialization. These are source-based hypotheses until
supported by source-level compiler analysis or separate measurements.

The semantic target compares original tree observations across both policies
and checks unused fields, sharing, no-op hints, zero work and incorrect-minimum
rejection. Rune normal pilots retain the original 100 repetitions. Source-order
setup diagnostics remain separate from final checks; full configuration and
selected large coverage are recorded explicitly in the validation ledger.

### Literature and evidence scope

[Hartel and Langendoen (1993)](https://doi.org/10.1145/165180.165230), collection
metadata/abstract reviewed in the initial survey, supplies translation context.
The pinned program establishes this particular scheduling policy and data;
the independent DAG oracle does not replace its enumerating algorithm.
Original and independent results establish correctness, while performance
mechanism claims remain hypotheses.

## wave4main-lazy

### Algorithm and workload

Evolve the source staggered u/v/height arrays with the original finite-difference
updates, splitting them into two spatial regions and exchanging boundary
columns. Retain all six array domains, U-then-V-then-height dependencies,
physical constants, update parentheses and boundary guards. Do not substitute
the independent unsplit-grid checker for this workload.

### History, names and notices

[nofib Hartel wave4main](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/spectral/hartel/wave4main)
is pinned at b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798. The generated module states no individual author or
separate program notice. Preserve complete Main.hs, Makefile, original fixtures
and the parent Fast2haskell shim; collection credits do not establish individual
authorship. No external dataset is required.

The -lazy/-strict names distinguish finite array/cell/triple policy. Both are
sequential computations of this pinned source; the boundary decomposition
does not introduce parallel execution or a runtime prerequisite.

### Translation, numeric semantics and demand

Represent immutable indexed boxed arrays with bounded vectors of delayed
cells. The same SML97 adapter runs on all hosts. Direct vector construction
replaces the shim's Data.Array association-list construction bridge; this
changes temporary builder allocation and is a library replacement. Bounds and
small structural descriptors are strict metadata. Prepend/append retain
original indices and build separate immutable border views at source call
sites.

The lazy policy memoizes outer triples, arrays, rows and real cells. The strict
policy materializes these finite values. Global initial fields are shared;
every requested solution performs fresh step evolution. Keep the U i=0/8 and
V j=0/8 guards before neighbor reads, including for strict data. Source zero
boundaries must not access out-of-range arrays.

Default floating values are binary64 on the configured hosts. Preserve
right-associated Coriolis sums and source multiply/divide grouping. Initial
height remains 3*i/7, depth thirty and the source fixed constants. Selected
indices/counts/checksum totals fit signed 31-bit integers. No substitute
numeric representation or arbitrary-precision kernel is introduced.

### Inputs, profiles and checks

| Profile | Repetitions | Time steps | Source setting |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Smoke | 1 | 8 | FAST steps, reducing its fixed 500 repetitions. |
| Normal | 500 | 80 | Original normal setting. |
| Large | 500 | 400 | Original slow setting. |

Preserve repetition count and time steps separately, rather than a universal
size. Reference files record exact domains and every final value in all six
arrays, totaling 208 values. Require finite values within 1e-10 absolute plus
1e-10 relative error, then retain the original 1465-character output formatter
and exact source sumcode. The additional full numeric traversal precedes
formatting and adds validation/retention work; the coarse source checksum is
not the sole oracle.

The source five-character formatting, sign handling, rounding and overflow
stars remain. Each repetition verifies a fresh solution and consumes its
formatted result; the driver suppresses repeated stdout and returns checked
repetition/value counts. Argument/reference reads move outside the repetition
loop, replacing repeated getArgs. Host optimization of pure strict computations
is a diagnostic question, not a claimed identical opaque barrier.

Original observers record nine complete states through 400 steps, including
all bounds and source checksums. An independent full-grid implementation,
with no split/halo representation, agrees on all 1872 observed values.
Tests cover full states in both policies, memoized cells, strict materialization,
halo indices, boundary demand, out-of-range access, numerical perturbation/NaN,
corrupt values, zero work and reference-step mismatches.

### Compiler/runtime behavior and recorded validation

Investigate boxed versus specialized cells, delayed history retention, boundary
views, tuple/array materialization, closure specialization, arithmetic and
additional consumers. These are source-based hypotheses, not individual
performance attributions from timing alone.

Private normal pilots retain all 500 repetitions in both policies and match
complete original numerical/format results. The semantic target passes on the
configured engines/hosts; canonical profile outcomes and final large runs
are recorded separately. No new compiler or runtime feature is included.

### Literature and evidence scope

[Hartel and Langendoen (1993)](https://doi.org/10.1145/165180.165230), initial
survey metadata/abstract scope, supplies translated-workload context. The
specific grid scheme, constants, indexing and data dependencies come from
source inspection. The numerical interpretation is source-based, not a
newly claimed review of a hydrodynamics paper. Original and independent
state agreement supports correctness; compiler/collector effects remain
hypotheses pending separate evidence.

## fulsom-lazy

### Algorithm and workload

Render the fixed union of three coloured spheres using source interval
arithmetic, constructive-solid-geometry residual pruning, an octree, front-to-
back quadtree projection and the original coloured raster stream. Preserve
source child order, lighting calculations and the overlapping topBit z-half.
The workload is a sequential renderer, requiring no graphics or foreign API.

### History, variants and notices

Duncan Sinclair's Fulsom sources carry copyright 1990,1991,1992,1993 and an
individual permission grant. Complete original notices, including their
spelling, remain in source copies and translated derivative modules.
README.original and dated correspondence supply the program history;
README.nofib credits Will Partain with directory flattening. Historical machine,
heap and time examples are not current performance measurements.

[nofib](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798) is pinned
at b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798. The gc/fulsom and real/fulsom Main programs are materially
different consumers: one writes one complete raw raster; the other computes
and prints a signed machine-integer hash in 1000 iterations. Their shared
reachable renderer is implemented once. The unsuffixed family fulsom denotes
the GC source and fulsom-nofib the colliding real source, matching the inventory.
Each receives explicit -lazy/-strict finite-data names.

The source modules mostly match byte for byte; the interval copies also contain
formatting/type-context differences. Both exact copies are retained. Bah.hs
is an auxiliary test explicitly excluded by each Makefile. Cube, transforms,
other sample scenes and unused interval operations are not entrypoints of
either fixed Main workload. Retain their original definitions without
claiming runnable imports of inactive library APIs. No external dataset is
needed; scene coordinates, colours and light vector come from Shapes/Kolor.

### Translation, demand and numeric decisions

Keep infinite octree and quadtree control, CSG nodes, change flags, stream
spines and branch choices memoized in both policies. Fully eager infinite
control would not terminate. The lazy policy memoizes finite interval bounds,
RGB components and child-list spines; the strict policy materializes those
finite fields. Shared global scene definitions remain global.

## symalg-lazy

### Algorithm and workload

Run the source symbolic arithmetic command interpreter: lexical analysis,
precedence parsing, persistent environment lookup/update, expression
evaluation and printing. Its supplied workload sets decimal precision and
repeatedly computes square roots of integers two through ten. Preserve the
RealM arbitrary-precision decimal approximation algorithms and memoized
infinite trees, rather than replacing them with floating square roots.

### History, source variants and notices

[nofib real/symalg](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/real/symalg)
is pinned at b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798. The individual modules state no author, dated
program history or separate license grant. Preserve all twelve original
modules, NofibUtils, Makefile and FAST/NORM/SLOW fixtures; do not infer
authorship from collection maintainers or incidental comments.

The -lazy/-strict names distinguish delayed finite AST/numeric values and
approximation-tree integer labels. Infinite tree branches remain memoized
in both. BasicNumber and BasicNumberApprox contain inactive class helpers;
the runnable command interface retains all reachable lexer, parser,
environment, evaluator and printer behavior. No external dataset is needed.

### Translation and numeric semantics

Use IntInf for source Integer values, rational numerators/denominators,
approximation-tree labels and precision arithmetic. Preserve truncating quot,
the source rounding biases and intermediate decimal scales. Tree lookup
follows the original binary path for 1-tolerance; mapping retains shared
numberTree structure and per-approximation memoization.

The source square-root iteration uses a binary64 seed only at its original
base case. Preserve that conversion, nearest/even rounding and subsequent
integer refinement. Decimal tokens containing nonzero fractional digits
follow the original default binary64 read then exact rational conversion;
do not silently substitute the decimal rational. Replace Data.Ratio with
normalized IntInf pairs and explicit gcd/cross-product arithmetic, recording
this library implementation/allocation difference.

Retain the source operator precedence, associativity, symbolic unknown
functions, literal/evaluated assignments, environment order and print quirks.
Negative rational numerators keep the source extra parentheses. Source
RealM comparisons use its precision-dependent two-unit band where invoked.
Positive sqrt profiles require exact original decimal strings; no floating
tolerance is substituted for their arbitrary-precision results.

AST nodes, evaluated number payloads and integer labels follow the finite-data
policy. Token descriptors and finite argument/environment list spines are
strict portable metadata containing delayed values. Infinite approximation
branches always use explicit memoized delays. Only selected ASCII command
inputs are supplied; Data.Char is replaced by portable SML character predicates.
No Unicode runtime or other prerequisite feature is added.

The source output hash has tested signed 64-bit machine semantics, made explicit
with Word64 modular arithmetic and IntInf signed conversion. The same sources
run on every host, including hosts with default signed 31-bit integers.
Selected precision/exponent metadata fits that range.

### Inputs and complete result validation

| Profile | Decimal precision | sqrt commands | Parameter source |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Smoke | 20 | 9 | Small complete source command cycle. |
| Normal | 300 | 9 | Reduced precision and one source command cycle. |
| Large | 3000 | 9 | Original FAST precision, one source command cycle. |

Each cycle evaluates two through ten and exits deterministically. Originals
use 261 sqrt commands at precisions 3000/15000/40000 for FAST/NORM/SLOW.
Preserve all original scripts/results and document these reductions.
Longer precision pilots retain their actual guard/timeout outcomes separately;
selected normal validation does not claim completion of the original scripts
or the full SML large profile.

Preload fixed script/reference files in SML97; stream prompts and command
outputs to an online exact checker. Additionally observe every complete
formatted numeric string before hashing and compare it with reviewed full
original values. This adds a uniform validation callback/traversal, potentially
affecting optimization; it is not an assumed opaque barrier or an identical
I/O cost. Reset the callback on success and failure. Suppress terminal output
and return checked numeric-value and transcript-byte counts.

An output-only Haskell observer replaces hashing with full numeric text;
unmodified originals separately match all supplied hashed fixtures. Complete
original sqrt values through 40000 digits also agree with an independent
integer-square-root oracle. Compare each scaled value with the exact floor;
the measured gap is recorded, with a one-decimal-unit permitted bound.
Runtime references remain exact source strings.

Additional original command transcripts exercise help, empty commands,
assignments, environments, arithmetic/precedence, rational/real conversion,
unknown functions, comparisons and syntax errors. Direct arithmetic observers,
memoized-tree sharing, zero-product demand and deliberately perturbed complete
numbers/transcripts provide independent checks. The original zero-times-
nonzero exact-real magnitude search can fail to terminate; do not repair
inactive/source-bug paths silently or include them in successful fixtures.

### Compiler/runtime concerns and evidence

Investigate arbitrary-precision representation, integer multiplication and
division, memoized precision reuse, infinite-tree retention, closure
specialization and AST forcing. Library rational replacements, strict finite
spines and extra validation are explicit costs. These are hypotheses from
source inspection; passing values or count agreement does not assign
individual performance causes.

Recorded semantic, smoke/normal profile, count and repository acceptance
outcomes are separate in the validation ledger. Native group labels use
host-default flags; Rune compilation levels are checked explicitly. Full
original SML FAST/NORM/SLOW and selected large runs remain separate checks,
never inferred from small-input or original-Haskell results.

### Literature and review scope

[Partain's nofib suite paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17) supplies application-coverage context at the
survey scope already recorded. RealM.hs supplies the particular decimal-tree
representation, scale rules, magnitude search and Newton-style recurrences.
No external exact-real paper is claimed as the derivation of this source.
Original observations and integer square roots support numerical validation;
compiler/collector and arithmetic-cost questions require separate measurement.

Preserve all original scripts/results and document these reductions.
Longer precision pilots retain their actual guard/timeout outcomes separately;
selected normal validation does not claim completion of the original scripts
or the full SML large profile.

Preload fixed script/reference files in SML97; stream prompts and command
outputs to an online exact checker. Additionally observe every complete
formatted numeric string before hashing and compare it with reviewed full
original values. This adds a uniform validation callback/traversal, potentially
affecting optimization; it is not an assumed opaque barrier or an identical
I/O cost. Reset the callback on success and failure. Suppress terminal output
and return checked numeric-value and transcript-byte counts.

An output-only Haskell observer replaces hashing with full numeric text;
unmodified originals separately match all supplied hashed fixtures. Complete
original sqrt values through 40000 digits also agree with an independent
integer-square-root oracle. Compare each scaled value with the exact floor;
the measured gap is recorded, with a one-decimal-unit permitted bound.
Runtime references remain exact source strings.

Additional original command transcripts exercise help, empty commands,
assignments, environments, arithmetic/precedence, rational/real conversion,
unknown functions, comparisons and syntax errors. Direct arithmetic observers,
memoized-tree sharing, zero-product demand and deliberately perturbed complete
numbers/transcripts provide independent checks. The original zero-times-
nonzero exact-real magnitude search can fail to terminate; do not repair
inactive/source-bug paths silently or include them in successful fixtures.

### Compiler/runtime concerns and evidence

Investigate arbitrary-precision representation, integer multiplication and
division, memoized precision reuse, infinite-tree retention, closure
specialization and AST forcing. Library rational replacements, strict finite
spines and extra validation are explicit costs. These are hypotheses from
source inspection; passing values or count agreement does not assign
individual performance causes.

Recorded semantic, smoke/normal profile, count and repository acceptance
outcomes are separate in the validation ledger. Native group labels use
host-default flags; Rune compilation levels are checked explicitly. Full
original SML FAST/NORM/SLOW and selected large runs remain separate checks,
never inferred from small-input or original-Haskell results.

### Literature and review scope

[Partain's nofib suite paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17) supplies application-coverage context at the
survey scope already recorded. RealM.hs supplies the particular decimal-tree
representation, scale rules, magnitude search and Newton-style recurrences.
No external exact-real paper is claimed as the derivation of this source.
Original observations and integer square roots support numerical validation;
compiler/collector and arithmetic-cost questions require separate measurement.

## cacheprof-lazy

### Algorithm and workload

Annotate textual x86 assembly with instruction counters and calls to a cache
profiler. Preserve source preparsing, AT&T lexical/operand parsing, repeat
and leave expansion, basic-block grouping, operand effects, source-location
cost centres, generated descriptors/calls, peephole cleanup and debug-line
removal. Assembly and hook files are text input/output; this workload never
assembles or executes them and needs no FFI facility.

### History, source variants and notices

[nofib Cacheprof](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/real/cacheprof)
is pinned at b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798. Main, Arch_x86 and Generics credit Julian Seward,
copyright 1999, with GPL version two or later notices. Preserve both source
collections and notices. The pinned directories refer to LICENSE but omit
that file; supply an unmodified GPL-2 text as COPYING from the installed
Debian common-license text. Translated derivative modules retain the full
original notice. Hook assembly has no separate notice in its header.

The GC Main emits one annotated input followed by hook text. The real Main
opens a hook file and fully forces annotated output in 200 repetitions,
printing nothing. These are materially different consumers of shared code.
Use cacheprof-lazy/strict for the GC source and cacheprof-nofib-lazy/strict
for the colliding real source, retaining both original modules and all
provenance. Finite stage streams and generated groups follow the named policy.

Assembly fixtures identify heimdall.c and historical gcc output. No separate
dataset author/license notice is stated in the scanned assembly; retain full
pinned files and their identities without assigning program credits to the
underlying C input. The supplied FAST/normal/SLOW inputs contain 76/600/3040
lines; cacheprof.full contains 13708.

### Translation, evaluation and numeric decisions

Use tagged SML datatypes for source instructions, operands, annotations and
location metadata. Generate all 206 opcode constructors/effect-table entries
from the pinned source and check them against original Haskell observations.
Preserve the explicit 67-entry nonJumpy list; do not replace it with a broader
derived jump classification. Parser combinators, ordered alternatives and
instruction simplification remain the source algorithms.

Use memoized finite list spines/heads and deferred generated groups in the lazy
policy; the strict policy materializes them. Parsed instruction descriptors
are strict metadata, corresponding to the original forceLine boundary. Rollup
descriptor lists/indices use explicit finite strict bridges; debug text follows
the policy. Source ASCII character lists become SML strings at input and
per-output-line boundaries. Record these representation, library and temporary
allocation differences rather than claiming identical Haskell costs.

Preserve source quirks: generated repeat-label Pseudo numbers are the label
counter; quoted commas in stabs arguments become underscores; file/function
guessing, canonical-name order, arbitrary nonJumpy membership and the counter
peephole predicate remain unchanged. Level-zero prefix demand can skip a bad
later instruction; level two's global cost-centre guard must inspect it.
Independent original prefix observations confirm both cases.

No floating-point or arbitrary-precision kernel arithmetic is needed.
Source indices, line numbers, counter increments, 28-byte descriptor offsets
and selected aggregate byte counts fit signed 31-bit integers. The generated
64-bit counter operations are assembly text, not SML machine arithmetic.

### Inputs, profiles and complete validation

| Consumer | Smoke | Normal | Large |
|---|---|---|---|
| GC/raw | one FAST 76-line input | one normal 600-line input | one full 13708-line input |
| Real/forced | one FAST input | 200 normal inputs | 200 SLOW 3040-line inputs |

FAST input is borrowed explicitly from the real collection for GC smoke.
GC normal is byte-identical to the real normal input. Real normal/large retain
the source 200 repetitions; smoke reduces that count to one. Per-profile
input-origins tables identify original paths and SHA-256 values.

The pinned GC stdout fixture belongs to the full input reservoir, while its
current default stdin is a 600-line prefix. The unmodified GC executable fed
cacheprof.full reproduces all 1671273 fixture bytes exactly. Retain that
complete input/fixture pairing for GC large and obtain reviewed normal output
from the unmodified original. Do not treat the mismatch as a compiler failure
or overwrite the historical fixture.

Check every annotated output byte online. Raw GC additionally emits/checks
all hook text; the real consumer checks only its annotated output, retaining
per-iteration hook open/close without reading unused contents. SML closes
those handles deterministically, replacing the Haskell lazy-handle lifetime.
Preload source/reference strings once and retain the source 9999999-character
input cap; all selected fixtures are smaller. Source take-list allocation is
replaced by the string adapter. Return checked byte/repetition counts instead
of raw terminal output. The extra reference comparisons are explicit work.

Original full outputs cover all three supplied input sizes and the complete
reservoir. Additional original cases cover 206 opcodes, applicable operand
arities, indirect forms, three profiling levels, repeat expansion, location
metadata, syntax and rejected inputs. Synthetic parser/effect cases exercise
the source grammar; they are not claims of executable x86 instruction validity.
Demand, memoization, strict materialization, zero-work and deliberately
corrupted/truncated-output controls supplement complete original fixtures.

### Compiler/runtime behavior and validation scope

Investigate persistent stage spines, shared consumers, descriptor rollup,
closure specialization, string/list boundaries and strict allocation lifetimes.
These are source-based hypotheses; counter agreement does not attribute
individual performance costs.

Separate the bounded 822-assertion semantic target from four explicit full-
reservoir checks. An initial mixed target exhausted ML Kit's 1 GiB limit
during strict full-result materialization. Retain that failed attempt.
The isolated large target passes ML Kit with the declared 8 GiB profile
limit under the protective process-tree guard. Kernel and expected bytes are
unchanged. The large probe does not establish every large profile/host run.

Smoke/normal engine and host results, count scopes and full repository
acceptance are recorded in the validation ledger. Native O0/O2 labels repeat
host-default options. Deterministic input references and correct results are
required before accepting measurements.

### Literature and evidence scope

[Partain's nofib paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4471-3215-8_17)
provides application-suite context at the survey scope already recorded.
Seward's individual source notices and stage comments establish this tool's
history and transformation design. No external cache-profiling paper is
claimed as a reviewed derivation. Original executable/fixture and exhaustive
source-table observations support correctness; compiler/runtime explanations
remain hypotheses until measured separately.

## comp_lab_zift-lazy

### Algorithm and workload

Label four-neighbor connected black regions in tiled binary images. Preserve
horizontal run extraction, unique row/run labels, balanced recursive field
union, persistent labelled-set trees, boundary merging, component lookup and
label mapping. The original zift operation crops the trees inspected by
recursive label mapping; it is not replaced by a mutable union-find algorithm.

### History, names and source variants

[nofib Hartel comp_lab_zift](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/spectral/hartel/comp_lab_zift)
is pinned at b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798. Preserve the complete generated module, Makefile,
FAST/NORM/SLOW fixtures and parent Fast2haskell shim. The program heading
states no individual author or separate notice; collection/helper credits
do not establish individual authorship. No external dataset is needed.

The established comp_lab_zift name denotes the original sifting mode.
comp_lab_nozift retains the source f_no_zift alternative, separately named
because it skips generator demand and local tree pruning. The source helper
f_main_field' selects that alternative with a negative tiling argument, while
the benchmark Main itself tiles positive sizes. The portable explicit mode
uses positive tiling and the original f_comp_lab_diff' plus f_no_zift, with
the same complete renderer. It does not run a divergent negative repetition
loop or invent another component-labelling algorithm.

Each mode has explicit -lazy/-strict finite-data names. The unused parallel
prediction fields and sandwich calls use the source no-op miraseq shim.
Execution is sequential and requires no parallel runtime.

### Translation, sharing and tree semantics

Use SML97 tagged datatypes and policy-controlled memoized finite lists, trees,
labels, ranges, fields and paired results. Strict variants materialize these
finite values. Paired splits, generator views, shared base-image handles and
ignored prediction hints retain delayed control where required. Preserve
memoized mapped integer fold accumulators, rather than forcing every lazy
accumulator at construction.

## fem-lazy

### Algorithm and workload

Perform two-dimensional truss structural analysis: parse model arrays,
assign free degrees, construct the variable-bandwidth diagonal-address vector,
assemble element stiffness/load contributions, compute the recursive LL
factorization and forward/back substitution, recover all nodal displacements
and element forces, then render and hash the report.

Keep the original one-dimensional boxed vector/matrix representation,
association-list accumulation order and skyline/variable-bandwidth indexing.
The routine named beam2d implements axial bar stiffness; preserve its unused
EI parameter and zero rotational entries. No dense pivoted solver replaces
the benchmark's recursive factorization.

### History, authorship, source variants and notices

[nofib real/fem](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/real/fem)
is pinned at b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798. README credits Dr. Junxian Liu, Imperial College;
module headers date the vector/matrix and application work to March 1991.
Preserve all eighteen Haskell modules, Makefile, README, MAIL and datasets.
The inspected program/data headings state no separate redistribution grant;
do not infer one from historical correspondence.

The April 1994 correspondence, forwarded by Paul H. J. Kelly, identifies
Glasgow/distr as the properly packaged Haskell version and describes earlier
Miranda/Hope+ origins and incompletely tested compiler-specific directories.
Those historical directories are not additional implementations in this pin.
The -lazy/-strict names distinguish portable finite-array materialization.

Retain the complete inC tree as a historical comparison with fixed mutable
arrays, separate input/output and timing scripts. No maintained nofib target
builds/invokes that C program; its explicit ancillary disposition does not
assign Haskell author credit to uncredited C headers. Generated assembly/C
or runtime-specific facilities are not prerequisites of this Haskell workload.

### Translation and exact numeric decisions

Represent Haskell Float values exactly in SML real while rounding every
source arithmetic operation to binary32, using the existing portable
BenchLinearFloat rounding helper. Keep multiplication/addition grouping,
sqrt/refinement order, signed zero and binary32 bit validation. This is a
numeric-semantics adapter with binary64 storage and explicit rounding cost;
it is not a claim of native binary32 layout or Haskell-equivalent timing.

Preserve the unusual database parser: tokens containing a decimal point are
real fields, other tokens are integer fields; float digits, decimal powers,
division and addition round in source order. Do not replace that parser with
a generic decimal read. Retain its digit fallback behavior. Selected dataset
indices, offsets, counts and report totals fit signed 31-bit integers.

Use bounded immutable boxed arrays/vectors with memoized cells, retaining the
source flattened matrix/list-index builder and ordered accumulating updates.
The lazy policy demands cells as needed; the strict policy forces finite
values after construction. Both retain memoized recursive-array control:
install the vector/matrix knot before materialization, preserving the diagonal
recurrence, LL factor, forward vector and backward vector. Dependencies may
force cells in a different index order. Share the factor and final displacement
vector where the source does, avoiding duplicate solves in the benchmark.

Finite bounds/position metadata uses explicit strict bridges. The common
representation retains memo cells even in the strict policy. Record that
library/layout cost, not an assumed identical source runtime representation.
Unused library exports remain in the retained originals; the portable modules
cover every dependency of the selected Main computation.

The original report uses shortest Float formatting. The portable report uses
nine fixed decimal places through the common SML real formatter, preserving
headings, field order, padding rules and all values. An output-only Haskell
observer applies that same formatting; no numerical kernel changes. Complete
report bytes are validated separately from exact binary32 final values.

Preserve the original post-report hash as explicit modular 64-bit arithmetic,
comparing its Word64 bit pattern on every host. This fixes the tested source
machine-integer width without introducing arbitrary-precision kernel math.
Do not rely on the report hash alone to validate floating values.

### Inputs, profiles and result validation

| Profile | Repetitions | Model |
|---|---:|---|
| Smoke | 1 | Author-supplied data.0, the small two-free-degree model. |
| Normal | 100 | Original fem.stdin, 36 nodes and 62 free degrees. |
| Large | 500 | Original fem.stdin with the source SLOW count. |

Original FAST uses twenty full-model repetitions; smoke deliberately reduces
both repetition count and model size. Normal/large retain source counts and
input. data.3 is byte-identical to fem.stdin; retain both provenance paths.
The other author datasets are covered by broader semantic checks.
No random or external dataset is required.

Each iteration runs the original final-result path once, renders the report,
checks every final displacement/force bit, complete report bytes and 64-bit
hash. Require finite values and zero binary32-ulp deviation from reviewed
original final results. Parse inputs/references outside the loop, replacing
source lazy stdin/getArgs/salt plumbing. No opaque optimization barrier is
assumed. Return validated repetition/report-byte/final-value counts.

Intermediate snapshots belong to separate correctness tests: parsed arrays,
degree maps, diagonal addresses, stiffness, factor, loads, forward/back solve,
full displacement and forces all agree bit for bit across four datasets on
the validated configurations. They are not extra solves in timed workloads.
Original FAST/NORM/SLOW executables fully evaluate their original reports/hash
and print no stdout, as recorded.

An independent binary64 dense assembly and partial-pivot solve, using reviewed
binary32 input data, checks physical assembly, factor residual, free-degree
equilibrium and forces. Its norm bounds are explicit: assembly 2e-6, LL residual
1e-5, solution 1e-12 plus 2e-4 times solution infinity norm, scaled equilibrium
1e-5, and forces 1e-10 plus 1e-5 times force norm. A one-percent solution
perturbation is rejected. These independent-model tolerances do not loosen
the runtime's exact original-bit requirement.

### Compiler/runtime concerns and recorded validation

Investigate binary32 adapter overhead, boxed/lazy array cells, cyclic sharing,
list-index matrix builders, skyline sparsity, strict materialization, closure
specialization and report/validation costs. Treat these as source-based
hypotheses until separate measurements support a narrower explanation.

Direct tests cover complete original states and reports, binary32 ties/
subnormal/overflow/sign cases, recursive arrays in both dependency directions,
band-matrix knots, update order, bounds, overwritten cells, materialization,
zero work and deliberately perturbed values/reports/hashes.

Legacy 64-bit SML/NJ has default-configuration numeric failures. The same
program passes the other managed hosts; repeated legacy defaults vary and
separate 64 MiB nursery diagnostics pass. This is consistent with the existing
GC-root report, not proof of the application's exact cause. Preserve all
failures, standard defaults and expected bits. Diagnostic heap settings are
separate configurations, never substituted for the standard comparison.

repository acceptance are recorded in the validation ledger. Native group
labels use host defaults; Rune O0/O2 are explicit. Unrecorded large checks
are not inferred from smaller inputs.

## fem-strict

### Algorithm and workload

Perform two-dimensional truss structural analysis: parse model arrays,
assign free degrees, construct the variable-bandwidth diagonal-address vector,
assemble element stiffness/load contributions, compute the recursive LL
factorization and forward/back substitution, recover all nodal displacements
and element forces, then render and hash the report.

Keep the original one-dimensional boxed vector/matrix representation,
association-list accumulation order and skyline/variable-bandwidth indexing.
The routine named beam2d implements axial bar stiffness; preserve its unused
EI parameter and zero rotational entries. No dense pivoted solver replaces
the benchmark's recursive factorization.

### History, authorship, source variants and notices

[nofib real/fem](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/real/fem)
is pinned at b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798. README credits Dr. Junxian Liu, Imperial College;
module headers date the vector/matrix and application work to March 1991.
Preserve all eighteen Haskell modules, Makefile, README, MAIL and datasets.
The inspected program/data headings state no separate redistribution grant;
do not infer one from historical correspondence.

The April 1994 correspondence, forwarded by Paul H. J. Kelly, identifies
Glasgow/distr as the properly packaged Haskell version and describes earlier
Miranda/Hope+ origins and incompletely tested compiler-specific directories.
Those historical directories are not additional implementations in this pin.
The -lazy/-strict names distinguish portable finite-array materialization.

Retain the complete inC tree as a historical comparison with fixed mutable
arrays, separate input/output and timing scripts. No maintained nofib target
builds/invokes that C program; its explicit ancillary disposition does not
assign Haskell author credit to uncredited C headers. Generated assembly/C
or runtime-specific facilities are not prerequisites of this Haskell workload.

### Translation and exact numeric decisions

Represent Haskell Float values exactly in SML real while rounding every
source arithmetic operation to binary32, using the existing portable
BenchLinearFloat rounding helper. Keep multiplication/addition grouping,
sqrt/refinement order, signed zero and binary32 bit validation. This is a
numeric-semantics adapter with binary64 storage and explicit rounding cost;
it is not a claim of native binary32 layout or Haskell-equivalent timing.

Preserve the unusual database parser: tokens containing a decimal point are
real fields, other tokens are integer fields; float digits, decimal powers,
division and addition round in source order. Do not replace that parser with
a generic decimal read. Retain its digit fallback behavior. Selected dataset
indices, offsets, counts and report totals fit signed 31-bit integers.

Use bounded immutable boxed arrays/vectors with memoized cells, retaining the
source flattened matrix/list-index builder and ordered accumulating updates.
The lazy policy demands cells as needed; the strict policy forces finite
values after construction. Both retain memoized recursive-array control:
install the vector/matrix knot before materialization, preserving the diagonal
recurrence, LL factor, forward vector and backward vector. Dependencies may
force cells in a different index order. Share the factor and final displacement
vector where the source does, avoiding duplicate solves in the benchmark.

Finite bounds/position metadata uses explicit strict bridges. The common
representation retains memo cells even in the strict policy. Record that
library/layout cost, not an assumed identical source runtime representation.
Unused library exports remain in the retained originals; the portable modules
cover every dependency of the selected Main computation.

The original report uses shortest Float formatting. The portable report uses
nine fixed decimal places through the common SML real formatter, preserving
headings, field order, padding rules and all values. An output-only Haskell
observer applies that same formatting; no numerical kernel changes. Complete
report bytes are validated separately from exact binary32 final values.

Preserve the original post-report hash as explicit modular 64-bit arithmetic,
comparing its Word64 bit pattern on every host. This fixes the tested source
machine-integer width without introducing arbitrary-precision kernel math.
Do not rely on the report hash alone to validate floating values.

### Inputs, profiles and result validation

| Profile | Repetitions | Model |
|---|---:|---|
| Smoke | 1 | Author-supplied data.0, the small two-free-degree model. |
| Normal | 100 | Original fem.stdin, 36 nodes and 62 free degrees. |
| Large | 500 | Original fem.stdin with the source SLOW count. |

Original FAST uses twenty full-model repetitions; smoke deliberately reduces
both repetition count and model size. Normal/large retain source counts and
input. data.3 is byte-identical to fem.stdin; retain both provenance paths.
The other author datasets are covered by broader semantic checks.
No random or external dataset is required.

Each iteration runs the original final-result path once, renders the report,
checks every final displacement/force bit, complete report bytes and 64-bit
hash. Require finite values and zero binary32-ulp deviation from reviewed
original final results. Parse inputs/references outside the loop, replacing
source lazy stdin/getArgs/salt plumbing. No opaque optimization barrier is
assumed. Return validated repetition/report-byte/final-value counts.

Intermediate snapshots belong to separate correctness tests: parsed arrays,
degree maps, diagonal addresses, stiffness, factor, loads, forward/back solve,
full displacement and forces all agree bit for bit across four datasets on
the validated configurations. They are not extra solves in timed workloads.
Original FAST/NORM/SLOW executables fully evaluate their original reports/hash
and print no stdout, as recorded.

An independent binary64 dense assembly and partial-pivot solve, using reviewed
binary32 input data, checks physical assembly, factor residual, free-degree
equilibrium and forces. Its norm bounds are explicit: assembly 2e-6, LL residual
1e-5, solution 1e-12 plus 2e-4 times solution infinity norm, scaled equilibrium
1e-5, and forces 1e-10 plus 1e-5 times force norm. A one-percent solution
perturbation is rejected. These independent-model tolerances do not loosen
the runtime's exact original-bit requirement.

### Compiler/runtime concerns and recorded validation

Investigate binary32 adapter overhead, boxed/lazy array cells, cyclic sharing,
list-index matrix builders, skyline sparsity, strict materialization, closure
specialization and report/validation costs. Treat these as source-based
hypotheses until separate measurements support a narrower explanation.

Direct tests cover complete original states and reports, binary32 ties/
subnormal/overflow/sign cases, recursive arrays in both dependency directions,
band-matrix knots, update order, bounds, overwritten cells, materialization,
zero work and deliberately perturbed values/reports/hashes.

Legacy 64-bit SML/NJ has default-configuration numeric failures. The same
program passes the other managed hosts; repeated legacy defaults vary and
separate 64 MiB nursery diagnostics pass. This is consistent with the existing
GC-root report, not proof of the application's exact cause. Preserve all
failures, standard defaults and expected bits. Diagnostic heap settings are
separate configurations, never substituted for the standard comparison.

Canonical smoke/normal cases, semantic counts, timing/count scopes and full
repository acceptance are recorded in the validation ledger. Native group
labels use host defaults; Rune O0/O2 are explicit. Unrecorded large checks
are not inferred from smaller inputs.
