## solid-lazy

### Algorithm and workload

Approximate the area of a fixed two-dimensional constructive solid using
adaptive four-way spatial subdivision. Preserve postfix CSG parsing,
primitive bounding-circle pruning, source Boolean simplification order,
the classification tables, midpoint approximation, terminal stopping and
right-associated area accumulation. The selected embedded scene is the union
of 300 circles; do not replace the kernel with uniform-grid sampling.

### History, names, source defect and notices

[nofib Hartel solid](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/spectral/hartel/solid)
is pinned at b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798. The generated module states no individual author or
separate program/dataset notice. Preserve the complete module, original
Makefile/fixtures and parent Fast2haskell shim without assigning helper credits
to the program or embedded numeric data.

The original classification adapter contains a concrete indexing defect:
the list adapter is zero-based, but callers supply one-based vector indices.
For example union(OUT,OUT) returns UNKNOWN, and the normal depth-nine scene
overcounts 65 finest-grid cells. Original FAST/NORM/SLOW outputs still match
their supplied fixtures; those fixtures retain the defect.

The runnable port applies the reviewed one-line correction in the indexing
adapter, preserving every table entry and operation. A corrected Haskell
reference and an independent geometric oracle agree. The unrepaired baseline
has an explicit correctness deferral in the variant inventory, with its
original fixtures and counterexamples retained. It is not a passing workload.
The -lazy/-strict names distinguish finite numeric/data materialization.

The line primitive's unusual point-expression grouping is retained from
source; selected profiles contain only circles. Source-observation controls
record that unused branch without claiming general geometric validation
of arbitrary line scenes.

### Translation, demand and numeric decisions

Use policy-controlled finite point/primitive/cell fields and child-list data.
Both policies retain memoized CSG and subdivision control, preserving pruning
before expansion. Strict variants materialize finite fields; neither eagerly
builds an unbounded spatial tree. Midpoint coordinates and shared child bounds
retain their source sharing.

Preserve the order of full/empty checks. Union with a full left child skips
the right child; intersection checks the right-full case before the left-empty
case. Point classification uses the table and demands both operands even where
Boolean reasoning would permit a shortcut. The simple-terminal test precedes
the depth limit. Ignored surface identifiers/primitive-count metadata do not
acquire a new stopping role.

Keep binary64 operation grouping, sqrt, decimal conversion and source
positive digits/dot parser behavior. Extract the embedded c_aap literal into
a fixed profile file, preserving all 599 postfix codes and 300 primitive rows.
Each requested depth parses the scene in the source helper's written scope.
Compiled constant-input sharing/specialization may differ from the original
closed Haskell expression; no opaque barrier or identical cross-language
allocation cost is assumed.

Bounds, depths, primitive IDs and finest-grid counts fit signed 31-bit
integers. Within selected depths, coordinates/areas are dyadic and every final
area is an exact multiple of 4^-depth, with at most 24 fractional binary bits.
Validate exact scaled counts, not an arbitrary floating tolerance.

The original report uses shortest Double formatting. The portable driver
renders 24 fixed decimal places and checks the complete formatted value.
Every selected dyadic fraction terminates within those places; this is an
explicit output/library adaptation shared by all SML compilers.

### Inputs, profiles and result checks

| Profile | Repetitions | Depth sweep |
|---|---:|---|
| Smoke | 1 | 1 through 3 |
| Normal | 200 | 1 through 9 |
| Large | 200 | 1 through 12 |

Normal and large preserve the original 200 repetitions and NORM/SLOW sweep.
Smoke reduces source FAST 200-by-five explicitly. Scene coordinates and
distribution remain the fixed embedded source data, with no random generator
or external runtime facility.

For every repetition/depth, compute and validate the exact corrected-reference
finest-grid count and complete fixed-decimal output. Return validated
repetition/value/byte counts instead of repeated stdout. CLI/reference reads
move outside the loop, replacing repeated getArgs; timing/count reports
include the documented parsing/format/validation work.

Original/corrected observers record all thirteen areas through depth twelve
and complete adaptive tree shapes through depth nine. A separate direct union
membership scan over every finest-grid midpoint, with no CSG tree or adaptive
pruning, agrees on all ten independently checked depths through nine.
Synthetic circle/union/intersection/difference/full/empty controls and all
48 classification-table entries are observed independently.

### Compiler/runtime behavior and evidence scope

Investigate CSG simplification, memoized numeric fields, shared bounds,
subdivision spines, deep left-associated scene structure, parser/constant
specialization, allocation and formatting. These are source-based hypotheses
until separate counts or measurements establish narrower findings.

Direct tests preserve source demand order, ignored count metadata, midpoint/
rectangle short circuits, exact reference areas/shapes, zero work and
deliberately incorrect results. All checks remain valid on hosts exposing
compiler/runtime defects; no tolerance increase accepts them.

The semantic matrix has one incorrect legacy 64-bit SML/NJ area check;
other groups pass and a repeated host-default group passes. Native O0/O2
labels do not represent different native compiler options. All three SML/NJ
builds also fail canonical normal profiles: five attempts reject complete
FIX24 formatting, while legacy strict rejects the exact area count first.
A kernel-independent formatter probe confirms SML/NJ rounds the depth-nine
value before padding to 24 places. Exact expected answers remain unchanged.
All Rune configurations, MLton, Poly/ML and ML Kit pass both profiles.
Individual large states do not establish the full 200-repetition selected
large run. See the archived host diagnostics and validation ledger.

### Literature and review scope

[Hartel and Langendoen (1993)](https://doi.org/10.1145/165180.165230)
provides the previously recorded collection/translation context. Specific CSG
tables, pruning, parser and spatial algorithms come from pinned source review.
No separate solid-modelling paper is claimed as the derivation of this code.
Corrected original observations, explicit table counterexamples and independent
geometric counts establish the recorded repair/correctness scope. Runtime
or compiler performance attribution remains a hypothesis.

## lift-lazy

### Algorithm and workload

Transform a fixed nested functional-language AST with both a plain lambda
lifter and a modular fully-lazy lambda lifter, then pretty-print the input
and both supercombinator programs. Preserve free-variable analysis,
abstraction, lambda separation, binding-level annotation, maximal-free-
expression identification, renaming, floating and final lambda lifting.
Both algorithms run in every iteration, matching the original driver.

### History, authorship, variants and notices

[nofib real/lift](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/real/lift)
is pinned at b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798. LambdaLift.lhs is the executable literate paper
*A modular fully-lazy lambda lifter in Haskell*, by Simon L. Peyton Jones
and David Lester. Its title/author block and complete prose/code are retained,
together with Utilities, Print, Test, Main, the modern NofibUtils adapter,
Makefile and all FAST/NORM/SLOW golden outputs. No additional individual
permission grant is inferred from the author block or from a helper.

The paper separates full-laziness transformation from lambda lifting.
This is algorithmic full laziness, distinct from the port's evaluation-policy
suffix. Both lift-lazy and lift-strict execute both source transformations.
They differ in finite intermediate AST/annotation materialization; they do
not denote plain versus fully-lazy algorithms.

### Translation and semantic decisions

Keep parameterized AST/annotation datatypes, list-based sorted name sets,
source quicksort/dedup and ordered union/difference, association-list
environments, list-backed bags, body-first supercombinator collection and
source definition/name-supply order. No replacement optimizer or parser
generates the result. Test.hs supplies the fixed AST; the portable
constructor transcription is checked against the complete original AST.

Both policies use explicit memoized AST/name/annotation/supply delays.
The strict policy traverses finite results at pass boundaries; the lazy
policy leaves them demand-driven. Recursive let renaming ties the
extended environment through deferred name cells, installing fresh names
before they are demanded. Strict traversal occurs after that knot is ready.
This source-level support requires no compiler or runtime extension.

The source lambda-renaming branch returns the supply after its arguments,
rather than the later supply returned from its body. Preserve and test
that behavior; do not silently repair it or claim the observed examples
prove a general naming theorem for arbitrary inputs.

Retain arbitrary-precision integer literals with IntInf. Selected name,
level, repetition and byte counts fit signed 31-bit integers. Replace the
host-width hash with explicit modular Word64 arithmetic, reproducing the
original 64-bit GHC outputs even on 32-bit SML hosts.

Preserve higher-order Iseq/Oseq printers, delayed expression inspection,
pending indentation after newlines, restored outer indentation, definition
order and complete textual output. Numeric literal formatting explicitly
uses Haskell's minus spelling.

The original Test.program is a shared top-level value. The portable driver
creates one memoized input root per invocation and shares it across all
iterations; zero repetitions do not force it. CLI/reference reads move
outside the loop. The GHC NOINLINE salt IO barrier has no portable SML
equivalent and is not claimed; source specialization/loop motion remains
a compiler concern.

### Inputs, profiles and validation

| Profile | Iterations | Input |
|---|---:|---|
| Smoke | 1 | Fixed original Test.program AST |
| Normal | 4000 | Same fixed AST |
| Large | 20000 | Same fixed AST |

Normal and large preserve NORM/SLOW repetition counts; smoke explicitly
reduces the source FAST count of 400. Each iteration validates the entire
1948-byte input/plain/fully-lazy report and modular hash
0x8a2cd0a394a3204d. It returns validated iteration/byte counts rather than
printing one signed hash per iteration. A failed complete result or hash
is rejected before accepting measurement data.

Read-only GHC observers record all input/plain/full ASTs for seven cases:
identity, captured variables, nested arguments, shadowing, an unused
recursive cycle, factorial and the fixed source program. Both policies
must match all complete structures and the exact source pretty output.
A separate memoized Python evaluator checks six terminating cases, including
factorial 720, before and after each transformation; it also checks scoped,
closed, lambda-free supercombinator programs. The fixed source program is
structurally validated, not claimed to terminate under that evaluator.

Direct tests cover shared node/name demand, strict pass boundaries,
recursive renaming knots, the source returned-supply quirk, name sets,
large integer literals, delayed printing, indentation, zero work and
deliberately incorrect reports/hashes.

An earlier ML Kit auxiliary region-analysis crash is preserved separately.
Both complete normal applications and equivalent explicit fixed-case calls
pass. The final common semantic target retains all assertions and passes on
all six managed hosts and every Rune configuration; the benchmark kernel
contains no host-specific workaround.

### Compiler/runtime questions and evidence limits

Investigate higher-order printer composition, recursive AST allocation,
annotation sharing, environment lookups, repeated analyses and pass-boundary
materialization. These are source-based hypotheses. Count and timing
evidence must identify input/policy/configuration; cross-language salt,
fusion, allocation and constant specialization are not assumed equal.

### Literature and review scope

The full primary executable paper is reviewed in the pinned LambdaLift.lhs,
including its abstract, introduction and algorithm code. It explicitly
presents full laziness as a separate pass and discusses let/letrec handling.
The maintained nofib source and previously reviewed Partain suite paper
supply collection context. Complete original observations and the independent
evaluator support the recorded cases; they do not prove general equivalence
for every AST or establish a compiler performance mechanism.

Read-only GHC observers record all input/plain/full ASTs for seven cases:
identity, captured variables, nested arguments, shadowing, an unused
recursive cycle, factorial and the fixed source program. Both policies
must match all complete structures and the exact source pretty output.
A separate memoized Python evaluator checks six terminating cases, including
factorial 720, before and after each transformation; it also checks scoped,
closed, lambda-free supercombinator programs. The fixed source program is
structurally validated, not claimed to terminate under that evaluator.

Direct tests cover shared node/name demand, strict pass boundaries,
recursive renaming knots, the source returned-supply quirk, name sets,
large integer literals, delayed printing, indentation, zero work and
deliberately incorrect reports/hashes.

An earlier ML Kit auxiliary region-analysis crash is preserved separately.
Both complete normal applications and equivalent explicit fixed-case calls
pass. The final common semantic target retains all assertions and passes on
all six managed hosts and every Rune configuration; the benchmark kernel
contains no host-specific workaround.

### Compiler/runtime questions and evidence limits

Investigate higher-order printer composition, recursive AST allocation,
annotation sharing, environment lookups, repeated analyses and pass-boundary
materialization. These are source-based hypotheses. Count and timing
evidence must identify input/policy/configuration; cross-language salt,
fusion, allocation and constant specialization are not assumed equal.

### Literature and review scope

The full primary executable paper is reviewed in the pinned LambdaLift.lhs,
including its abstract, introduction and algorithm code. It explicitly
presents full laziness as a separate pass and discusses let/letrec handling.
The maintained nofib source and previously reviewed Partain suite paper
supply collection context. Complete original observations and the independent
evaluator support the recorded cases; they do not prove general equivalence
for every AST or establish a compiler performance mechanism.

## parstof-lazy

### Algorithm and workload

Recognize the source's embedded functional-language scheduling program using
a character-dispatch lexer and backtracking parser combinators. Preserve
balanced lexical dispatch by first-character sets, ordered alternatives,
keyword prefixes, token attributes, right-recursive repetition, precedence,
associativity, tuple/union constructors, let/case/if syntax, type declarations
and source error selection/preview behavior.

The original timed consumer observes parser success, not the AST payload.
The lazy variant retains that recognition workload. The strict variant
materializes finite lexical/AST attributes as parsing proceeds; complete
tree comparisons are separate semantic checks rather than extra timed
tree traversals.

### History, authorship, names and notices

[nofib Hartel parstof](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/spectral/hartel/parstof)
is pinned at b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798. The generated module states no separate individual
author or program/data notice. Preserve the complete module, Makefile,
FAST/NORM/SLOW fixtures and parent Fast2haskell shim, without assigning
collection/helper credits to this parser or its embedded program text.

The -lazy/-strict suffixes identify meaningful finite-data demand policies.
This parser is distinct from the scheduling simulator: its input describes
scheduling, while its executed algorithm is lexical/syntactic analysis.
No generated or parsed target program is executed.

### Translation, sharing and semantic decisions

Retain all eighteen typed source AST datatypes, constructor field order and
source combinator grammar. Portable constructor and grammar transcription
scripts are archived with the original source and read-only observers.
Use memoized character/token control for backtracking and shared input.
A cached closure for each of the 42 nonterminals preserves top-level grammar
sharing; explicit source-derived result types make these caches portable
under the value restriction.

Both policies represent semantic attributes with policy-controlled cells.
Conversion/join callbacks remain delayed in the lazy variant, including
unused success attributes. The strict variant forces finite attribute
construction. A character-list attribute materializes its finite SML list
when demanded; default recognition leaves those payloads unused. Control
streams retain per-cell memoization and neither policy eagerly expands
an unbounded parser/control structure.

Preserve left-biased successful alternatives, farther-line known failures
with left-biased ties, and the source repetition/optional combinators'
recovery even from known failure messages. Error formatting remains separately
memoized and takes the first 25 rendered preview characters. Preserve the
missing inequality entry in the source token-display table and the source
hex-escape code-subtraction rule; do not replace them with guessed fixes.

Selected text, decoded character values and names are ASCII/byte characters.
Their identifiers, literals, line numbers, checksums and lengths fit signed
31-bit integers. Haskell Char is wider than SML Char: escapes whose source
arithmetic produces code points above 255 are outside these profiles and
are not claimed to be portable general Unicode parsing. No such escape or
integer overflow is introduced into a selected profile.

Extract the exact positive-index c_the_program literal into program.input
through the original module. Share its memoized character root across all
parses, matching the source constant text. Read CLI/reference files once.
Each iteration constructs the selected number of parser results and traverses
the concatenated success messages with the original sum-plus-length checksum;
lazy numeric accumulators remain delayed. Parser rejection is an immediate
correctness failure.

### Inputs, profiles and result validation

| Profile | Outer iterations | Programs per iteration |
|---|---:|---:|
| Smoke | 1 | 1 |
| Normal | 100 | 8 |
| Large | 100 | 40 |

Normal and large preserve the original Main repetition count and NORM/SLOW
arguments; smoke reduces the source FAST 100 iterations explicitly.
Every recognized program contributes the exact source success message,
26 characters. Each iteration checks its full original checksum string,
2483*n / 26*n with its newline, and returns validated iteration/program/
checksum-byte counts. Suppress repeated stdout and the additional putStrLn
newline, recording that output adaptation.

Read-only GHC observers record complete token streams, ASTs, remaining input
and known errors for ten inputs, including the fixed program, application,
conditional, let/case, lexical escapes, malformed declarations, missing
expressions, empty input and an unterminated comment. Both policies must match
all complete observations. The original FAST/NORM/SLOW executions also match
their supplied fixtures.

An independent ordered regular-expression lexer agrees on all 1898 observed
tokens. A separate structural check validates AST constructor ownership,
arity, primitive types and selected integer bounds. This is not a second
full parser or a general parsing-equivalence proof.

Direct controls test unused/shared semantic callbacks, strict demand,
alternative/sequence short circuits, known-error priority and recovery,
deferred/shared error text, cached grammar use, zero work and rejection of
incorrect programs/checksums. Read-only JSON renderers support these checks;
the benchmark driver does not call them.

Common explicit character and cached-nonterminal types resolve the initial
portable typing errors. Earlier incomplete attempts are retained; the final
20 semantic groups and all 56 profile cases pass on every selected host and
Rune engine, without changing expected answers.

### Compiler/runtime questions and evidence limits

Investigate backtracking, shared token tails, grammar closures, unused AST
allocation, finite-field materialization, higher-order combinators and checksum
accumulators. These are source-based hypotheses. Closed-input specialization,
constant sharing and allocation are not assumed identical between Haskell
and SML compilers, and no opaque evaluation barrier is claimed.

### Literature and review scope

The previously reviewed Hartel and Langendoen (1993) translation account
supplies collection context. Specific lexer/parser algorithms, grammar,
recovery rules and demand behavior come from pinned source inspection and
original observations. No separate parser-construction paper is claimed as
the derivation of this generated module. Correctness observations do not
establish a compiler performance explanation.

## transform-lazy

### Algorithm and workload

Parse functional dataflow programs, remove aliases/redundant definitions,
retain used stream bindings, label nodes, inline eligible functions and
perform the original stream/state rewrites. Render six successive versions
as source/script text and sum their output lengths. The generated programs,
include paths and shell commands are output data; never execute them.

Preserve the v/v0/v1/v3/v5/v6 pipeline and its exact ordering. This is a
compiler/symbolic workload even where the input describes FFT, wave or other
numerical networks; those target networks are not evaluated.

### History, names, inputs and notices

[nofib Hartel transform](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/spectral/hartel/transform)
is pinned at b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798. The generated module states no separate individual
program/data author or permission notice. Preserve its complete text,
Makefile, original FAST/NORM/SLOW outputs and parent Fast2haskell shim.
References to a person's home-directory paths do not establish authorship
or an external runtime dependency.

The original module contains eleven embedded examples. The selected cyclic
stream is FFT, Fibonacci, Fibonacci sum, flip-flop, gamma, Hamming, set/reset
and wave4, in that exact order. Simple, tailtest and wavestream remain
complete source/semantic controls. They are additional input examples for
this algorithm, not separate imported algorithms or default cycle entries.
The -lazy/-strict suffixes identify meaningful finite-data policies.

### Translation, demand and representation

Keep typed definition, where and expression nodes, character-list names,
source comparisons, merge/quicksorts, single-occurrence removal, ordered
substitution, reachability approximation and first eligible inlining.
Retain label comparisons and short-circuit later fields after an earlier
comparison differs. Inline only matching-arity no-where functions, remove the
current definition from candidates and do not recursively inline a newly
substituted body in the same pass.

Preserve the source variable analysis that ignores Cons/Maps state fields.
Labelling increments by two, labels a stream before its Cons state and labels
Maps arguments before its state. Memoized paired results share transformed
values and counters without forcing an unused numeric projection.

Preserve t5's four scans, reversed prefix accumulators, restart behavior and
remembered label-pair termination guard. Do not insert helpful reversals or
sorts. T6 partitions the used program but appends its new output/state
definitions to the original program. Source stopping and selection rules
remain unchanged.

Data fields and finite list spines use the common memoized/strict policy;
lexical, parser-result, paired-labelling and cyclic-program control remains
memoized. The cyclic input is tied explicitly before forcing it, and a finite
take bounds the selected work. Conversion/join callbacks remain delayed in
the lazy parser. Typed cached grammar closures retain source sharing.

The source parser chooses the first accepted program prefix and discards
remaining tokens; do not add an EOF requirement. Preserve its first-result
cuts, pragma/comment rules, and numeric-token rule that treats 1+2 as one
raw numeric spelling. This syntax pass does not evaluate numeric literals.

The original consumer forces report list spines to determine length, rather
than validating every character. Keep character cells separate from spines:
length alone skips unused characters. The source indentation routine does
inspect character contents to match newlines, and retains that demand.
Complete text/AST validation is a separate semantic target, not extra timed
character forcing.

The shared shim's miraseq and force are no-ops. Preserve lazy numeric
accumulation instead of inferring strictness from the helper's name.
Strict variants materialize finite data while retaining bounded control.

Embed exact original input strings in portable SML source. Each benchmark
invocation creates eight shared, delayed prepared roots and cycles over them.
Repeated in-process invocations rebuild those roots; grammar/literal caches
belong to the functor instance. Record that adapter scope instead of claiming
identical cross-language CAF behavior in every measurement mode.

Fixed character-list literals are created once per functor instance, matching
source immutable literal sharing. An offline token-aware transcription step
lifts 55 distinct literals used at 83 sites; runtime contains ordinary SML
bindings and no lookup interpreter or opaque barrier. Preserve compiled-input
specialization opportunities without claiming equal compiler transformations.

### Profiles and correctness checks

| Profile | Programs selected from the eight-example cycle |
|---|---:|
| Smoke | 8 |
| Normal | 3000 |
| Large | 15000 |

Normal and large preserve NORM/SLOW counts. Smoke explicitly reduces source
FAST 300 to one complete cycle. Every selected report length is checked
against the reviewed original length, and the total is checked independently.
Return the original integer total without its newline through the common
driver. Smoke totals 28275, normal 10603125 and large 53015625.

All embedded text and emitted profiles are ASCII. Numeric literals remain
raw syntax strings; labels, lengths, namespace counters and totals fit signed
31-bit integers. The driver bounds counts to 0..20000 and rejects invalid
arguments. No floating-point approximation or arbitrary precision shortcut
replaces the compiler algorithm.

Read-only original observers record all eleven complete token streams,
parsed/prepared trees, transformation states and reports. Both policies must
match every full state and all report bytes. Original FAST/NORM/SLOW executions
match their supplied fixtures. Independent structural checks cover 88 original
ASTs and 5072 nodes, including constructor types/arity, ASCII names and bounded
odd positive labels. Independent cycle arithmetic agrees with all three
golden outputs; it is not a proof of dataflow-network equivalence.

Direct controls cover callback sharing/demand, first-result cuts, prefix
parsing, lexer quirks, self-inlining exclusion, source variable analysis,
comparison short circuits, character/indentation demand, zero work, cycle
wrap and deliberate wrong-length rejection. Full large SML runs are recorded
only when actually executed, separately from individual case/state coverage.

### Compiler/runtime questions and evidence limits

Investigate parser backtracking, symbolic tree copying, sort/comparison order,
repeated rewrites, name/label generation, character-list sharing, delayed
numeric accumulators, finite materialization and retained prepared inputs.
These are source-based hypotheses. Same-source SML compiler/engine counts
and measurements must identify their exact mode/configuration; original
Haskell is a correctness reference rather than an identical-cost baseline.

### Literature and review scope

The previously reviewed Hartel and Langendoen (1993) translation account
supplies collection context. Pinned source establishes this parser, compiler
pipeline and demand behavior. No paper on the numerical target networks is
claimed as a derivation of the executed transformation code. Original full
observations and independent structural/cycle checks establish the recorded
scope; no general transformation-correctness proof or measured compiler
mechanism is implied.

## simple-nofib-lazy

### Algorithm and workload

Advance the original two-dimensional SIMPLE hydrodynamics/heat-conduction
state using immutable boxed arrays: velocity and position, area/volume and
density, artificial viscosity, temperature, pressure/energy, two directional
heat sweeps, energy error and adaptive time step. Retain polynomial table
searches, finite-difference Newton updates and every source arithmetic order.

The totals consumer forces thirteen final scalar sums without printing the
original state. The report consumer formats every coordinate/value in eleven
arrays plus time step and error, constructs the complete report and writes it
to standard output. Both consumers force the thirteen totals of each
intermediate state before advancing. They share one numerical implementation
but remain separate workloads because final traversal, formatting and I/O
differ materially.

### History, authorship, aliases and source variants

[nofib spectral/simple](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/spectral/simple)
is pinned at b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798. The Id source credits Kattamuri Ekanadham and carries
1989 correspondence/edit history. Its Haskell translation is described as an
Id-to-pH translator with hand-added types and strictness annotations; do not
invent a named translator from that description. Historical MAIL documents
RPaul Johnson's Haskell/pH correspondence, Andy Shaw's C submission, and a
Fortran version supplied by Olaf Lubeck. The C file explicitly credits both
Andy Shaw and Kofi Fynn. Supplying the Fortran is not proof of sole authorship.

Preserve Main.hs, Makefile, MAIL, simple.c and simple.f in full. No separate
permission notice is stated for these individual files. The repository-level
nofib notices remain recorded in the pinned inventory. Embedded numeric
constants and geometry are the input; no external historical dataset is
silently substituted.

Makefile explicitly selects SRCS = Main.hs to exclude the C comparator.
The Fortran source is likewise outside that build. Both ancillary comparators
are preserved and inventoried with this concrete build-scope exclusion,
rather than claimed as additional passing nofib executables. The C pi
constant differs and Fortran declares single-precision REAL; neither is an
exact binary64 oracle for this Haskell program.

The classic unsuffixed simple and simple-smlnj imports retain their mutable
SML implementations and original profiles. This port uses the -nofib collision
suffix. Memoized and strict finite-array policies receive -lazy and -strict;
the reporting consumer adds -report before the policy suffix. Similar ancestry
does not establish identical representations, evaluation or input profiles.

### Translation, numeric semantics and demand

Keep the original boxed, immutable arrays with inclusive tuple-index bounds,
row-major enumeration, shared pair/triple results and memoized real cells.
Keep the original nbc boundary-code array and its undefined interior cells,
the four-entry pbb/pb tables and the qb alias of pb. One-dimensional constant
tables use vectors with explicit one-based source index translation. A private
association builder fills the immutable nbc array, sharing its missing-element
cell and literal values. Strict construction materializes supplied entries
while leaving omitted source cells undefined. No boundary lookup is replaced
by an equivalent conditional computation.

Paired/triple array results use a shared memoized tuple table in this portable
encoding. Projection closures can retain that table until they are consumed;
this additional support storage and its lifetime are explicit representation
costs, not a claim of identical GHC object layout or retention.

Recursive boundary arrays and forward/backward heat recurrences install their
shared stores before optional strict materialization. Lazy projections do not
force unused tuple fields. A strict policy materializes finite array cells
when its array root is demanded; memoized state/control roots remain shared.

Preserve memoized scalar-list elements and the source left folds for array
totals, polynomial sums, energy/error reductions and time-step extrema.
Lazy accumulators remain delayed until their result is demanded; strict
variants force each accumulator before continuing. Array elements are
enumerated through the boxed vector in source row-major order. Do not fuse
these source producer/fold pipelines by hand.

Retain the fixed thirteen-tuple of delayed totals behind a memoized root.
Intermediate loop checks force it before advancing; the reporting consumer

initialization and fractional power. Do not round to binary32 or reuse the

structures. Explicit tuple patterns and numeric types resolve Standard ML

for the common runner. The report consumer retains the complete headings,
bounds, coordinates, order, eleven arrays, scalars and done marker. Map its
Haskell shortest floating printer to SML97 Real.fmt GEN17, normalize sign and

same documented error bound. Decimal spellings can differ by host; numerical
values and structure supply the oracle, not one host's formatted text.

### Profiles, input generation and result validation

| Profile | Grid maximum | Steps |
|---|---:|---:|
| Smoke | 8 | 1 |
| Normal | 100 | 20 |
| Large | 100 | 100 |

All three preserve the original FAST/NORM/SLOW step counts. Smoke reduces
the compile-time grid maximum from 100 to 8 for bounded correctness checks;
normal and large retain the actual upstream grid maximum 100. A thin
profile-specific SML driver selects that constant; the numerical kernel and
data representation are identical. The full-grid source FAST observations
and initial attempts are retained separately. The driver accepts
bounded step counts 0..100 and requires an explicit reviewed reference.
Inputs preserve source constants, polar geometry and boundary distributions.
Normal and large use the actual grid of 100. Smoke and the bounded semantic
target use a separately recorded source-constant configuration with grid 8.
A complete one-step report has 708 cells at grid 8 and 110004 at grid 100.

Totals require thirteen finite results. Reports require the exact eleven
names, inclusive bounds, row-major coordinates, number of cells and finite
scalar values, then validate each formatted numeric token. Per-cell and scalar checks retain abs(x-e) <= a + r*abs(e), where
a=1e-12 and r=1e-11. Array sums need a conditioning-aware bound: let n
be the number of cells, S an upward-rounded sum of reference magnitudes,
u=2^-53, gamma=n*u/(1-n*u), and B=n*a+r*S. Require aggregate error at most
(1+gamma)*B+2*gamma*S, with outward rounding padding. This follows from
componentwise compatibility and the recursive-summation error model;
it does not prove physical-model accuracy. Time step and energy error
retain the original scalar bound. Exact rational review checks every
reference scale/bound and deliberate out-of-bound perturbations.

[The Accuracy of Floating Point Summation](https://nhigham.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/high93s.pdf),

componentwise/aggregate bound here is a separately derived application.

bits, bad counts/shapes/steps and incorrect references must be rejected.

as required. Read-only observers capture every array cell and all thirteen
totals at 0/1/2/5/20/100 steps. Both initial SML policies agree bit for bit on
every captured full-grid state, including the complete 100-step large state;

golden aggregates. Original reporting-mode outputs at 1/20/100 steps decode
to the same 110004 final array cells; complete source reports are preserved.
The zero-step state has 800 additional velocity boundary cells.

### Compiler/runtime questions and evidence limits

Investigate immutable-array construction, thunk memoization, shared tuple
projections, recursive array lifetimes, direction-dependent sweeps, reduction
chains, floating-point primitives and complete report allocation/I/O.

the performance comparison; Haskell is a correctness reference. Source and
adapter differences prohibit attributing cross-language times solely to
compiler quality.

Full-grid state observations, bounded semantic checks, primary profiles,
guarded counts, serial timing-adapter diagnostics and repository acceptance
are recorded separately. A passing initial private pilot does not establish
that a later host/profile passed. Retain compile errors, incorrect numerical
results and resource failures explicitly; no failed case contributes timings.

of equivalent costs or exact results.

## simple-nofib-strict

### Algorithm and workload

Advance the original two-dimensional SIMPLE hydrodynamics/heat-conduction
state using immutable boxed arrays: velocity and position, area/volume and
density, artificial viscosity, temperature, pressure/energy, two directional
heat sweeps, energy error and adaptive time step. Retain polynomial table
searches, finite-difference Newton updates and every source arithmetic order.

The totals consumer forces thirteen final scalar sums without printing the
original state. The report consumer formats every coordinate/value in eleven
arrays plus time step and error, constructs the complete report and writes it
to standard output. Both consumers force the thirteen totals of each
intermediate state before advancing. They share one numerical implementation
but remain separate workloads because final traversal, formatting and I/O
differ materially.

### History, authorship, aliases and source variants

[nofib spectral/simple](https://gitlab.haskell.org/ghc/nofib/-/tree/b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798/spectral/simple)
is pinned at b7391df4540ac8b11b35e1b2e2c15819b5171798. The Id source credits Kattamuri Ekanadham and carries
1989 correspondence/edit history. Its Haskell translation is described as an
Id-to-pH translator with hand-added types and strictness annotations; do not
invent a named translator from that description. Historical MAIL documents
RPaul Johnson's Haskell/pH correspondence, Andy Shaw's C submission, and a
Fortran version supplied by Olaf Lubeck. The C file explicitly credits both
Andy Shaw and Kofi Fynn. Supplying the Fortran is not proof of sole authorship.

Preserve Main.hs, Makefile, MAIL, simple.c and simple.f in full. No separate
permission notice is stated for these individual files. The repository-level
nofib notices remain recorded in the pinned inventory. Embedded numeric
constants and geometry are the input; no external historical dataset is
silently substituted.

Makefile explicitly selects SRCS = Main.hs to exclude the C comparator.
The Fortran source is likewise outside that build. Both ancillary comparators
are preserved and inventoried with this concrete build-scope exclusion,
rather than claimed as additional passing nofib executables. The C pi
constant differs and Fortran declares single-precision REAL; neither is an
exact binary64 oracle for this Haskell program.

The classic unsuffixed simple and simple-smlnj imports retain their mutable
SML implementations and original profiles. This port uses the -nofib collision
suffix. Memoized and strict finite-array policies receive -lazy and -strict;
the reporting consumer adds -report before the policy suffix. Similar ancestry
does not establish identical representations, evaluation or input profiles.

### Translation, numeric semantics and demand

Keep the original boxed, immutable arrays with inclusive tuple-index bounds,
row-major enumeration, shared pair/triple results and memoized real cells.
Keep the original nbc boundary-code array and its undefined interior cells,

tables use vectors with explicit one-based source index translation. A private
association builder fills the immutable nbc array, sharing its missing-element
cell and literal values. Strict construction materializes supplied entries
while leaving omitted source cells undefined. No boundary lookup is replaced
by an equivalent conditional computation.

Paired/triple array results use a shared memoized tuple table in this portable
encoding. Projection closures can retain that table until they are consumed;

costs, not a claim of identical GHC object layout or retention.

Recursive boundary arrays and forward/backward heat recurrences install their
shared stores before optional strict materialization. Lazy projections do not

when its array root is demanded; memoized state/control roots remain shared.

Preserve memoized scalar-list elements and the source left folds for array
totals, polynomial sums, energy/error reductions and time-step extrema.
Lazy accumulators remain delayed until their result is demanded; strict
variants force each accumulator before continuing. Array elements are
enumerated through the boxed vector in source row-major order. Do not fuse
these source producer/fold pipelines by hand.

tables use vectors with explicit one-based source index translation. A private
association builder fills the immutable nbc array, sharing its missing-element
cell and literal values. Strict construction materializes supplied entries
while leaving omitted source cells undefined. No boundary lookup is replaced
by an equivalent conditional computation.

Paired/triple array results use a shared memoized tuple table in this portable
encoding. Projection closures can retain that table until they are consumed;
this additional support storage and its lifetime are explicit representation
costs, not a claim of identical GHC object layout or retention.

Recursive boundary arrays and forward/backward heat recurrences install their
shared stores before optional strict materialization. Lazy projections do not
force unused tuple fields. A strict policy materializes finite array cells
when its array root is demanded; memoized state/control roots remain shared.

Preserve memoized scalar-list elements and the source left folds for array
totals, polynomial sums, energy/error reductions and time-step extrema.
Lazy accumulators remain delayed until their result is demanded; strict
variants force each accumulator before continuing. Array elements are
enumerated through the boxed vector in source row-major order. Do not fuse
these source producer/fold pipelines by hand.

Retain the fixed thirteen-tuple of delayed totals behind a memoized root.
Intermediate loop checks force it before advancing; the reporting consumer
leaves the final totals root unused. Conversion to a list is a separate
correctness-observation adapter. The first revised-energy term is shared
across Newton evaluations, as in the original binding.

The source strictArray evaluates only the first constructor of map evalValue
(elems array). It does not traverse and force every element, despite its
comment. The lazy policy follows actual demand; the strict policy is a
separately named finite-materialization experiment. Do not repair the source
helper according to its name.

Preserve the source's positive-residual-only Newton stopping test and its
reuse of the previous residual argument. Preserve the energy-error boundary
work calculation that reads pressure into its u1/u2 variables and position z
into w1/w2. These are source behaviors, not corrections to a physical model.
Retain exact operation grouping, table coefficients, boundary classifications,
reflection directions, sweep dependencies and traversal/reduction order.
The upstream source contains a stale size-10 comment; its actual grid_max is
100. Normal and large retain it; the smoke-only grid reduction is explicit.

Use binary64 real arithmetic, including source powers, sqrt, trigonometric
initialization and fractional power. Do not round to binary32 or reuse the
classic imperative implementation. Integer coordinates, counters and cell
counts fit signed 31-bit integers. Reference hexadecimal bits decode using
portable IntInf arithmetic and Real.fromManExp, avoiding optional packing
structures. Explicit tuple patterns and numeric types resolve Standard ML
record overloading/value restrictions without host-specific kernels.

The original positive consumer emits nothing. Add a checked compact summary
for the common runner. The report consumer retains the complete headings,
bounds, coordinates, order, eleven arrays, scalars and done marker. Map its
Haskell shortest floating printer to SML97 Real.fmt GEN17, normalize sign and
exponent spelling, and verify every rendered number parses back within the
same documented error bound. Decimal spellings can differ by host; numerical
values and structure supply the oracle, not one host's formatted text.
The full report still reaches controlled standard output before the common
RESULT/PASS/SUMMARY protocol. Formatting and I/O remain part of this workload.

### Profiles, input generation and result validation

| Profile | Grid maximum | Steps |
|---|---:|---:|
| Smoke | 8 | 1 |
| Normal | 100 | 20 |
| Large | 100 | 100 |

All three preserve the original FAST/NORM/SLOW step counts. Smoke reduces
the compile-time grid maximum from 100 to 8 for bounded correctness checks;
normal and large retain the actual upstream grid maximum 100. A thin
profile-specific SML driver selects that constant; the numerical kernel and
data representation are identical. The full-grid source FAST observations
and initial attempts are retained separately. The driver accepts
bounded step counts 0..100 and requires an explicit reviewed reference.
Inputs preserve source constants, polar geometry and boundary distributions.
Normal and large use the actual grid of 100. Smoke and the bounded semantic
target use a separately recorded source-constant configuration with grid 8.
A complete one-step report has 708 cells at grid 8 and 110004 at grid 100.

Totals require thirteen finite results. Reports require the exact eleven
names, inclusive bounds, row-major coordinates, number of cells and finite
scalar values, then validate each formatted numeric token. Per-cell and scalar checks retain abs(x-e) <= a + r*abs(e), where
a=1e-12 and r=1e-11. Array sums need a conditioning-aware bound: let n
be the number of cells, S an upward-rounded sum of reference magnitudes,
u=2^-53, gamma=n*u/(1-n*u), and B=n*a+r*S. Require aggregate error at most
(1+gamma)*B+2*gamma*S, with outward rounding padding. This follows from
componentwise compatibility and the recursive-summation error model;
it does not prove physical-model accuracy. Time step and energy error
retain the original scalar bound. Exact rational review checks every
reference scale/bound and deliberate out-of-bound perturbations.

The recursive-summation model is reviewed in Higham,
[The Accuracy of Floating Point Summation](https://nhigham.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/high93s.pdf),
1993, section 2, especially the bound in equation 2.6. The combined
componentwise/aggregate bound here is a separately derived application.
No summation algorithm, ordering, expected value or per-cell tolerance changes.
Deliberately perturbed near-zero and large values, NaN, infinity, malformed
bits, bad counts/shapes/steps and incorrect references must be rejected.
Do not widen this bound to hide a host failure.

Unmodified original totals-mode executions at 1/20/100 steps return no stdout
as required. Read-only observers capture every array cell and all thirteen
totals at 0/1/2/5/20/100 steps. Both initial SML policies agree bit for bit on
every captured full-grid state, including the complete 100-step large state;
this is observed agreement, not a requirement to substitute approximate
golden aggregates. Original reporting-mode outputs at 1/20/100 steps decode
to the same 110004 final array cells; complete source reports are preserved.
The zero-step state has 800 additional velocity boundary cells.

### Compiler/runtime questions and evidence limits

Investigate immutable-array construction, thunk memoization, shared tuple
projections, recursive array lifetimes, direction-dependent sweeps, reduction
chains, floating-point primitives and complete report allocation/I/O.
These are hypotheses from source analysis. Same-source SML engines/hosts are
the performance comparison; Haskell is a correctness reference. Source and
adapter differences prohibit attributing cross-language times solely to
compiler quality.

Full-grid state observations, bounded semantic checks, primary profiles,
guarded counts, serial timing-adapter diagnostics and repository acceptance
are recorded separately. A passing initial private pilot does not establish
that a later host/profile passed. Retain compile errors, incorrect numerical
results and resource failures explicitly; no failed case contributes timings.

### Literature and review scope

Arvind and Kattamuri Ekanadham, [Future scientific programming on parallel
machines](https://research.ibm.com/publications/future-scientific-programming-on-parallel-machines),
Journal of Parallel and Distributed Computing (1988), supplies background.
The reviewed IBM abstract describes composing a SIMPLE excerpt from Id
Nouveau functions and discusses transformations such as inlining. That is
paper-supported context rather than a measured explanation for this port.
Only the abstract/metadata was reviewed here; do not imply a full paper review.

The pinned program references CSG 273 and contains specific equation/edit
history. Its MAIL warns about the historical physical correctness question
and small-grid long-run NaNs. Validation establishes agreement with this
specific Haskell program, not validation of the physical model. No parallel
runtime feature is introduced. Upstream mutable C/Fortran comparisons and the
classic SML version need separate numeric/evaluation review before any claim
of equivalent costs or exact results.
